ceqa-6423aaa84985d685b0.name: Owens River Water Trail
ceqa-6423aaa84985d685b0.description: The County of Inyo proposes to implement the Owens River Water Trail Project within the Lower Owens River floodplain from Lone Pine Narrow Gauge Road south to State Route 136, just east of Lone Pine. The project would allow recreational access for non-motorized watercraft (kayaks, stand-up paddleboards, and canoes) on an approximately 6.3-mile segment of the Owens River, representing approximately 10 percent of the newly rewatered, 62-mile Lower Owens River. The project would remove emergent vegetation and excavate within the river channel to remove occlusions and establish a continuous navigable waterway, and would develop boat launch and take-out facilities with limited amenities (vault restroom, wildlife-resistant trash receptacles, and signage). The project area is owned by the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power. The County would provide ongoing maintenance of the water trail.

ceqa-6423aaa84985d685b0.developmentType: Recreational (Development of a water trail on the Lower Owens River)

ceqa-60a8f9ff616f91ca96.description: The project consists of installing the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) infrastructure. This initiative is designed to create a fully operational system that will eventually support two future dual port, pedestal-mounted Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS). Note that the installation of the EVCS themselves is outside our current scope and may be handled by others at a later date. As part of this project, four parking stalls will be specially stenciled and restriped. Clear signage will be installed to indicate that these stalls are reserved for electric vehicle use, ensuring easy identification and proper use The project involves the installation of buried conduits, fixed bollards, wheel stops, and new electrical equipment, including all necessary wiring, to deliver a complete and functional system. Electrical power for the EVSE will be drawn from an existing source already available at the site. All aspects of the work, including waste disposal, will be conducted in strict compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances. The work will involve pavement saw cutting, trenching, backfilling, and restoring the affected lot surface to its original condition once the installation is complete.

ceqa-5c9bac2593d9282eaf.name: Bishop and Pine Creek Fuels Reduction
ceqa-5c9bac2593d9282eaf.projectTitle: Bishop and Pine Creek Fuels Reduction
ceqa-5c9bac2593d9282eaf.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ceqa-5c9bac2593d9282eaf.agencyName: Forestry and Fire Protection, Department of
ceqa-5c9bac2593d9282eaf.description: The primary purpose of this project is to provide defensible space to help protect structures and developments and provide safety for visitors and residents in the Bishop Creek and Pine Creek drainages in the event of a wildfire. An additional objective is to improve and protect the ecological health of the vegetation in the project area. The project should allow managers more flexibility to meet resource objectives to improve and maintain ecological health using wildfire away from the developed recreation areas and communities once they are buffered by a zone of sparser fuels. Defensible space and fuelbreaks are not intended to stop a fire, but to help reduce the fire intensity and provide a safer location for fire suppression forces to defend structures and control a fire if needed. Methods used will depend on vegetation types, terrain and the overall setting, including distance to homes or other development. The different methods that will be used are mowing, hand cutting, thinning, limbing, removal of dead and down, fuelwood collection, piling and burning, chipping, and seeding/planting native species.

ceqa-0752817c5527914457.description: The proposed project will replace portions of old barbed wire perimeter fence, totaling approximately 8,200 linear feet, with modern 5 strand barbed wire fencing. Large portions of the existing fence line are in poor condition, with rotting wood posts, damaged barbed wire, and corners that a not adequately anchored. Approximately 5,400 linear feet will be direct replacement along the existing fence alignment. In the northwest corner of the airfield approx. 1000 LF of fence line will be moved in, to avoid floodplain and potential wetland impacts along the existing alignment. On the northwest fence line, the proposed project would relocate approximately 1,800 feet of the existing fence towards the adjacent airport perimeter road. This new alignment will create a path for walking or biking outside the airport fence, connecting Wye Rd. to Airport Rd. The new fence will be installed within the footprint of the existing dirt road.

ceqa-6488b49011de438ff9.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ceqa-6488b49011de438ff9.agencyName: Forestry and Fire Protection, Department of
ceqa-6488b49011de438ff9.description: CAL FIRE is providing funding to the North Fork Mono Tribe to implement tribal wildfire resilience treatment activities on culturally significant lands within Sierra National Forest and Inyo National Forest using Tribal land management practices. These treatments will enhance biodiversity and improve hydrology, climate, and wildfire resilience and aim to serve California Native American Tribes and advance forest health and cultural use of fire.

ceqa-3bc9bd8989e04b2d95.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS-INY-60408-R6, pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 1602, the project Applicant, California Dept of Transportation, District 9. The Project is limited to the modification of drainage systems at two locations, called Locations 1 and 2. Activities for Location 1 are limited to the removal of a Siberian elm tree (Ulmus pumila), the installation of a temporary water diversion hose, gravel bag diversion berm, and pump system with fish screen, the installation of a 24-inch diameter culvert to bypass an existing culvert system and connect to a recently installed culvert system, and the removal of the temporary diversion system after completion of construction activities. Activities for Location 2 are limited to the removal of four Siberian elm trees near the existing culvert outlet headwall, the removal of an existing 24-inch diameter culvert, flared end section at the culvert inlet, and headwall at the culvert outlet, and the installation of a slightly shorter 24- inch culvert with flared end sections at the inlet and the outlet. The length of the replacement culvert is shorter so that the new flared end section at the outlet will be within the footprint of the culvert and headwall that were removed at the outlet.

ceqa-1ac7db398188bebf0a.name: Little Lakes Thin Blanket
ceqa-1ac7db398188bebf0a.description: This project proposes to perform a 0.1’ hot mix asphalt (HMA) overlay in Inyo County near Little Lake, from PM R8.4 to PM R15.2, including driveways and roadway connection conforms. The edge of pavement will include standard 3-foot-wide shoulder backing, and all existing AC dike will be replaced in kind. Rumble strips will be installed, with gaps in the shoulder rumble strip to allow bicycle movement between lanes and shoulders. Conform grind operations will be performed at the beginning of construction from PM R8.4 to PM R11.8. Grinding involves tapering the roadway profile from the overlay height down to the existing roadway height. All shoulder backing will occur within the existing road prism width and depth on previously disturbed compacted dirt. The work also includes grinding and repaving several failed pavement areas (0.4’ deep) between PM R11.8 and PM R15.2. There will be one long dig out section from PM 10.2 to PM 10.4 in the southbound direction and shoulder. It will be 0.2’ deep. The existing paved median (PM R8.55 to PM R11.25) will receive a fog seal treatment

ceqa-d96d18a66e710af7f5.name: South Census Station Replacement Project #2
ceqa-d96d18a66e710af7f5.description: The project proposes to install new loop detectors, piezo, cabinets, foundations and pull boxes. All constructions will be on pavement or in previously disturbed ground. Detector loops are installed 3” at maximum depth in pavement. All locations will require the installation of new conduit under pavement or in previously disturbed areas. Location 3, the new conduit will be installed in the dirt area (30 inches below the surface). The new foundation for the new controller cabinet will be installed in the dirt area (16 inches below the surface). The 2 new pull-boxes will be added.

ceqa-924a99ba4d61d96a35.name: Crystal Geyser Roxane Grant Ranch Project

ceqa-924a99ba4d61d96a35.description: The project would include the construction of a water bottling facility, internal roadways, employee parking and truck staging areas, a fire suppression tank and fire pump building, and other utilities. The project also seeks Planning Department approval of Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 2025-01 to permit the water bottling facility on the Light Industrial (M-2) zoning district, and CUP No. 2025-05 for the water transfer pursuant to Chapter 18.77 of the Inyo County Code of Ordinances. The project would require demolition of the existing vacant ranch house on the project site that was constructed in 1985. The water bottling facility would be an approximately 124,500-square-foot (sf) steel building that would house two bottling lines, a warehouse, and shipping facilities. A new production well would be drilled approximately 1,200 feet northwest of the proposed water bottling facility, which would be used as the source for all water uses during operation.

ceqa-34b08fcda3e114b649.name: Bishop MTS Utilities and Fencing
ceqa-34b08fcda3e114b649.description: The project will construct a chain link fence, driveway, and bring utility hookups to the property line for the Caltrans Bishop Maintenance Station expansion. Approximately 1700 feet of 6-foot chain link fencing will be placed around the sub-parcel, joining the existing Bishop Caltrans Maintenance Station perimeter fence. A curb cut in City of Bishop sidewalk will be required to construct a 24-foot driveway, with gate, to provide access the parcel from Spruce Street. Pavement trenching approximately 200 feet long and 36 inches deep is required to bring the City of Bishop Water/Sewer and Southern CA Edison Electrical hookups to the property line. An encroachment permit from the City of Bishop will be obtained for utility work and driveway construction.

ceqa-2af969ef2e55d2319e.name: California Department of Fish and Wildlife Western Joshua Tree Seed Collection Project
ceqa-2af969ef2e55d2319e.projectTitle: California Department of Fish and Wildlife Western Joshua Tree Seed Collection Project
ceqa-2af969ef2e55d2319e.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Habitat Conservation Planning
ceqa-2af969ef2e55d2319e.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife (Headquarters), Habitat Conservation Planning Branch - Sacramento
ceqa-2af969ef2e55d2319e.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife and its agents will collect and store western Joshua tree seed to provide source material for the long-term maintenance, restoration, and enhancement of western Joshua tree habitat. Project activities directly support conservation and recovery activities as outlined in the Western Joshua Tree Conservation Plan (August 2025). CDFW and its agents will attempt to collect from at least 110 locations throughout the range of western Joshua tree in California between 2026 and 2033. Only a very small percentage (not to exceed 10%) of available fruit will be collected. At each collection site, CDFW and its agents will harvest approximately 20,000 - 30,000 seeds, roughly 10 gallons of ripened fruit, from at least 50 individuals. Collections will only occur in “mast” years (i.e., when many western Joshua trees within a region flower and produce fruit synchronously) and will follow Center for Plant Conservation standards. Staff will use telescoping poles with a hooked attachment or long trash grabbers to gently remove fruit from trees. Site information will be recorded for each collection location. Seed will be processed and placed into long-term storage using standard seed banking practices at a CDFW storage facility. Seed will be used for future restoration, enhancement, or research projects.

ceqa-0a2498e5eed2fbafed.name: Highway 6 Dixon Lane Bicycle Enhancement
ceqa-0a2498e5eed2fbafed.description: The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) proposes to construct a highway improvement project 0.3-miles north of the City of Bishop to address safety and environmental issues caused by semi-trucks parking along the shoulders of US Highway 6. The semi-truck parking has created hazardous conditions by blocking pedestrian and bicycle access to the paved and compacted dirt highway shoulders and by causing significant accumulation of trash and biological materials within the Caltrans Right-of-Way (ROW) on adjacent parcels and within North Fork Bishop Creek. To address these concerns, Caltrans proposes to install a striped 4-foot bike lane with a buffer, apply fog seal treatment, re-stripe the highway, and install a Type 5 standard wire fence with 15-foot wire mesh gates along the highway shoulder. The project intends to restore safe access for multi-modal highway use and reduce environmental damage.

ceqa-c43c7b95572b9f627e.description: SWP #26026 provides for the conveyance of up to 20,000 acre-feet of Arvin-Edison Water Storage District’s 2026 Central Valley Project (CVP) water (Non-Project Water) to KCWA under Article 55 of KCWA’s Water Supply Contract with DWR. This Non-Project Water will be made available by the United States Bureau of Reclamation (Reclamation) to DWR at O’Neill Forebay and/or Banks Pumping Plant for subsequent delivery by DWR to KCWA through February 28, 2027 for use in the CVP place of use. ceqa-9958a0af5333b4e641.name: Devil’s Den Pipeline Visual Inspection
ceqa-9958a0af5333b4e641.description: The Department of Water Resources (DWR) plans to inspect the Devil’s Den pipeline (DEPL). To safely inspect the line, the pipe will first be fully drained. To assist with dewatering, DWR will use 4-inch lay flat PVC to transfer water from the DEPL to the Berrenda Mesa canal. Lay flat pipe will connect to a portable diesel pump at vault 16.70. DWR workers will run the lay flat pipe uphill towards vault 16.60, approximately 535-feet away, and then downhill towards Kecks Rd, approximately 1,440-feet away. From there, the pipe will turn and run south along Kecks Rd for 620-feet and end at Berrenda Mesa canal. Once the lay flat pipe is in place, DWR staff will start dewatering. After DEPL is completely drained, DWR staff will roll up the pipe either by hand or with assistance of a small off-road vehicle. Dewatering is anticipated to last one week. Equipment and vehicle staging will take place at vault 16.70. This work is necessary for assessing the condition of the DEPL.

ceqa-bd3938599533715385.name: Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operations, Maintenance, and Capital Improvement Program ("Project")
ceqa-bd3938599533715385.projectTitle: Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operations, Maintenance, and Capital Improvement Program ("Project")
ceqa-bd3938599533715385.description: The Kem-Tulare Water District (KTWD) proposes to implement its Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operations, Maintenance, and Capital Improvement Program across the existing District facilities and pipeline rights-of-way identified above. The Project encompasses routine inspection and maintenance, repair, sediment removal, and in-kind replacement or rehabilitation of existing agricultural water conveyance infrastructure to maintain operational reliability, improve energy efficiency, and prevent service disruptions during peak irrigation periods. All activities will be confined to previously disturbed District property, existing concrete pads and structures, and established utility easements; no work will expand the existing purpose or diversion capacity of the affected facilities. Activities primarily consist of mechanical servicing and capital rehabilitation at existing pumping facilities. This includes annual maintenance and overhauls of pump and motor assemblies at the A venue 24, A venue 36, and Cecil pumping plants. At the Shafter Check structure, the District will design and rebuild a failed pump housing to restore mechanical function; this discrete repair is necessary to maintain essential water service and prevent or mitigate an emergency. At the Woollomes Pumping Plant, the Woollomes Pump Station Efficiency Increase Project will remove, rebuild, and reinstall worn pumps and motors to restore operating efficiency from approximately 60 percent to 76 percent without increasing diversion capacity, and will include hydrovac suction cleanout of accumulated sediment within the enclosed pump intake vault. Additional structural preservation includes surface preparation and repainting of exposed piping and infrastructure at the Twin Pipes and Quinn pumping plants. At Cameo #4, Guzman Reservoir, other District­operated regulating reservoirs, and the identified mainline, lateral, and turnout locations, activities will be limited to routine inspection and maintenance, repair, sediment removal, and in-kind replacement or rehabilitation of existing components within the previously disturbed areas described above.

ceqa-d37995c8799a57bb88.name: 2026 Emergency Overchute Work (Mettler)
ceqa-d37995c8799a57bb88.description: San Joaquin field division plans to clean out overchute 244.65, 246.51, and 291.19. To complete this work, staff will use hand tools to remove sediment and debris from the overchutes, dragon teeth, and concrete aprons. A water truck or pump will be used to wash down the overchutes. A vacuum truck will be used to remove sediment and water. A dump truck will be used to haul off debris. A skid steer might be used on overchute 246.51 and 291.19 to aid with debris removal. If necessary, a crane may also be used to move equipment and remove debris. All work will take place within the DWR right-of-way. Work is expected to take two to five days per site. This work is necessary to maintain overchutes.

ceqa-44a2dcce279d27fa2f.description: McIntosh and Associates, Inc. (applicant), on behalf of ATG Investments, LLC (property owner), is proposing a General Plan Amendment (GPA) and Zone Change (ZC) on approximately 24.86 acres located at 9737 Ashe Road (southwest corner of Taft Highway and Ashe Road). The request includes: (1) an amendment of the Land Use Element of the Metropolitan Bakersfield General Plan land use designation from HMR (High Medium Residential) to HR (High Density Residential) and GC (General Commercial) or a more restrictive designation; and (2) a change in zone classification from R-2 (Single Lot Single-Unit Dwelling) to C-2 (Regional Commercial) and R-3 (Medium Density Multi-Unit Dwelling) zone or a more restrictive zone to facilitate the development of multi-family residential and commercial retail. A Mitigated Negative Declaration will also be considered.

ceqa-5cad8f639f5e86f06e.description: The proposed Euismod Energy Storage Project is a battery energy storage system (BESS) facility with associated infrastructure, which will use lithium-ion batteries and ancillary equipment to store approximately 1,150 megawatts (MW) or 9,200 megawatt-hours (MWh) of electricity from the regional grid, to be supplied back as needed, on an approximate 120-acre proposed project site in the unincorporated area of southeastern Kern County, California. The proposed project includes land-use entitlement request for a Zone Change Case (ZCC), Conditional Use Permits (CUPs), Zone Variance ('ZV), and Nonsummary Street Vacations (NSVs) from the Kem County Planning & Natural Resources Department.

ceqa-533eae763b867b292f.name: 713492_CREH_OG
ceqa-533eae763b867b292f.description: CREH proposes to rework 2-3A-1C (API 0402902619), part of UIC Project No. 08006009, in the Buena Vista field to repair holes in well 2-3A-1C’s casing. The Operator proposes to restore well 2-3A-1C’s mechanical integrity and prevent further deterioration by running 5 ½-inch inner casing to the top of the current liner, cementing the casing to surface, and performing post-remediation casing integrity testing to verify isolation of fluid flow between the wellbore and annulus. Temporary equipment such as pumps and return bins may be needed. Various mobile temporary equipment will be used including, but not limited to, workover rig, etc., and vehicles to transport personnel and materials to/from the site. No production facilities and no new ground surface disturbance will be associated with the reworks. Any waste materials will be properly disposed of in accordance with all applicable laws and regulations. The proposed project consists of the California Department of Conservation, Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM) approving a permit for California Resources Elk Hills, LLC to rework the well listed below, in the Buena Vista Oil Field. API # Well Name 0402902619 2-3A-1C

ceqa-b142b5779032bc57ab.name: PLO26-00924
ceqa-b142b5779032bc57ab.projectTitle: Second Supplemental Recirculated Environmental Impact Report (SSREIR) for Revisions to Title 19- Kern County Zoning Ordinance (2024) focused on oil and gas
ceqa-b142b5779032bc57ab.description: CRC proposes to drill new production well 13SEY-35S in the Elk Hills oil field, utilizing existing access. 13SEY-35S (35.27745100, -119.37557400) is being drilled on an existing well pad location, a 2-in flowline (700-ft) and a 3-in gas line (400-ft) will follow an existing pipeline. The proposed well is located on existing well pad but will require the construction of a new sump resulting in 0.24 acre of permanent habitat disturbance. Several burrows were observed within the vicinity of the proposed sump. No sensitive species or their sign was observed during the biological pre-activity survey. Per the EHOF ITP, a biological monitor is required for all vegetation removal, ground disturbing activities, and off road travel, should it occur. A 2-in flowline (700-ft) and a 3-in gas line (400-ft) will follow an existing pipeline corridor. Two road crossings will be required to install the pipeline and approximately 0.06 ac of habitat disturbance related to off-road travel is estimated for pipeline placement. In addition, the pipeline route will cross one dry ephemeral drainage. No impact to the drainage are anticipated. A new power pole and a new service pole will be placed at the edge of the existing location and result in no additional disturbance. All drilling and construction activities will be confined to the disturbed location/approved project areas, no parking or staging of equipment in habitat.

ceqa-0aa72f819d95cba40c.description: [Title continued... and Modification to Special Plan No. 3, Map 219] The project proponent is requesting to reallocate development maximums within the six (6) planning Sub Areas of the Grapevine Specific and Community Plan, update the roadway network within Sub Area 6a and revise language to allow final road alignment deviations to be determined at the Tract Map stage and update figures, exhibits, and tables throughout the Grapevine Specific and Community Plan and the Grapevine Special Plan to reflect the proposed changes: (a) Amendment to the Grapevine Specific and Community Plan (SPA 163, Map 500) to amend Chapter 2 - Land Use, Conservation, Open Space, and Recreation to reallocate single-family detached and single-family/multi-family attached residential units from Sub Areas 4 and Sa to Sub Arca 6a; reallocate commercial square footage from Sub Area 6a to Sub Areas 4 and Sa; and reallocate industrial square footage from Sub Area 6a to Sub Areas 6b-6e, and amend Chapter 3 - Circulation and Infrastructure to update the roadway network within Sub Area 6a from a grid to a loop pattern and update text and figures to allow final road alignment deviations greater than 300 feet within the Specific Plan Boundary except in the EA (Exclusive Agriculture) and OA (Open Area) zoning districts. ceqa-24f167fe06db404a53.name: Sentinel Peak Resources California LLC, Midway-Sunset Oil Field (Band Lease), CalGEM PFID 785461
ceqa-24f167fe06db404a53.projectTitle: Sentinel Peak Resources California LLC, Midway Sunset (Band Lease), CalGEM PFID 785461
ceqa-24f167fe06db404a53.description: Sentinel Peak Resources California LLC proposes to drill one new exploratory oil and gas production well. The proposed project would occur on public lands containing BLM administered sub-surface minerals within the Midway-Sunset Oil Field. The proposed project location is approximately 2.5 miles northwest of Fellows, California, and lies along Highway 33 between Sunrise Cogen Road and Mocal Road. The proposed activity includes the grading of a 200’ x 100’ well pad. No flowlines, producing facilities or other infrastructure are being evaluated under this proposal. The proposed project will result in 0.50 acres of permanent ground disturbance associated with the project footprint. The project is estimated to take ten days to complete. The grading portion will take two days with 10-hour operations, followed by six days of drilling with 24-hour operations, and finally two days of completion work with 10-hour days. In accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) (Pub. Resources Code, § 21000 et seq.), the CEQA Guidelines (Cal. Code Regs., tit. 14, § 15000 et seq.), and the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), CalGEM is the CEQA Lead Agency for the proposed project, while the BLM is the NEPA Lead Agency. CalGEM has reviewed the approved Environmental Assessment (EA)/Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) (DOI-BLM-CA-C060-2025-0112-EA) and finds that it meets the requirements of CEQA when combined with the actions taken by CalGEM to comply with CEQA public circulation and Tribal consultation requirements. BLM found that the project will not have a significant effect on the environment; therefore, CalGEM intends to use the FONSI rather than preparing a Negative Declaration (ND) for this project. The project activity(s) being permitted by CalGEM are within the scope of DOI-BLM-CA-C060-2025-0112-EA. CalGEM, as the CEQA Lead Agency, approved a permit for Sentinel Peak Resources California LLC to drill the well listed below, in the Midway-Sunset Oil Field in Kern County. Project Well(s): Band Govt 125, API # 0403070329, 35.214881, -119.559863

ceqa-fbbc947c11c7e2f6cd.name: Gurdial Singh Travel Center Project by LAV Consulting and Engineering
ceqa-fbbc947c11c7e2f6cd.projectTitle: Gurdial Singh Travel Center Project by LAV Consulting and Engineering
ceqa-fbbc947c11c7e2f6cd.description: The project proposes a Precise Development Plan to allow a 12,303-square-foot travel center on a 10.6-acre portion of a 26.41-acre parcel. The proposed travel center will include a convenience store, a fast-food drive-thru restaurant with a limited dine-in seating, one service station for standard vehicles with 16 auto fuel pumps, and a 9 bay semi-truck diesel fueling station with an associated semi-truck scale. The proposed travel center will operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, with an anticipated 8-12 full-time employees per shift. The travel center will also include an office, food and beverage sales (including closed lid alcohol). Additional services for long haulers include a small lounge with couches, televisions, a vending machine and a separate restroom with shower area. The plan includes 49 truck parking spaces intended for short term and overnight use, four electric vehicle (EV) charging stations, and six heavy truck (EV) charging spaces. Above ground fuel storage tanks with a maximum storage capacity of 100,000 gallons of diesel and 100,000 gallons of gasoline would be located in the northern portion of the project site. The proposed project includes a request for a Zone Variance to allow a pole sign with a 300-square-foot sign face where a maximum 240-square foot sign face is allowed and a 70-foot-sign height where a maximum of 35-feet is allowed.

ceqa-247834c038b59d6f1c.name: Maricopa Sun Solar Complex Project (Project) (California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2014-060-04, Minor Amendment No. 8 (ITP as amend
ceqa-247834c038b59d6f1c.projectTitle: EIR 03-09 JLB Maricopa Sun Solar Complex Project by Maricopa Sun LLC (PP10216)
ceqa-247834c038b59d6f1c.description: The Project, as permitted by CDFW, involves the construction, operation, and decommissioning of a 3,856.1 acre photovoltaic solar facility and associated on-site distribution lines, as well as the permanent conservation of 5,692.6 acres of on-site and nearby off-site lands. The Project will result in permanent impacts to 3,798.2 acres of San Joaquin kit fox (Vulpes macrotis mutica), San Joaquin antelope squirrel (Ammospermophilus nelsoni), and Tipton kangaroo rat (Dipodomys nitratoides nitratoides) (collectively, Covered Species) habitat and temporary impacts to 81.9 acres of utility and railroad easements. The Project is expected to result in incidental take of San Joaquin kit fox and San Joaquin antelope squirrel, which are designated as threatened species under the California Endangered Species Act (CESA) and Tipton kangaroo rat, which is designated as an endangered species under CESA. The ITP as amended, authorizes incidental take of the Covered Species that may occur as a result of Project implementation. Minor Amendment No. 8 amends several Conditions of Approval to clarify duties of the Designated Biologist(s), updates contact information, extends the timeframe for completing certain mitigation requirements, and revises with minor formatting changes.

ceqa-82f4d185fd448e2f13.name: Golden Mussel Chemical Injection Mitigation - Coastal Upstream Aqueduct Trench Work
ceqa-82f4d185fd448e2f13.projectTitle: Golden Mussel Chemical Injection Mitigation - Coastal Upstream Aqueduct Trench Work
ceqa-82f4d185fd448e2f13.description: Golden Mussel ICT plans to trench in three locations along the coastal aqueduct branch to run conduit for chemical injection lines and possibly electrical cords. All trenching will take place within aqueduct access roads. A backhoe will be used to trench and backfill. All trench work will be completed by San Joaquin Field Division staff. Each trench will be at least 6-inches wide, 14-inches deep, and less than 40-feet long. The chemical tubing will be hosed in PVC 2-inch diameter conduit. All work will take place within the DWR right-of-way. This work is necessary to prevent the spread of invasive golden mussels and to protect State Water Project infrastructure.

ceqa-3cb9422b9a0d6ab61a.name: WELL #8 AND PIPELINE REPLACEMENT PROJECT
ceqa-3cb9422b9a0d6ab61a.projectTitle: New Well #8 and Pipeline Replacement Project
ceqa-3cb9422b9a0d6ab61a.description: The Frazier Park Public Utilities District (FPPUD or District) is proposing to implement two water infrastructure Projects in the near future for which the District is seeking funding from the State Water Resources Control Board’s Division of Drinking Water (DDW). The first Project is a new potable water well, proposed District Well #8. The second Project is the replacement of approximately 18,300 feet of District potable water distribution pipelines in three of the District’s service areas, Summit Area, Lower Summit Area, and Texas Trail. The well drilling rig (Direct Rotary Rig) will be brought onto the site to drill the well. This will require about two to three weeks (14-21 days). Once Well #8 is completed, the equipment will be brought onsite to complete the well for production. Most of the 18,300 lineal feet of 8” pipeline (of the District’s total of approximately 100,000 lineal feet) within these areas will be installed within existing road rights-of-way (ROW), with a few alignments located on undisturbed land immediately adjacent to developed areas. The pipelines will be installed using standard trenching methods.
ceqa-3cb9422b9a0d6ab61a.crossStreets: Mt Pinos Way and Frazier Park Mountain Road

ceqa-b37a9434867aa4ae2d.name: Kern Council of Governments 2026 Regional Transportation Plan
ceqa-b37a9434867aa4ae2d.projectTitle: Kern Council of Governments 2026 Regional Transportation Plan
ceqa-b37a9434867aa4ae2d.description: Pursuant to federal metropolitan transportation planning requirements established under 23 U.S.C. § 134 and 23 CFR Part 450, Kern COG must prepare and update a transportation plan for its metropolitan planning area every four years to ensure that the plan adequately addresses future travel needs and is consistent with the federal Clean Air Act. Kern COG’s last RTP was adopted in 2022. The 2026 RTP is the culmination of a multi-year effort with the intent to improve the balance between land use and transportation systems. Kern COG is required by federal law to develop an RTP that determines the needs of the transportation system and prioritizes proposed transportation projects. The RTP is also necessary to obtain and allocate federal funding for regional transportation projects. Kern COG does not implement individual projects in the RTP; these projects will be implemented by local jurisdictions and other agencies. Consultation activities are a part of the 2026 RTP and PEIR development processes.

ceqa-1bf9d55772fb57c88b.name: New Vista High School Campus and Bakersfield High School Playfields Project Incidental Take Permit (CA Endangered Species Act ITP No. 2081(b)-2026-034-04)
ceqa-1bf9d55772fb57c88b.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has issued an ITP (No. 2081(b)-2026-034-04), pursuant to Section 2081(b) of the Fish and Game Code to Kern High School District. The Project involves take authorization of San Joaquin kit fox (Vulpes macrotis mutica, SJKF) in association with the demolition of the existing Vista High School and movement of the campus to the northwest portion of the site, with the varsity baseball field location remaining as-is, and the other three fields being reconstructed to the east side of the site. The Project site is within the range of SJKF and is known to support individuals of the species. The Project will result in permanent impacts to 1.1 acres of SJKF habitat. The project is expected to result in incidental take of SJKF, which is designated as a threatened species under the California Endangered Species Act (CESA). The ITP referenced above as issued by CDFW authorizes incidental take of species listed under CESA that may occur as a result of Project implementation.

ceqa-1e7782e2c22d9ee0f4.name: 2026 Emergency Golden Mussels Treatment Program (Project)
ceqa-1e7782e2c22d9ee0f4.description: District staff recently discovered the presence of Golden Mussels in District water conveyance system facilities. The mussels pose a clear and imminent danger to the District water conveyance system, including the District's thereof to provide essential public water service to its landowners and water users. In response to such emergency conditions, the District has adopted Resolution No. ST 26-03, making emergency findings pursuant to Public Contract Code section 22050 and authorizing emergency contracting for the Project without the need for competitive public bidding, and, in accordance therewith, the District will contract with one or more contractors for application of registered liquid copper solutions to District water supplies in its water system conveyance facilities for the purpose of eradicating, minimizing, and preventing future establishment of Golden Mussels in such facilities. Applications would occur as soon as possible, consistent with label instructions and recommended application parameters, to eliminate, mitigate and/or prevent further damage to the District's water conveyance system, limit the spread of Golden Mussels, and minimize threats to property, essential public services, and the environment. Upon completion of the application(s), existing District water conveyance system facilities damaged by Golden Mussels, if any, may be replaced.

ceqa-17aa3bf549f33e6418.name: Beacon Long Duration Energy Storage (LDES)
ceqa-17aa3bf549f33e6418.agency: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power
ceqa-17aa3bf549f33e6418.agencyName: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power
ceqa-17aa3bf549f33e6418.description: The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) proposes to develop the Beacon Long Duration Energy Storage (LDES) Project on LADWP-owned property in Mojave, California, adjacent to the existing Beacon 230-kilovolt (kV) Switchyard. The Project consists of constructing a 50-megawatt (MW) standalone Vanadium Redox Flow Battery (VRFB) energy storage facility with a 5-hour discharge duration to enhance grid reliability and support renewable energy integration. Construction would occur within an approximately 12.15-acre project footprint and include a temporary 5-acre laydown area. Major Project components include installation of approximately 312 modular battery containers, associated electrical infrastructure, substation expansion, and interconnection upgrades to the existing switchyard. Construction activities would include installation of approximately 4,500 linear feet of underground conduits, construction of approximately 75,000 square feet of concrete foundations, and installation of eight new 34.5-kV tie-line poles and one new 12-kV interconnection pole. Construction is anticipated to begin in early 2027, and temporary construction disturbance areas would be restored following completion of construction.

ceqa-4242bbf7eb879ff8ef.name: Tule Elk State Natural Reserve Restoration Project
ceqa-4242bbf7eb879ff8ef.projectTitle: Tule Elek State Natural Reserve Restoration Project
ceqa-4242bbf7eb879ff8ef.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-4242bbf7eb879ff8ef.description: The Project aims to restore and enhance up to 825 acres of habitat throughout the Reserve, including degraded upland habitat and riparian habitat along the Buena Vista Slough (Figure 2). Historically, this site was part of a dynamic and diverse floodplain ecosystem on the valley floor, supporting a wide array of native plant and animal species. Since the Reserve was established in the 1930s to protect the small remaining population of Tule elk at the time, the upstream dam and diversions have reduced flows to the slough and low elevation channels, resulting in a loss of riparian and wetland habitat. Combined with the introduction of non-native grasses and overgrazing by the elk, today the site primarily consists of non-native grassland and small patches of native forbs and shrubs. The Reserve currently has a herd of five to six Tule elk. The lack of habitat and forage has resulted in a supplemental feeding program to provide the elk with sufficient nutrients, and several elk have been recently relocated from the Reserve. Restoring high-quality native habitat at this site will enhance its capacity to support declining wildlife populations, including riparian songbirds, reptiles, small mammals, and pollinators. Project implementation will include enhancement and active restoration activities. Implementation would occur over several phases. Phasing of implementation will allow elk to be safely excluded from the restoration areas and will be necessary due to limitations on water available for irrigation within the Reserve. Project Objectives include: 1. Establish self-sustaining riparian habitat along Buena Vista Slough. 2. Expand wetland habitat. 3. Enhance upland habitat across the Reserve. 4. Improve wildlife use of restored area. 5. Create pollinator and invertebrate habitat. 6. Expand rare plant populations. 7. Increase climate resiliency of the site. 8. Provide cultural and land stewardship opportunities for surrounding tribes. Enhancement Activities Portions of the Reserve that still host high-quality remnant herbaceous, wetland and upland scrub habitat supporting wildlife will be designated as enhancement areas where work will primarily consist of weed control—including hand weeding, mowing, herbicide application, and prescribed fire—and possibly supplemental seeding of native forbs and shrubs. Prescribed burning may be utilized to reduce non-native annual grass cover across the Reserve to prepare the area for restoration activities while minimizing ground disturbance to avoid impacts to sensitive species. Restoration Activities Other portions of the Reserve that are dominated by weeds (including non-native grasses) will require active restoration. Active restoration techniques may involve the use of prescribed fire, herbicide application and irrigation installation to prepare the site for seeding and planting. After hand-planting and seeding, using a drill-seeder or broadcast seeder, the site may be irrigated and weed control (herbicide, mowing, string trimming, hand-weeding) will be conducted to promote native plant establishment during the first three to five growing seasons, after which the Docusign Envelope ID: 6AB63BB5-3867-817F-831B-6E0B490AF028 DPR 508 (Rev. 4/2003)(Word 2/11/2005) plants will be self-sufficient. Container plants and cuttings will be irrigated using a drip irrigation system to supply a precise, targeted amount of water to plants, and a sprinkler system may be utilized for the seeded areas to ensure even water distribution. Irrigation water for restoration may be sourced from both the existing wells within the Reserve, as well as potentially purchased from a surrounding water district. Irrigation systems will be temporary in nature, providing water for three to five years, with the exception of demonstration plantings around the Day Use Area which will utilize an existing permanent irrigation system. For a more detailed project description contact the Great Basin District of California State Parks.

ceqa-9d5da73728320a4fab.description: Holmes Western Oil Corporation proposes to drill ten new oil & gas production wells in the Midway-Sunset Oil Field in Kern County. The proposed project would use existing well pads that are located on disturbed sites with existing access roads. The project area directly impacted by drilling each new well will occupy a temporary use area of approximately 100 x 200 feet (0.5 acres). Five existing well pads would be used for the ten new production wells. The project would take place on public lands containing BLM administered mineral estate, with a total project footprint equal to 2.82 acres. Drilling is expected to take approximately four days per well. A production rig will be used to complete the wells. Temporary equipment such as pumps and return bins will be needed. No permanent facilities will be constructed, and no expansion of associated facilities will be required. Waste materials will be properly disposed of as non-hazardous or hazardous waste, as appropriate, at a facility licensed to accept the waste.

ceqa-652da9a2362e906273.description: Santa Clara Valley Water District (Valley Water) and Kern-Tulare Water District (KTWD) are South of Delta Central Valley Project (CVP) contractors and are eligible participants in the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (USBR) South of Delta Accelerated Water Transfer Program for Contract Years 2025-2030, which provides an accelerated process for annual water transfers and/or exchanges between South of Delta CVP contractors that occur between March 1, 2025 and February 28, 2030. Valley Water has determined that up to 7,500 acre-feet of its 2026-2027 Municipal & Industrial Central Valley Project water supply allocation is surplus to the existing needs of its customers. During the 2026-2027 federal water year, Valley Water would request that USBR transfer up to 7,500 acre-feet of Valley Water’s surplus supplies to KTWD’s existing turnouts.

Valley Water will request that the California Department of Water Resources (DWR) transfer up to 8,000 acre feet of Valley Water’s surplus 2026 SWP Table A water to KCWA. DWR will deliver the water to KCWA via the SWP Banks Pumping Plant on Reach 1 of the California Aqueduct. KCWA will then deliver the water to Lost Hills Water District, Berrenda Mesa Water District, and Westside Mutual Water Company for use on existing agricultural lands in Kern County. The water will be transferred using existing diversion, conveyance, and storage facilities.

ceqa-318fc38f8f42187ad4.projectTitle: Airport Commerce Center Industrial Project by ACC Bakersfield JV, LLC.
ceqa-318fc38f8f42187ad4.description: The proposed Airport Commerce Center Industrial Project by ACC Bakersfield JV, LLC includes the development of four (4) industrial warehouse buildings totaling approximately 1,505,440 square-feet consisting of 625,446 square-feet for warehousing, 393,624 square-feet for cold storage, 335,826 square feet for industrial manufacturing or assembly for a food/beverage company, 150,544 square feet for office space, and two (2) associated quick-serve restaurants totaling approximately 9,410 square-feet on approximately 110 acres on privately owned parcels in the central portion of unincorporated Kern County. Implementation of the proposed project includes the following land use entitlements requests: General Plan Amendment No. 5, Map 81-35 of the Metropolitan Bakersfield General Plan Land Use Element from Map Code GC (General Commercial) to SI (Service Industrial) on an approximate 13.76-acre parcel of the 110-acre proposed project site. Zone Classification Change No. 46, Map 81-35 from M-1 PD H (Light Industrial – Precise Development Combining – Airport Approach Height Combining) to M-2 PD H (Medium Industrial – Precise Development Combining – Airport Approach Height Combining), or a more restrictive district, on an approximate 13.76-acre portion and from FPP (Floodplain Primary) to M-2 PD H (Medium Industrial – Precise Development Combining – Airport Approach Height Combining), or a more restrictive district, on an approximate 8.56-acre portion of the 110-acre proposed project site. Precise Development Plan No. 36, Map 81-35 for the development of four (4) industrial warehouse buildings totaling approximately 1,505,440 square-feet consisting of 625,446 square-feet for warehousing, 393,624 square-feet for cold storage, 335,826 square feet for industrial manufacturing or assembly for a food/beverage company, 150,544 square feet for office space, and two (2) associated quick-serve restaurants totaling approximately 9,410 square-feet on approximately 110 acres pursuant to Sections 19.38.020.D.1, 19.38.020.D.4, and 19.38.020.E.2 of the Kern County Zoning Ordinance. Nonsummary Vacation, Map 81-35 to vacate two (2) drainage easements on the proposed project site totaling approximately 10.24 acres.

ceqa-80e4866aca54f9de38.name: Initial Study and Negative Declaration for Amendment to General Plan and Annexation 22
ceqa-80e4866aca54f9de38.projectTitle: Initial Study and Negative Declaration for Amendment to General Plan and Annexation 22
ceqa-80e4866aca54f9de38.description: The City of McFarland conducted an environmental review of a project on the south side of McFarland. This project involves a general plan amendment and annexation into City limits of one relatively large parcel to the immediate south of Whisler Road, with SR 99 demarcating its western boundary and Driver Rd. demarcating its eastern boundary. The development application for Annexation #22 involves the parcel hitherto identified as 060-250-02. The parcel lies right outside the City limits and its coterminous sphere of influence (SOI). The initial development proposal is to pre-zone the parcel totaling 326 acres of vacant land via the annexation application to M-3, which refers to a “General Manufacturing” or “Heavy Industrial” district. It is the most intensive type of industrial zone, which allows for heavy manufacturing, chemical processing, large-scale warehousing, and similar activities that involve intensive industrial operations (17.152.030(8)). Notable land uses include: commercial stockyards and animal slaughter; dairies and livestock feed yards; dumps and refuse disposal areas; dwellings; junk, salvage or auto wrecking yards; sewer farms or sewage disposal plants. The project contains no new proposals which would result in any significant effects. The IS/ND for this annexation project has determined that the project contains no new proposals which would result in any significant effects that were not examined in the General Plan EIR. Therefore, the project would not have a significant effect on the environment.
ceqa-80e4866aca54f9de38.developmentType: Industrial (A project with building size has not yet been proposed. )(Sq. Ft. 1, Acres 326, Employees 1)

ceqa-82186c8b8d20f9b443.name: Cable Slope Repair DDO
ceqa-82186c8b8d20f9b443.description: The purpose of this project is to repair existing shoulders, slopes, and guardrail to prevent future erosion. Concentrated roadway drainage is overflowing existing drainage facilities on State Route 58 causing erosion damage to the shoulder, slope, and guardrail posts from postmile 88.8 to 89.1. The project consists of repairing erosion damage and increasing the hydraulic capacity of the roadside dike to prevent future erosion. Work includes removal and replacement of 40’ of the guardrail and dike, extension of the guardrail and dike, and placement of shoulder backing. Ground disturbance will be limited to the previously disturbed shoulder. All work and staging areas will be confined to Caltrans right-of-way.

ceqa-66f44b4e662312c3c2.name: Rosamond South Solar Project; Amendment No. 4 to the Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act (WJTCA) Incidental Take Permit (ITP) No. 1927-ITP-2023-018-04
ceqa-66f44b4e662312c3c2.projectTitle: Rosamond South Solar Project by Golden Fields Solar IV, LLC
ceqa-66f44b4e662312c3c2.description: The Project includes the construction and operation of photovoltaic (PV) solar facilities and associated infrastructure necessary to generate up to 165 megawatt (MW) alternating current (MW-AC) of renewable energy, including up to 245 MW (or 980 megawatt hours (MWh)) of energy storage, on approximately 1,302 acres of privately-owned land. The Project will result in incidental take of 1,354 western Joshua trees (WJT, Yucca brevifola), which are protected under the WJTCA and the California Endangered Species Act. The WJTCA ITP referenced above as issued by CDFW authorizes incidental take of WJT that may occur as a result of Project implementation. Amendment No. 1 revised the number of impacted WJT from 1,346 to 1,347 adding one additional live Class B WJT. Amendment No. 2 revised the number of impacted WJT from 1,347 to 1,371 trees. Amendment No. 3 authorized take of an additional 229 WJT and removes take authorization for 246 WJT, further revising the number of impacted WJT from 1,371 to 1,354. Amendment No.4 amends the WJT Preservation Condition of Approval and extends the deadline for recordation of the conservation easement.

ceqa-002b9f86ca15f44d1c.name: Eastside Sewer Lift Station (S25214)
ceqa-002b9f86ca15f44d1c.description: The Project proposes to develop a sewer lift station at an existing City of Tehachapi drainage easement location. The sewer lift station consists of the development of concrete pads, installation of lift station equipment and underground pipeline, and construction of a spillway. Ground disturbance associated with the sewer lift station will occur through development of the lift station’s wet well and spillway. The pipelines will consist of 6-inch force mains and 10-inch sewer lines that connect the proposed lift station to existing City infrastructure.
ceqa-002b9f86ca15f44d1c.crossStreets: East Tehachapi Blvd and Tehachapi Willow Springs Rd.

ceqa-30cfaeeaa5bbdbb346.name: City of Ridgecrest Las Flores Avenue HAWK (State Project Number HSIPSL-5385(078))
ceqa-30cfaeeaa5bbdbb346.projectTitle: City of Ridgecrest Las Flores Avenue HAWK (State Project Number HSIPSL-5385(078))
ceqa-30cfaeeaa5bbdbb346.description: The proposed project consists of pedestrian safety improvements at two existing intersections within the City of Ridgecrest, California. Improvements are intended to enhance pedestrian visibility and safety and reduce the potential for pedestrian-vehicle conflicts. At the intersection of Las Flores Avenue and Sierra View Street, the project includes installation of a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon (PHB/HAWK signal). The intersection is directly adjacent to Las Flores Elementary School and several residences. Construction activities would occur within the existing public right-of-way and include minor roadway paving, curb ramp reconstruction to improve accessibility, median construction, installation of traffic signal equipment, associated wiring and conduit, and roadway signing and striping. Existing asphalt pavement would be removed and re-compacted with asphalt rubber hot mix over approximately four inches of asphalt base. No roadway widening is proposed. Construction limits at this intersection extend approximately 200 feet along each approach of Las Flores Avenue and approximately 50 feet into Sierra View Street. At the intersection of Graaf Avenue and Alene Avenue, the project includes installation of an overhead pedestrian warning assembly, consisting of a flashing pedestrian sign and rapid rectangular flashing beacons (RRFBs). The intersection is adjacent to a parking lot and several residences. Work would include installation of traffic signal equipment and related hardware necessary to support the overhead pedestrian warning system. All improvements would occur within the existing roadway and right-of-way. Construction limits at this intersection extend approximately 50 feet from each approach. The project would not introduce new land uses, increase roadway capacity, or alter traffic patterns beyond improving pedestrian safety. The proposed improvements are consistent with the Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP), which is intended to reduce fatalities and serious injuries on public roadways. The Las Flores Avenue and Sierra View Street improvements are funded through Caltrans HSIP Cycle 12, while the Graaf Avenue and Alene Avenue improvements are funded through local sources. There are no mapped hazardous waste incidents or facilities, including leaking underground storage tanks, in the project vicinity. (Calif. RWCB Geotracker, available at https://geotracker.waterboards.ca.gov/; U.S. EPA Cleanups in My Community maps, available at https://www.epa.gov/cleanups/cleanups-my-community; California Dept. of Toxic Substances Control maps, available at https://www.envirostor.dtsc.ca.gov/public/, accessed February 2026). Setting: The project intersections are located within developed areas. There is no natural habitat within or immediately adjacent to the project boundaries. Beneficiaries: Ridgecrest pedestrians will benefit from improved safety at the intersections, reducing fatalities and serious injuries on the public roads.
ceqa-30cfaeeaa5bbdbb346.crossStreets: Las Flores Avenue and Sierra View Street, Graaf Avenue and Alene Avenue

ceqa-9516c81bf6579dd0db.description: The proposed project consists of the California Department of Conservation, Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM) approving 1 permit for California Resources Elk Hills, LLC to rework the well: 326-10Z listed below, in the Railroad Gap Oil Field in Kern County. The rework project includes bringing well-repaired equipment to the site and setting it up for use. Pull sucker rods, pump and production tubing. Perforate from 5900’ to 7500’ (net footage TBD). Run production tubing, pump and rods. Remove the well repaired equipment from the site after rework is complete. Return well to production. The proposed project is located within Kern County, California, in an area where oil and gas exploration and production activities have historically occurred and are anticipated to continue. The project site lies within the San Joaquin Valley portion of Kern County, generally defined as lands below an elevation of 1,000 feet above mean sea level. Kern County encompasses approximately 8,202 square miles and is located at the southern end of California’s Central Valley. The County includes a diverse range of land uses and environmental conditions, including agricultural lands, oil and gas development areas, and desert environments. The project site is located within the southern portion of the San Joaquin Valley Air Basin, which is regulated by the San Joaquin Valley Air Pollution Control District. The area is also located within the Tulare Lake Groundwater Basin, including the Kern River and Poso Hydrographic Units, which are subject to Regional Water Quality Control Board oversight. These environmental conditions are typical of areas supporting long-standing oil and gas operations in Kern County. Project Well(s): • Well Name: 326-10Z, API 0403041456

ceqa-4c4b5f8afe203abac2.description: Holmes Western Oil Corporation (H5200) proposes to rework existing well Pacific 15 to cement off existing perforations and then re-perforate the section, ensuring cement gets outside the 6-5/8" casing into the 8-5/8" x 6-5/8" annulus and cement a 4-1/2" tieback string in the well. The project is expected to take 4 days. Construction related activities are not required. All equipment will be contained within existing facilities and there will be no expansion of existing former use. Temporary equipment needed for the project includes a Production Rig, Rig Pump, Cement Truck, Bins, and a Storage Tank. Vehicles needed to transport personnel, deliver supplies and materials, and transport waste will also visit the project site. Reworking the well will require the use of 321 bbls (10,112 gallons) of produced water and 52 bbls (1,638 gallons) of fresh water to mix the cement. Produced water will come from our Parkinson Production Facility, approximately 1.49miles from the well location. The produced water will be transported to the project location by vacuum truck. Fresh water will be provided by the cementing service company. The proposed project consists of the California Department of Conservation, Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM) approving 1 permit(s) for Holmes Western Oil Corporation (H5200)to rework the well(s) listed below, in the Midway-Sunset Oil Field. ceqa-31478dbff8eb5b20e2.description: The project consists of routine roadway and right-of-way maintenance activities conducted by the Bear Valley Community Services District within Bear Valley Springs, Kern County. Work will occur within existing disturbed rights-of-way and will not involve expansion of roadways or new ground disturbance beyond minor surface impacts associated with maintenance activities. ceqa-8dadf35144bb83c954.name: EDPP Surge Tank Control Line Project Phase 2 Additional Work
ceqa-8dadf35144bb83c954.projectTitle: EDPP Surge Tank Control Line Project Phase 2 Additional Work
ceqa-8dadf35144bb83c954.description: San Joaquin Field Division plans to remove twenty power poles, install eight power poles, install 1.5 miles of fiber, and replace .25 miles of conductor cable between the Edmonston Pumping Plant and Edmonston surge tank. Where accessible, a ¾-ton pickup truck, digger derrick, and portable air compressor will be used to excavate holes for new poles. In areas where no existing ground access is available, a helicopter will be used to transport personnel and equipment. New poles will be flown in by helicopter. Once the new poles are installed, workers will climb the poles and move the wires by hand from the old poles to the new poles. Power poles that are slated for removal will be cut below grade level and flown out by helicopter. Fiber installation will involve no ground disturbance. Crews will be flown to each pole to install mounting hardware and travelers. A rope rig will be placed at Pole VV. Fiber installation will start at Pole 001. Crews will pull rope and fiber by hand. SJFD staff will complete all required splices and final connections. Damaged #4 conductor cable from poles LL to VV will be replaced with #2 ACSR conductor. This work will also include the reframing of three poles. Conductor will be pulled directly, eliminating the need for rope. All vehicles and equipment will stay on established roads and within designated areas. All other work areas will be reached by foot or helicopter. The following equipment will be used to complete this work: two ¾-ton pickup trucks, two 55’ AWD bucket trucks, two 47’ AWD digger derricks, two air compressors, one rope rig, one helicopter, a water buffalo, a flatbed truck, and a telehandler or forklift. All equipment staging will occur within graveled or paved areas. This work is necessary to continue to deliver water to southern California.

ceqa-52c987073f0a406064.name: CESA Amended ITP No. 2081-2022-064-04 (Minor Amendment No. 7) for the SoCalGas eTS 58713.01 Line 85 Milepost 75.85 Remediation Digs Project
ceqa-52c987073f0a406064.projectTitle: California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2022-064-04 for the eTS 58713.01 Line 85 Milepost 75.85 Remediation Digs Project
ceqa-52c987073f0a406064.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Central Region 4
ceqa-52c987073f0a406064.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 4 - Central, Fresno
ceqa-52c987073f0a406064.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has issued an amended ITP (No. 2081-2022-064-04-A7), to authorize SoCalGas (Permittee) to incidentally take Tipton kangaroo rat (Dipodomys nitratoides nitratoides) which is as an endangered species under CESA, San Joaquin antelope squirrel (Ammospermophilus nelsoni) which is designated as a threatened species under CESA, and San Joaquin kit fox (Vulpes macrotis mutica) which is designated as a threatened species under CESA (Fish & G. Code § 2050 et seq.; see Cal. Code Regs., tit. 14, § 670.5, subd. (a)(6)(D), (b)(6)(B), and (b)(6)(E), respectively). Collectively, these are referred to as the Covered Species. The Project includes activities necessary to inspect and repair five segments of the 26-inch natural gas pipeline (Line) 85 near MP 75.85 where anomalies were identified and to install cathodic protection for integrity and safety of the pipeline. This Amended ITP (Major Amendment No. 7) extends the expiration date for an additional 6 months, extends the timeline to complete the HM Lands requirement by an additional 18 months, expands Work Area 6 from 1,500 square feet (0.034 acre) to 3,375 square feet (0.077 acre) to accommodate an additional laydown area and parking area, installs a new concrete pad for the new cabinet rectifier, reroutes and buries the existing gas tap that served the former TEG to connect to the new TEG to restore cathodic protection and maintain pipeline integrity within the approved Project Area, and revises Figure 6a. The resulting impacts of the Project to the Covered Species remain the same. The Project will result in temporary impacts to 0.76 acres of Covered Species habitat and permanently impacts to 2.67 square feet (0.000061 acre) of habitat for the Covered Species. Covered Species may disperse across the 1.23-acre disturbed/developed area (existing unvegetated, compacted dirt roads), which may be disrupted while Project activities are occurring, but these areas do not provide other habitat values for the Covered Species. The project is expected to result in incidental take of the Covered Species. The ITP referenced above as issued by CDFW authorizes incidental take of species listed under CESA that may occur as a result of Project implementation.

ceqa-ae121458d45eb050ab.name: Galaxy Solar PV and Storage Project by Galaxy Solar Storage, LLC
ceqa-ae121458d45eb050ab.projectTitle: Galaxy Solar PV and Storage Project by Galaxy Solar Storage, LLC (Terra-Gen)
ceqa-ae121458d45eb050ab.description: The proposed Galaxy Solar PV and Storage Project is a photovoltaic (PV) solar facility with associated infrastructure necessary to generate up to 600-megawatt (MW) of renewable electrical energy, which may include up to 4 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of energy storage capacity (approximately 1,000 MW), on an approximate 3,519-acre project site, across 184 privately owned parcels, in an unincorporated area of southeastern Kern County, California. A temporary offsite laydown area would be placed adjacent to State Route (SR)-58, at the northern extent of the project site. PV solar panels, a power collection system, including medium-voltage (MV) lines that connect the solar facilities, inverters, a switchyard, foundations, and transformers will be installed onsite. Associated project infrastructure includes an operations and maintenance (O&M) facility, telecommunication facilities, energy storage system(s), an onsite collector substation, a 230-kV switchyard, and offsite water storage tanks for construction and operation. The proposed project also includes a generation-tie (gen-tie) line to connect the project to the existing Windhub Substation. Implementation of the project as proposed includes the following land use entitlement requests: Zone Change (a) Zone Classification Change No. 5, Map 195 from A-1 (Limited Agriculture) to A (Exclusive Agriculture) on approximately 1007 acres; (b) Zone Classification Change No. 4, Map 212 from A-1 (Limited Agriculture) to A (Exclusive Agriculture) on approximately 2,460.02 acres; Conditional Use Permit (a) Conditional Use Permit No. 4, Map 195, to allow for the construction and operation of a solar facility up to 150 MW and associated infrastructure, including energy storage, a switchyard, and temporary construction staging and equipment storage on approximately 974.95 acres in an A (Exclusive Agriculture) District, pursuant to Chapter 19.12.030.G and 19.12.030K of the Kern County Zoning Ordinance. (b) Conditional Use Permit No. 5, Map 195, to allow for a temporary construction laydown area on approximately 25.08 acres of a 41.62 acre parcel, pursuant to Chapter 19.12.030.G and 19.12.030.K of the Kern County Zoning Ordinance. (c) Conditional Use Permit No. 7, Map 212, to allow for the construction and operation of a solar facility up to 450 MW and associated infrastructure, including energy storage, a switchyard, and temporary construction staging and equipment storage on approximately 2,244.99 acres in an A (Exclusive Agriculture) District, pursuant to Chapter 19.12.030.G and 19.12.030K of the Kern County Zoning Ordinance; General Plan Amendment (Circulation) (a) General Plan Amendment No. 5, Map 195, to the Circulation Element of the Kern County General Plan (General Plan) to remove future road reservations on section and mid-section lines within the project boundary; (b) General Plan Amendment No. 6, Map 212, to the Circulation Element of the General Plan to remove future road reservations on section and mid-section lines within the project boundary; (c) General Plan Amendment No. 7, Map 212, to the Open Space, Land Use, and Conservation Element of the General Plan to re-designate two parcels (APNs 244-233-06 and 244-421-01) from General Plan Designation 3.3 (Other Facilities) to General Plan Designation 8.5 (Resource Management). Zone Variance: (a) Zone Variance No. 1, Map 195, to authorize multiple parcels of substandard size where a minimum of 20 acres is required for each change in base zoning from the A-1 (Limited Agriculture) District to the A (Exclusive Agriculture) District across approximately 79.56 total acres. (b) Zone Variance No. 2, Map 212, to authorize multiple parcels of substandard size where a minimum of 20 acres is required for each change in base zoning from the A-1 (Limited Agriculture) District to the A (Exclusive Agriculture) District across approximately 88.91 total acres Vesting Tentative Parcel Maps: (a) Vesting Tentative Parcel Map No. 12577—Proposing a merger and re-subdivision of three (3) parcels into one (1) parcel of Case Map 195, Section 28, Township 11 North, Range 11 West, of County of Kern, consisting of 23.02 acres (gross), resulting in a 23.02 acre (gross) parcel. (b) Vesting Tentative Parcel Map No. 12578—Proposing a merger and re-subdivision of twenty-eight (28) parcels into one (1) parcel of Case Map 195, Section 33, Township 11 North, Range 11 West, of County of Kern, consisting of 302.32 acres (gross), resulting in a 302.32 acre (gross) parcel. (c) Vesting Tentative Parcel Map No. 12579—Proposing a merger and re-subdivision of six (6) parcels into one (1) parcel of Case Map 195, Section 34, Township 11 North, Range 11 West, of County of Kern, consisting of 157.93 acre acres (gross), resulting in a 157.93 acre (gross) parcel. (d) Vesting Tentative Parcel Map No. 12580—Proposing a merger and re-subdivision of twenty-seven (27) parcels into one (1) parcel of Case Map 212, Section 4, Township 10 North, Range 11 West, of County of Kern, consisting of 90.81 (acres (gross), resulting in a 90.81 acre (gross) parcel. (e) Vesting Tentative Parcel Map No. 12581—Proposing a merger and re-subdivision of fifty-two (52) parcels into one (1) parcel of Case Map 212, Section 4, Township 10 North, Range 11 West, of County of Kern, consisting of 298.29 acres (gross), resulting in a 298.29 acre (gross) parcel. (f) Vesting Tentative Parcel Map No. 12582—Proposing a merger and re-subdivision of twenty-four (24) parcels into one (1) parcel of Case Map 212, Section 8, Township 10 North, Range 11 West, of County of Kern, consisting of 500.58 acres (gross), resulting in a 500.58 acre (gross) parcel. Offsite Features: (a) Zone Classification Change No. 5, Map 212 from A-1 (Limited Agriculture) to A (Exclusive Agriculture) to facilitate installation of offsite water storage tanks for construction and operations on approximately 20.00 acres; (b) Zone Classification Change No. 57, Map 197 from A-1 (Limited Agriculture) to A (Exclusive Agriculture) to facilitate installation construction and operation of an off-site switchyard and temporary construction and equipment storage on approximately 34.82 acres; (c) Conditional Use Permit No. 24, Map 197, to allow for the construction and operation of an off-site switchyard and temporary construction staging and equipment storage on approximately 29.14 acres in an A (Exclusive Agriculture) District, pursuant to Chapter 19.12.030.G and 19.12.030K of the Kern County Zoning Ordinance; (d) Zone Variance No. 21, Map 197, to authorize multiple parcels of substandard size where a minimum of 20 acres is required for each change in base zoning from the A-1 (Limited Agriculture) District to the A (Exclusive Agriculture) District across approximately 34.82 total acres.

ceqa-f9110f15e8c8908e84.name: Mojave Life of Mine Reclamation Plan Amendment Project by CalPortland Company
ceqa-f9110f15e8c8908e84.projectTitle: Mojave Life of Mine Reclamation Plan Amendment Project by CalPortland Company
ceqa-f9110f15e8c8908e84.description: The proposed Mojave Life of Mine Reclamation Plan Amendment Project consists of reclamation activities, such as recontouring, stabilizing, revegetation, and monitoring of final slopes and disturbed mining areas; reclamation of roads and ancillary equipment and facilities; and removal of the processing and cement plant facilities within the approximately 4,367-acre proposed project site. Although some reclamation activities are and would continue to be performed concurrent with ongoing mining and processing, reclamation activities for final site reclamation would occur after the completion of mining and processing operations. On March 15, 2021, the Kern County Planning and Natural Resources Department determined that mining and processing activities are a legal nonconforming (vested) use on approximately 6,658 acres of land owned by the project proponent, inclusive of the approximately 4,367 acres covered by the proposed project. As such, vested and continuing mining activities such as drilling, blasting, material recovery, material movement (with the exception of material movement pertaining to reclamation, e.g. redistribution of stockpiled growth media to aid in revegetation efforts), processing, cement production, and material transport for sale are not subject to discretionary approval by Kern County, and as such are not part of the proposed project. The project proponent proposes to continue to develop its limestone and construction materials resources within the existing vested properties and to increase the life of the mine by approximately 200 years to continue cement and construction materials production. The proposed project would not involve changes to the existing vested mining operations including, for example, production levels, mining systems or processes, and ultimate throughput from the cement plant. Reclamation of continued operations would require the approval of the proposed project which would amend the approximately 1,542-acre existing reclamation plan (approved in 1979) through approval of the proposed approximately 4,367-acre reclamation plan applicable to the vested properties.
ceqa-f9110f15e8c8908e84.crossStreets: Tehachapi Willow Springs Road and Oak Creek Road

ceqa-ed1c20fd2a5478447b.name: Pastoria Solar Gen-Tie Project (California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2025-006-04 (ITP) Minor Amendment No. 1)
ceqa-ed1c20fd2a5478447b.projectTitle: Pastoria Solar Project by Pastoria Solar Energy, LLC
ceqa-ed1c20fd2a5478447b.description: The Project includes work along a solar generation tie line that provides connection between the proposed Pastoria Solar Project and the existing Pastoria Energy Facility Lebec switchyard east of the Project site. The Project is expected to result in incidental take of the fully protected and state endangered blunt-nosed leopard lizard (Gambelia sila), which is protected under the California Endangered Species Act (CESA) and Fish and Game Code section 5050 (fully protected species). The Project is expected to cause permanent impacts to 0.14 acres and temporary impacts to 1.49 acres of blunt-nosed leopard lizard habitat. All anticipated impacts will occur within previously disturbed areas such as established dirt roads. The Permittee will purchase 1.91 acres in Covered Species credits at a CDFW-approved mitigation or conservation bank to fully mitigate these habitat impacts in a manner that meets the conservation standard required by Fish and Game Code section 2081.15. Minor Amendment No. 1 amends several Conditions of Approval to extend ITP expiration date, extend the deadline to purchase Covered Species credits, and clarify the requirements for mitigation bank credit purchase.

ceqa-2ab60d7ba0fa8e0385.name: 2026 MP 275.56 Double Overchute Cleaning
ceqa-2ab60d7ba0fa8e0385.description: San Joaquin Field Division plans to remove sediment and debris from overchute 275.56 of the State Water Project. To do this work, a skid steer, bulldozer, loader, and/or excavator will be used to remove sediment and debris from the overchute and inlet area. A water truck will be used to control dust. A dump truck will be used to transport sediment and debris approximately 2 miles away to the Wheeler Ridge Pumping Plant (WRPP) spoil site. At the spoil site, all sediment will be spread out and compacted. Equipment will be stored overnight at the WRPP. This work is necessary to prevent flooding and damage to critical infrastructure. Work is estimated to take three weeks to complete. All work will take place within the DWR right-of-way.

ceqa-9e294c8c2dc08076ad.description: [PROJECT TITLE CONTINUED]: (SWP #26017, SWP #26018, and SWP #26019) SWP #26017, #26018, and #26019 collectively provide for a transfer of Solano County Water Agency’s (Solano’s) approved 2026 SWP Table A Water and Article 56 Carryover Water to KCWA and Dudley Ridge, on behalf of the Westside Districts, through December 31, 2026, as follows: • SWP #26017 provides for the transfer and delivery of up to 585 acre-feet of Solano’s approved 2026 Table A water to Dudley Ridge and/or KCWA; • SWP #26018 provides for the transfer and delivery of 7,625 acre-feet of Solano’s Article 56 Carryover Water to KCWA, on behalf of its member units that makeup the Westside Districts (Belridge Water Storage District, Berrenda Mesa Water District, Lost Hills Water District, and Wheeler Ridge – Maricopa Water Storage District); and • SWP #26019 provides for the transfer and delivery of 1,375 acre-feet of Solano’s Article 56 Carryover Water to Dudley Ridge.

ceqa-a560c59c815a8de1c0.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has issued an ITP (No. 2081-2021-039-04), pursuant to Section 2081(b) of the Fish and Game Code to Chevron U.S.A., Inc. The Project will construct six large, graded pads (i.e., Work Areas) ranging in size from approximately 3.2 acres to approximately 23.1 acres. These pads will support future oil production wells, injection wells, observation wells, and associated facilities and infrastructure, but those activities are not covered by this ITP. Pad construction consists of track-out control, vegetation removal, site preparation, grading, and compaction. The Project will result in impacts to 46.4 acres of San Joaquin antelope squirrel (Ammospermophilus nelsoni) and Temblor legless lizard (Anniella alexanderae) (Covered Species) habitat, permanently removing 46.4 acres of Covered Species habitat. The project is expected to result in incidental take of San Joaquin antelope squirrel, which is designated as a threatened species under the California Endangered Species Act (CESA) (Fish & G. Code, §§ 2050 et seq.) (See Cal Code Regs., tit. 14, § 670.5, subd. (b)(6)(B)) and Temblor legless lizard, a species designated as candidate for listing pursuant to CESA (Fish & G. Code, §§ 2050 et seq. and § 2068). The ITP referenced above as issued by CDFW authorizes incidental take of species listed under CESA that may occur as a result of Project implementation.
