ceqa-65c7f1b6dc6f9400d3.name: 568380_Group_Aera_UIC
ceqa-65c7f1b6dc6f9400d3.description: The primary work objective is to sidetrack two (2) existing well(s). This work is designed to support continuation of oil and gas resource development in the area. The wells are not being sidetracked (i) for abandonment purposes only or (ii) in connection with an enforcement order to mitigate or prevent environmental damage or surface expression. Sidetracking is the process of drilling a new wellbore from an existing wellbore. This is typically done when the original wellbore encounters a problem, when accessing remaining hydrocarbons within portions of the same reservoir, or when obstructions in the wellbore need to be bypassed. This process allows drilling a new section in an existing wellbore in the same rock formation restoring the well’s original functionality. The potential disturbance footprint would encompass an existing 20,000 square foot (100 ft x 200 ft) well pad per well. The entirety of this work would be located in an area of existing disturbance and no change in the surface topography (such as drainage patterns) would result. There will be no expansion of the existing well pads, roads, staging areas, or pipelines. No new grading would occur in any undisturbed areas. No new road construction or expansions would be required for the proposed project. Routine maintenance activities at the site would include removal of weeds and other ruderal vegetation for fire control and road maintenance. The work will commence after CalGEM permit approval. The time of year the work would occur is dependent on the date of final CalGEM permit approval. For a single well, it is expected to take approximately 17 operational days to complete all construction phases. Construction activities would generally include the following phases with estimated duration: 1. Plugging a portion of existing wellbore – 2 days • Zonal plugging of wellbore to be sidetracked from in accordance with CalGEM plugging requirements. 2. Site preparation – 7 days • Site location work on existing well pads to create safe work site for personnel and environment 3. Sidetrack drilling (construction) of the well – 3 days • Sidetracking operations in accordance with CalGEM regulations 4. Well completion – 2 days • Subsurface completion of well in accordance with CalGEM regulations 5. Final site surface construction – 3 days • Re-installation of various aboveground piping and equipment to connect well sites to the existing infrastructure Each phase requires different combinations of temporary equipment. At the end of each construction phase, the temporary equipment would be removed from the well site. All work during the project phases, except for the drilling phase, will occur during the days Monday through Friday, and approximate hours from 6 am to 5 pm. The drilling rig will operate 24 hours per day. The construction activity will not include installation of new pipelines or infrastructure. No new ground disturbance would occur. The proposed construction activities would use existing electrical lines. The proposed construction activities would involve a combination of re-use, repair, or reinstallation of various above-ground piping to connect subject well sites to the existing infrastructure. The proposed sidetracks are of existing cyclic steam wells which are completed in the Lombardi Sands (Pool: Lombardi, Pool Code: 10). The Lombardi Sands in the San Ardo Oil Field is a known hydrocarbon zone. The proposed sidetracks will remain in the same pool as the original wellbore. The pool designation will not change. The proposed sidetracks will NOT change the current designation of the existing wells. The proposed project consists of the California Department of Conservation, Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM) approving two (2) permit(s) for Aera Energy LLC to perform sidetrack work on the wells listed below, in the San Ardo Oil Field. API # Well Name 0405322271 Orradre 1613-12 0405322264 Orradre 1438-12

ceqa-ac572207d157d187be.name: Pajaro/Sunny Mesa Springfield Area Regional Consolidation Project
ceqa-ac572207d157d187be.projectTitle: Pajaro/Sunny Mesa Springfield Area Regional Consolidation Project
ceqa-ac572207d157d187be.agency: Pajaro Sunny Mesa Community Service District
ceqa-ac572207d157d187be.agencyName: Pajaro Sunny Mesa Community Service District
ceqa-ac572207d157d187be.description: The Proposed Project is a two (2)-phased project consisting of the consolidation of the Pajaro Water System (“PWS”), Sunny Mesa Water System (“SMWS”), and Springfield Water System (“SWS”), as well as the various water connections in the North of Moss Landing (“NOML”) area into a single water system to be owned and operated by the District. The First Phase of the Proposed Project is anticipated to be funded by the State Water Resources Control Board (“SWRCB”) Expedited Drinking Water Grant and would consist of annexation of parcels into the District’s service area, land acquisition and easements, an Iron and Manganese Treatment System at the existing District office, consolidation pipelines (Transmission Mains) connecting the PWS to the SMWS and the SMWS to the SWS, Transmission Pump Station to convey water from PWS to SMWS, rehabilitation of the PWS’ existing 600,000 gallon welded steel water storage tank, electrical upgrades to the Sunny Mesa tank site, conversion of SMWS Wells No. 1 and No. 2 to standby-only use, radio meter upgrades, and installation of a Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (“SCADA”) system. The First Phase of the Proposed Project is anticipated to be funded through the State Water Resources Control Board (“SWRCB”) Expedited Drinking Water Grant Program. The Second Phase of the Proposed Project is anticipated to be funded by the California Safe Drinking Water State Revolving Fund (“CA SRF”) funds from the SWRCB and would consist of the installation of the Springfield Expansion Distribution Main and the Bluff/Jensen Distribution Main, construction of the Bluff/Jensen tank and pump station, and installation of lateral service connections located on private property. The First Phase of the Proposed Project has been designed so that it could operate as a standalone water system in the event that the Second Phase of the Proposed Project is not funded or otherwise delayed. Once operational, the Proposed Project is anticipated to serve approximately 967 total connections. The Proposed Project includes approximately 46,000 linear feet (“LF”) of potable watermains between both phases, and a total of 235,000 LF of total pipeline when including service laterals and appurtenances. The pipeline infrastructure would include pipelines of six (6), eight (8), and 10-inch diameters. The Proposed Project would primarily be supplied water from three (3) sources, comprised of Pajaro Wells No. 1 and No. 2 and Springfield Well No. 2. Additionally, SMWS Wells No. 1 and No. 2 would be retained as standby sources of water for the Proposed Project, for an overall total of five (5) water sources. In addition, the Proposed Project includes additional infrastructure improvements at the existing PWS Water Storage Tank and Sunny Mesa Tank Site to facilitate O&M of the new water system.

ceqa-192c1a0b3f58f53691.name: 2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan/Sustainable Communities Strategy and 2050 Regional Transportation Plans for San Benito, Santa Cruz, and Monterey Counties
ceqa-192c1a0b3f58f53691.projectTitle: 2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan/Sustainable Communities Strategy and 2050 Regional Transportation Plans for San Benito, Santa Cruz, and Monterey Counties
ceqa-192c1a0b3f58f53691.agency: Association of Monterey Bay Area Governments
ceqa-192c1a0b3f58f53691.agencyName: Association of Monterey Bay Area Governments
ceqa-192c1a0b3f58f53691.description: As the metropolitan planning organization for the tri-county region of Monterey, San Benito, and Santa Cruz counties, the Association of Monterey Bay Area Governments (AMBAG) is charged with developing a 2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan/Sustainable Communities Strategy (MTP/SCS). The 2050 MTP/SCS is both a long-range transportation plan and Sustainable Communities Strategy for Monterey, San Benito, and Santa Cruz counties. The Council of San Benito County Governments, the Santa Cruz County Regional Transportation Commission, and the Transportation Agency for Monterey County are the state-designated Regional Transportation Planning Agencies for San Benito, Santa Cruz, and Monterey counties, respectively. Each prepares a county-level long-range Regional Transportation Plan, which is evaluated in the EIR. The 2050 MTP/SCS is used to guide the development of the Regional and Federal Transportation Improvement Programs, as well as other transportation programming documents and plans. The MTP outlines the region's goals and policies for meeting current and future mobility needs, providing a foundation for transportation decisions by local, regional, and state officials that are ultimately aimed at achieving a coordinated and balanced transportation system. The 2050 MTP/SCS sets forth actions, programs, and projects to address these needs consistent with adopted policies and goals. The 2050 MTP/SCS also documents the financial resources needed to implement the plan. Additionally, pursuant to SB 375, AMBAG (as the regional MPO) must prepare an SCS that demonstrates how the region will meet its greenhouse gas reduction target (6% reduction by 2035) through integrated land use, housing, and transportation planning.

ceqa-932089dc15ff99e40f.name: PG&E East Campus Gas Line Replacement Project
ceqa-932089dc15ff99e40f.projectTitle: PG&E East Campus Gas Line Replacement Project
ceqa-932089dc15ff99e40f.description: The proposed PG&E East Campus Gas Line Replacement project involves the replacement and upgrade of existing natural gas distribution infrastructure within the CSUMB East Campus Housing Area in unincorporated Monterey County, California. The project area includes Assessor’s Parcel Numbers (APNs) 031-101-031, 031-101-032, 031-171-033, and 031-181-056, and encompasses multiple residential streets within the East Campus Housing Area. The project is part of Pacific Gas and Electric Company’s (PG&E) statewide initiative to replace aging Aldyl “A” plastic gas pipelines manufactured prior to 1973, which have a documented history of cracking and failure. The replacement program was initiated in response to safety concerns following a pipeline failure incident in Cupertino, California, in 2011. The proposed project consists of replacing approximately 27,543 linear feet of existing gas distribution main and 390 service connections with new polyethylene plastic pipelines. Work would occur primarily within existing paved roadway corridors and disturbed areas using a combination of horizontal directional drilling (HDD) and open trenching construction methods to minimize surface disturbance. Construction activities would occur in multiple phases within the existing utility easements and rights-of-way. The purpose of the project is to reduce threats to the integrity of the natural gas distribution system, improve public safety, and enhance system reliability within the CSUMB East Campus Housing Area. The project would also ensure continued safe and efficient delivery of natural gas to residents and campus facilities and reduce the need for future emergency repairs and maintenance.

Electric vehicle owners would benefit from this project as well as the City residents, indirectly, as electric vehicles help reduce air pollution.

ceqa-01c583e121726b6996.name: PG&E East Campus Gas Line Replacement Project

ceqa-01c583e121726b6996.description: The proposed PG&E East Campus Gas Line Replacement project involves the replacement and upgrade of existing natural gas distribution infrastructure within the CSUMB East Campus Housing Area in unincorporated Monterey County, California. The project area includes Assessor’s Parcel Numbers (APNs) 031-101-031, 031-101-032, 031-171-033, and 031-181-056, and encompasses multiple residential streets within the East Campus Housing Area. The project is part of Pacific Gas and Electric Company’s (PG&E) statewide initiative to replace aging Aldyl “A” plastic gas pipelines manufactured prior to 1973, which have a documented history of cracking and failure. The replacement program was initiated in response to safety concerns following a pipeline failure incident in Cupertino, California, in 2011. The proposed project consists of replacing approximately 27,543 linear feet of existing gas distribution main and 390 service connections with new polyethylene plastic pipelines. Work would occur primarily within existing paved roadway corridors and disturbed areas using a combination of horizontal directional drilling (HDD) and open trenching construction methods to minimize surface disturbance. Construction activities would occur in multiple phases within the existing utility easements and rights-of-way. Please refer to Attachment A, CEQA Supporting Documentation, for additional project description information, available for review upon request at CSUMB’s Campus Planning and Development offices. The purpose of the project is to reduce threats to the integrity of the natural gas distribution system, improve public safety, and enhance system reliability within the CSUMB East Campus Housing Area. The project would also ensure continued safe and efficient delivery of natural gas to residents and campus facilities and reduce the need for future emergency repairs and maintenance. The beneficiaries of the project include Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) and residents of the CSUMB East Campus Housing Area on the California State University, Monterey Bay main campus. The project would provide long-term safety and reliability improvements to the local natural gas distribution system, consistent with PG&E’s ongoing efforts to modernize critical utility infrastructure across California. CSU discretionary action related to this project is limited to the issuance of a Right to Access permit and a Temporary Work Authorization permit to PG&E to allow it to carry out the proposed improvements on the CSUMB campus.

ceqa-eec47683b50a53dc7e.name: Invasive Species Control for Nipomo Mesa Lupine Recovery
ceqa-eec47683b50a53dc7e.projectTitle: Invasive Species Control for Nipomo Mesa Lupine Recovery
ceqa-eec47683b50a53dc7e.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Central Region 4
ceqa-eec47683b50a53dc7e.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 4 - Central, Fresno
ceqa-eec47683b50a53dc7e.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife is issuing a California Endangered Species Act scientific, educational, or management permit pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 2081, subdivision (a) to the California Department of Parks and Recreation, Oceano Dunes State Vehicular Recreation Area (Permit No. 2081(a)-26-011-RP). The permit will continue management activities that were previously authorized under California Endangered Species Act Permit No. 2081(a)-21-008-RP to support Nipomo Mesa lupine conservation, including invasive perennial veldt grass control, protection of plants from herbivory, and experimental aerial application of clethodim-based graminicide. Activities will include surveys and mapping of Nipomo Mesa lupine, ground herbicide application outside no-spray buffers, manual weed removal, and installation of protective cages around seedlings. A minimum 15-foot no-spray buffer will be maintained around identified plants and recent mapped locations, except within designated aerial research plots. Experimental aerial treatments will be conducted in the Walter’s Valley and Railroad North subpopulations, which were selected because of their heavy veldt grass cover and separation from other lupine populations. Treatments may be conducted up to twice per growing season for one to five years, using a helicopter or herbicide-equipped drone. Monitoring will evaluate plant condition, vigor, herbivory, phenology, and reproduction before and after treatment. The experiment builds on previous research studies indicating that aerial clethodim can effectively control perennial veldt grass without significant adverse effects on native vegetation or Nipomo Mesa lupine plants.

ceqa-82f8ffb0dffbf024ad.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ceqa-82f8ffb0dffbf024ad.agencyName: Forestry and Fire Protection, Department of
ceqa-82f8ffb0dffbf024ad.description: The Cal Poly SLO Fuel Reduction project will apply broadcast prescribed fire across approximately 535 acres within seven distinct treatment units of predominantly annual grasslands, intermixed with coyote brush. The seven treatment units are located within Cal Poly’s ranchland, campus-adjacent wildlands, and WUI zones, all within a High Fire Hazard Severity Zone. The primary objectives are to reduce high fuel loading of fine fuels and improve ecological resilience. Burns will be conducted under CAL FIRE approved burn plans, favorable weather prescriptions, and SLO APCD smoke management requirements. No mechanical treatments are proposed. CAL FIRE and Cal Poly Hand crews will be used along the existing access roads and proposed control lines to improve the access/evacuation route; and as needed in equipment exclusion zones. Hand crews may be used prior to burning to improve control lines or protect infrastructure (e.g., improve access/evacuation routes, protect fences/structures, trim oak trees adjacent to unit). No tree removal is proposed. Burns will utilize existing roads and trails as primary control lines; no new roads are planned. No work will occur with known sensitive species occurrences. Treatment activities include manual fire control line construction, prescribed burning, hand crew thinning, chipping, pile burning, pruning, and hazard tree removal, ultimately, reducing the threat of catastrophic wildfires in this area in cooperation with landowner objectives will result in ecological restoration, hazard reduction and range improvement.

ceqa-1889fc35a409ad9121.agency: California State Polytechnic University, San Luis Obispo
ceqa-1889fc35a409ad9121.agencyName: California State Polytechnic University, San Luis Obispo
ceqa-1889fc35a409ad9121.description: Cal Poly CCMS administers the Cal Poly Pier, which operates as a marine research and educational facility. The Cal Poly Pier and surrounding waters have been approved to be a part of the U.S. Department of Energy’s Testing Expertise and Access for Marine Energy Research (TEAMER) facility network as an open water test site. The Cal Poly Pier xNode Deployment Project is a 3-month sea trial of a small submergible, buoy scale, ocean wave energy converter at the Cal Poly Pier testing facility. The xNode technology converts ocean wave energy into electric power and data connectivity, offering a low impact solution for offshore operations. The project will help collect data in real ocean environment conditions and evaluate the feasibility of using wave energy systems to provide persistent, low-emission power for oceanographic monitoring, scientific research, remote sensing, communications, and other offshore applications. Development of the xNode is sponsored by the U.S. Department of the Navy and TEAMER. The sea trial is proposed by Cal Poly CCMS in partnership with Dolphin Labs. The project total duration could be for up to a 6 months, including deployment, 3-month open water testing, and decommissioning.

ceqa-de043f2b5ef0792198.projectTitle: CITY OF ATASCADERO COMPREHENSIVE 2045 GENERAL PLAN UPDATE AND ZONING CODE UPDATE
ceqa-de043f2b5ef0792198.description: The project involves a comprehensive update to the City’s current 2025 General Plan, which was adopted in 2002 and most recently amended in 2020 (City of Atascadero 2016 to reflect a 2045 horizon year (2045 General Plan Update). The project also includes updates to the Atascadero Municipal Code to ensure consistency with the 2045 General Plan Update, to clarify existing administrative standards and practices, and incorporate current City policy (Zoning Code Update). Chapter 2, Project Description, of the Environmental Impact Report (EIR) provides an overview of the Planning Area location and setting as well as the background, objectives, land use components, policies, and required approvals of the 2045 General Plan Update and Zoning Code Update (referred to herein collectively as the Project or the 2045 General Plan/Zoning Code Update) This Draft EIR evaluates the physical changes associated with community buildout anticipated to occur under the 2045 General Plan Update and Zoning Code Update, if adopted, as well as the physical effects that may result from the establishment and implementation of the goals and policies of the project. The 2045 General Plan Update would be comprehensive and internally consistent, serving as the City’s top-level planning document to guide the City’s future growth and development. The overall role of the 2045 General Plan Update is to: • Define a realistic community vision for Atascadero through the year 2045. • Provide the legal foundation for local government decision-making. This includes but is not limited to zoning regulations, ordinances, guidelines, standards, other adopted Citywide plans, compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) decisions and projects, all of which must be consistent with the General Plan. • Express policy direction in regard to the physical, social, economic, cultural, and environmental character of the city. • Serve as a comprehensive guide for making decisions regulating land use, circulation, environmental management, parks and recreation, housing, noise, public health, and safety. • Provide citizens the opportunity to participate in the planning and decision-making process of their community; and • Inform citizens, developers, decision-makers, and other cities and counties of the ground rules that guide development within a particular community. General Plan Elements. According to State law, General Plans are required to cover nine topics: land use, circulation, housing, conservation, open space, noise, air quality, safety, and environmental justice (note: including environmental justice is only required when a city has a State-identified disadvantaged community, which Atascadero does not). Jurisdictions may include any other topics that are relevant to planning its future and may address the required topics in conjunction with these other topics. The 2045 General Plan Update would include the following elements: • Land Use and Community Form Element • Economic Development Element • Mobility Element • Recreation and Open Space Element • Public Services and Infrastructure Element • Safety and Emergency Preparedness Element The City of Atascadero Housing Element was adopted in 2020 and is valid until 2028. It will not be part of this current update process. Updates to the Zoning Code are made by the General Plan. Land Use Element: Place Types and corresponding Zoning Districts. The Land Use and Community Form Element would fulfill the State requirements for the Land Use Element and identifies policies to preserve and foster community character when exploring opportunities for growth. The 2045 General Plan Update would include a combination of new and refined land uses and updated land use designations referred to as “Placetypes.” Placetypes intend to create more clarity around the character of new development. Placetypes are similar to land use designations, as they set densities and intensities, but also include detail on the character of the various types of uses, including scale, design quality, and relationship to the street. Placetypes would be further refined by zoning districts, which provide more detailed distinction of allowed uses and development standards within each Placetype established in the 2045 General Plan Update. Zoning Code Update. Final adoption of Zoning Code standards will follow adoption of the General Plan. The Zoning Code Update focuses on reorganization of Title 9 for readability and accessibility while incorporating new zoning districts to correspond to updated General Plan Placetypes, as well as codification of current City policies. The Zoning Code Update will also include changes to zoning code administration and entitlement processing to correspond to current best practice, current policy, State law, and/or to meet the Council’s streamlining and public outreach goals, as well as updated definitions and development standards to acknowledge new uses and economic trends and implement the General Plan vision for each Placetype. Potential Environmental Effects: Significant environmental effects are anticipated related to air quality, greenhouse gases, and transportation. Descriptions of specific impacts and associated mitigation are provided in the EIR.

ceqa-d650d6ffbf59552cfc.name: Pismo State Beach Golf Course Pollinator Plants
ceqa-d650d6ffbf59552cfc.projectTitle: Pismo State Beach Golf Course Pollinator Plants
ceqa-d650d6ffbf59552cfc.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-d650d6ffbf59552cfc.description: The Pismo State Beach Golf Course within Pismo State Beach (PSB) is operated by a concessionaire agreement through the Oceano Dunes District (ODD). ODD in partnership with the golf course manager proposes to restore and enhance approximately 1/4-acre patch of non-native iceplant (Carpobrotus edulis) and Kikuyu grass (Cenchrus clandestinus) into native nectar habitat for pollinator species. Planting native nectar-rich flowering plants will help provide critical food resources for declining pollinator species such as the monarch butterfly which overwinters at the nearby PSB Monarch Grove. Because golf courses occupy expansive, contiguous parcels of open land, converting out-of-play roughs into native habitats can offer significant environmental value to pollinator species. Additionally, out-of-play areas converted to native plants will require less mowing and irrigation compared to the adjacent managed fairways and greens. The Project includes the following restoration activities: •Removal of invasive plant species with manual, mechanical, and targeted herbicide application methods. •Collection of seeds from locally native dune-specialized species, including, but not limited to dune ragwort (Senecio blochmaniae), California aster (Corethrogyne filaginifolia), Scarlet bugler (Penstemon syntragitholias), Cardinal catchfly (Silene laciniata), and pink sand-verbena (Abronia umbellate). •Installation of interpretive signage and fencing around the project area. This “demonstration garden” will not only be visited by golf course players but the general public will be allowed to visit as well. Anticipated project implementation: The native plants will be grown in the fall of 2026 and planted at the golf course in the spring of 2027.

ceqa-00975525e49261929b.name: Eagle Ranch Vegetation Management EPP
ceqa-00975525e49261929b.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ceqa-00975525e49261929b.agencyName: Forestry and Fire Protection, Department of
ceqa-00975525e49261929b.description: The Eagle Ranch project will create a mosaic of mixed age class vegetation in a Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone (FHSZ) area with rural ranch sites, adjacent to the more densely populated community of Atascadero, by reducing high fuel loading and breaking up fuel continuity. The operational area is broken into three independent treatment units for a total of 250 acres. Primary treatment will be dozer crushing/mastication in chamise chaparral with broadcast burning of the slash within crushed areas along with adjacent areas where fuels and topography are suitable for prescribed burning. Mastication and additional hand crew work will be conducted in areas planned for broadcast burning in order to strengthen control lines and mow ladder fuels around trees and mature shrubs. CAL FIRE will also conduct thinning of grey pine. Retention of native oaks, except for very limited hazardous trees, is a project goal. CAL FIRE Hand crew will be used along the existing access roads to trim oak trees to improve the access/evacuation route; and as needed in equipment exclusion zones. Treatment activities include dozer crushing, fire control line construction, prescribed burning, hand crew thinning, chipping, pile burning, pruning, hazard tree removal, and mechanical mastication. Ultimately, reducing the threat of catastrophic wildfires in this area in cooperation with landowner objectives will result in ecological restoration, hazard reduction and range improvement.

ceqa-9727a3b74700030f29.name: Pismo Clarkia Habitat Enhancement and Management Study (Project)
ceqa-9727a3b74700030f29.projectTitle: Pismo Clarkia Habitat Enhancement and Management Study (Project)
ceqa-9727a3b74700030f29.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Central Region 4
ceqa-9727a3b74700030f29.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 4 - Central, Fresno
ceqa-9727a3b74700030f29.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife is issuing a Native Plant Protection Act scientific, educational, or management permit pursuant to California Code of Regulations, Title 14, section 786.9, subdivision (c) to The Land Conservancy of San Luis Obispo County (Permit No. 2081(a)-26-009-RP) for a project to improve the viability and long-term resiliency of Pismo clarkia (Clarkia speciosa ssp. immaculata) by continuing research and implementing habitat management to enhance the population on the Pismo Preserve. The Project builds on an effort that began in 2021 that established eight research sites approximately 9.3 square meters in size and documented a positive response of Pismo clarkia to grazing by reducing competition from nonnative annual grasses. The Project will implement seasonally appropriate rotational cattle grazing across an approximately 70 acre grass and oak woodland area that includes the eight established research sites. Virtual fencing that uses GPS enabled livestock collars and digitally established boundaries to manage cattle distribution will be used across the broader pasture. Once Pismo clarkia germinates, physical exclusion fencing will be installed to prevent cattle around the eight occupied research sites. Seed collection may also occur annually during July from Pismo clarkia populations on the Pismo Preserve and from nearby CNDDB EOs 2 and 5 for the purpose of broadcasting to enhance the existing population. Collection will be limited to less than 10 percent of the fruiting population. Supplemental seed sowing is expected to begin in 2027 and will typically occur in mid- to late December before a forecasted large rain event. Seed will be mixed with clean sand, broadcast by hand, and lightly raked into the soil within the 10-acre expansion zone identified as suitable Pismo clarkia habitat. Additional habitat management may include hand weeding, string trimming, and targeted herbicide treatment within research sites. Pre-treatment surveys will be conducted and any Pismo clarkia plants identified will receive a no-herbicide buffer of at least 15 feet but typically 25 feet. Only hand weeding will occur within these buffers. LCSLO will conduct approximately six census surveys each spring at the eight research sites. Treatment and monitoring data will be analyzed to evaluate grazing and weed management effects.

ceqa-157736d26817b300bc.name: Replacement of Energy Dissipating Valve Hydraulic Piping Project

ceqa-c5b2076ae1cf8fa2b9.name: Cal Poly Pond/Reservoir Maintenance
ceqa-c5b2076ae1cf8fa2b9.agency: California State Polytechnic University, San Luis Obispo
ceqa-c5b2076ae1cf8fa2b9.agencyName: California State Polytechnic University, San Luis Obispo
ceqa-c5b2076ae1cf8fa2b9.description: The project consists of routine maintenance and minor restoration at three existing campus agricultural water storage reservoirs: Indonesian Reservoir, Middlecamp Reservoir, and Drum Reservoir. Over time, sediment accumulation and dense emergent vegetation growth, primarily bulrush, have reduced water storage capacity and water quality and impaired existing reservoir infrastructure. Vegetation and sediment have obstructed overflow intake structures, clogged pump intakes, contributed to pump burnouts, and hindered routine inspections and maintenance. Project activities include selective removal of excess emergent vegetation and accumulated sediment; off-site transport and disposal of removed material at a licensed disposal facility; equipment staging for (refueling, stockpiling, and parking) outside aquatic resources, where feasible; and implementation of stormwater best management practices, including biodegradable straw wattles and native-species hydroseeding of disturbed banks. All work will occur within the existing reservoir footprints and associated infrastructure and will be conducted from reservoir banks using excavators. The project will not expand reservoir capacity, modify reservoir boundaries, remove trees, create new facilities or roadways, alter existing land uses, or increase operational capacity beyond existing conditions. The project does not involve expansion or creation of waters of the state. The reservoirs are existing managed water-storage facilities supporting campus agricultural pedagogy, including farms, gardens, and land laboratories used as living classrooms for hands-on, place-based learning. They also support campus flood-management resilience. Beneficiaries include campus students, faculty, agricultural programs, and the broader campus community. These activities will restore water storage volume, improve water quality, and enhance the reservoirs’ effectiveness for agricultural water supply and campus flood management. The reservoirs are also utilized by CAL FIRE for aerial wildfire-suppression support; by restoring reservoir function and reducing vegetation obstruction, the project will improve aerial access to available water resources.
ceqa-c5b2076ae1cf8fa2b9.crossStreets: Via Carta Road and Stenner Creek Road

ceqa-4f4b595c93c0062b75.name: AT&T Japan-U.S. Cable Network Decommissioning (JUS S8 and JUS S9 Cables) Project
ceqa-4f4b595c93c0062b75.projectTitle: AT&T Japan-U.S. Cable Network Decommissioning (JUS S8 and JUS S9 Cables) Project
ceqa-4f4b595c93c0062b75.description: The proposed Project would remove two fiber optic cable segments from the seafloor (JUS S8 and JUS S9) that are no longer in-service, and are offshore of San Luis Obispo and Mendocino Counties. The cables would be removed using a dive team to expose and cut the cables at the conduit exit points on the seafloor, and the cable would then be recovered by a cable recovery vessel (CRV) that would store and transport the cable for recycling. The conduit cable connected to the utility access point in Montaña de Oro State Park would also be cut by an onshore work crew and pulled from the conduit using a tugboat and later removed by the CRV. The conduit cables connected to the cable landing station in Manchester would remain inside the conduits. The Final MND contains revisions to Section 3.10 (Hazards and Hazardous Materials) and to Appendix F (Mitigation Monitoring Program).
ceqa-4f4b595c93c0062b75.crossStreets: SLO: Sandspit Road/Pecho Valley Road; Mendocino: Kinney Road/Biaggi Road
ceqa-4f4b595c93c0062b75.developmentType: Other (Removal of subsea fiber optic cable)

ceqa-795e02acbc42462fb4.description: The Department of Fish and Wildlife is issuing a permit to the California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo pursuant to Fish and Game Code Section 2081(a) for educational purposes. The Section 2081(a) permit authorizes the applicant to take coho salmon (Oncorhynchus kisutch) and Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha) during the course of sampling, subject to terms and conditions set forth in the permit. The purpose of this sampling is for the California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo’s permanent collections for educational classes. The Section 2081(a) permit authorizes the applicant to potentially capture coho salmon and Chinook salmon during surveys. The applicant will conduct year-round permanent collection sampling of nearshore and estuarine fishes, invertebrates, and zooplankton using hook & line – baited shrimp fly, hook & line – unbaited shrimp fly, beach seine, and fish trap through December 31, 2029.

ceqa-576fcb10757ad1cbbf.projectTitle: San Luis Obispo Creek at San Luis Bay Drive near Avila Beach Stream Gage Project No. 455R277613/ ED No. 26-0081
ceqa-576fcb10757ad1cbbf.description: As part of the California Stream Gage Improvement Program, the California Department of Water Resources has executed a contract with San Luis Obispo County Flood Control and Water Conservation District to install a stream gage on San Luis Obispo Creek at Avila Beach Drive. A radar stage sensor with a wire-weight reference gage will be installed over the creek on the Avila Beach Drive bridge railing to avoid drilling into or otherwise modifying the bridge structure. A pressure transducer and water temperature sensor will also be installed in the stream channel on the downstream side of the bridge crossing with conduit routed along the existing rock slope protection on the bank to an enclosure cabinet installed outside the channel. Installation of the enclosure cabinet will require minimal ground disturbance and will house the data logger and radio equipment. The equipment/conduit will be secured to the ground using drive pins and rock anchors. All work in the channel will be limited to the use of hand tools. Minor vegetation trimming may be required with no tree removal or alteration to the streambed or bank anticipated.

Additionally, the project proposes new improvements to the access road, return of evaporation pond back to a reservoir, extension of discharge line to San Simeon Creek, and a Zero Liquid Discharge facility. The WRF would operate up to 24 hours per day, 5 days per week, for 7 months per year, depending on precipitation. The project site is within the Agriculture land use category and is located at 990 San Simeon Creek Road, approximately 0.65 miles north of the Cambria Urban Reserve Line and 1.23 miles south of the San Simeon Urban Reserve Line. The site is in the North Coast Area Plan of the Coastal Zone. The proposed project is located within the Residential Single-Family land use category, accessed from Pasadena Drive (APN 038-733-012), within the community of Los Osos. The site is in the Estero Planning Area of the Coastal Zone. BACKGROUND On July 27, 2010, the Board of Supervisors (Board) authorized the preparation of the Los Osos Habitat Conservation Plan (LOHCP). On December 15, 2020, the Board certified the Final Environmental Impact Reports for the Los Osos Community Plan (LOCP) (SCH #2015031090) and the LOHCP (SCH #2013091071) in accordance with the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), including Public Resources Code Sections 21081 and 21082.1, and CEQA Guidelines Section 15090, which set forth the procedures and legal standards for preparation and certification of environmental impact reports. On February 15, 2024, the USFWS approved the LOHCP and issued the community-wide programmatic Incidental Take Permit (Permit No.: ESPER8245217) for a period of 25 years. As the permittee, the plan authorizes the County to issue Certificates of Inclusion that cover new disturbance via mitigation credit offsets and allowing for new development projects in Los Osos, as required by the Los Osos Community Plan (LOCP). On June 13, 2024, the California Coastal Commission certified Local Coastal Plan (LCP) Amendment Number LCP-3-SLO-21-0028-1-Part G. The Coastal Commission conditioned its certification by issuing a suggested modification to require that all development can only move forward with mandatory participation in the LOHCP and community-wide incidental taking permit approved by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, or equivalent mitigation. Staff presented the LOHCP implementation packet to the Board on December 10, 2024, which included actions necessary for LOHCP implementation, in which the Board approved the requested funding and staffing.

ceqa-e8d51cca8f9d637f8e.agencyName: Upper Salinas - Las Tablas Resource Conservation District (RCD)
ceqa-e8d51cca8f9d637f8e.description: The California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE) is providing funding to help implement vegetation treatments on State Responsibility Area (SRA) Lands in the North Coastal San Luis Obispo County. The Upper Salina-Las Tablas Resource Conservation District has prepared a Project Specific Analysis (PSA) and Addendum for the North Coastal San Luis Obispo County area covered by the California Vegetation Treatment Project (CalVTP) Program Environmental Impact Report (EIR) on July 8, 2025, which entails implementation of vegetation treatments on up to 88,151 acres; CAL FIRE is providing funding to the San Luis Obispo County Fire Safe Council, to implement treatments on up to 1,409 acres. The proposed treatment types are fuel break and ecological restoration. The proposed treatment activities consist of mechanical treatments, manual treatments, prescribed burning, herbicide application, and prescribed herbivory. Consistent with applicable Coastal Commission requirements, no ecological restoration or fuel break treatments will occur within chaparral or coastal sage scrub in the project area. Ongoing maintenance of initial treatments would involve the same vegetation types and activities used in the initial treatment, as funding other approvals allow. Treatment types and activities included in the proposed projects are consistent with those evaluated in the CalVTP.

ceqa-35ba127405c6c35be6.description: DWR is proposing to install soil sensor probes within 50 feet of the existing Black Mountain hydrometeorological station, located within the Los Padres National Forest. ceqa-aa015ad23778802bb8.projectTitle: Cambria Community Healthcare District - Minor Use Permit / Coastal Development Permit: C-DRC2025-00032 / ED26-0063
ceqa-aa015ad23778802bb8.description: A request by the Cambria Community Healthcare District for a Minor Use Permit / Coastal Development Permit (C-DRC2025-00032) to allow for the phased partial demolition and reconstruction of an ambulance station on the site of the existing facility, allowing administrative and crew functions to remain operational during construction. The ambulance bay will accommodate four emergency vehicles with direct access to Main Street for emergency response, and on-site staffing is anticipated to include approximately seven employees and responders. Phase 2 will include demolition of remaining existing facilities and associated site improvements consisting of landscaping, return driveway, public and staff parking, installation of an emergency generator and support appurtenances. The project is in the Public Facilities land use category, located at 2515 Main Street in the Community of Cambria. The project is in the North Coast Planning Area of the Coastal Zone.

ceqa-801bb6538e40f96100.name: Camp San Luis Obispo – Real Property Lease — Routine and Recurring Use of Training Infrastructure, Facilities, and Grounds

ceqa-9205748a231fc80cac.name: Harbor Terrace Water Tank - C-DRC2025-00022
ceqa-9205748a231fc80cac.projectTitle: Port San Luis Harbor Terrace Development Plan
ceqa-9205748a231fc80cac.description: A request by Tim Kihm with Redtail Acquisitions for a Minor Use Permit, Variance, and Coastal Development Permit (C-DRC2025-00022) to allow a new 53,000-gallon storage tank to supplement the existing water supply for Port San Luis Harbor District, as required under conditions of approval for DRC2013-00044 for the site formerly known as Harbor Terrace, now Flying Flags RV Resort and Camping facility located at 6450 Babe Lane in Avila. Redtail Acquisitions is the applicant, site lessee, developer and manager of the RV park and campground; Port San Luis Harbor District is the landowner and lessor. The project includes preparing a new tank pad and tank installation at the existing water storage facility site (located uphill from the RV campground), widening the 400-foot access road which ranges from 15%-23.8% gradient, addressing drainage conveyance, installing a new 12" storm drain line within the access road, and applying a gravel overlay extending from the tank site to the unfinished upper terrace of the campground development. The supplemental water tank installation will enable completion of the RV facility’s final buildout. Total project grading is approximately 1,756 cubic yards of cut and fill earthwork, and total disturbance is approximately 30,924 square feet. The grading requires findings for Adjustment under 23.05.034(3) for 373 cubic yards of impacts to slopes between 20% and 30% gradient. Findings for a Variance are also requested under 23.01.045 for 474 cubic yards of earthwork on slopes in excess of 30%. The site is located within the Avila Beach Urban Reserve, within the San Luis Bay Coastal Planning Area.

ceqa-3cd75789a5bab037b3.name: Cuyama Well Waterline Repair and Re-Route
ceqa-3cd75789a5bab037b3.projectTitle: Cuyama Well Waterline Repair and Re-Route
ceqa-3cd75789a5bab037b3.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Central Region 4
ceqa-3cd75789a5bab037b3.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 4 - Central, Fresno
ceqa-3cd75789a5bab037b3.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife plans to reroute a broken waterline that runs from State land through private property. The segment of the waterline located on private land will be abandoned in place. Approximately 3,600 feet of new water line will be installed. The new alignment will be constructed entirely on State lands. Installation will occur through trenching and/or jacking and boring. The project will require boring beneath State Route 166 and excavating bore pits along an existing dirt road. The new waterlines will connect to existing infrastructure that supplies a water cistern, wildlife pond, and wildlife troughs.

ceqa-e93da162a53862e7ae.name: Atascadero State Hospital Sewer Repairs
ceqa-e93da162a53862e7ae.description: The Department of State Hospitals (DSH) will complete repairs to four areas of the existing sewer system at Atascadero State Hospital. The current system has multiple failures and deteriorated components. The work includes removal and replacement of aging infrastructure, rerouting of sewer lines, point repairs, and cured in place pipe lining. The four areas of work are: Area 1 - Replacement of grease interceptor. Area 2 - Trench and install new 6" sewer line; abandon old sewer line in place. Area 3 - remove and replace section of sewer pipe that has been fractured by metal rod. Area 4 - Installation of Cured-In-Place Pipe lining for approximately 983 lin. ft. of 6" sewer main.

ceqa-a355e1e22dd24a5fc3.name: San Luis Obispo County Parks, Environmental Determination ED26-0116
ceqa-a355e1e22dd24a5fc3.projectTitle: San Luis Obispo County Parks, Environmental Determination ED26-0116
ceqa-a355e1e22dd24a5fc3.description: A request by the County of San Luis Obispo Department of Parks and Recreation to continue implementation of the Lopez Lake Quagga Mussel Prevention Public Outreach Plan at Lopez Lake Recreation Area. The project includes continued operation of a Resource Protection Team, consisting of a WIT 1-certified Resource Protection Inspector and K9 Team, to conduct primary and secondary watercraft inspections for quagga mussels and veligers (larvae); continued plankton tow sampling and substrate monitoring in coordination with the County Department of Public Works for early detection of quagga mussels; and continued public education and outreach at the California Mid-State Fair through an interactive booth staffed by a Park Ranger and K9 Team, including educational activities, boater surveys, and quizzes to assess public awareness and program effectiveness. Project activities are limited to watercraft inspections, environmental monitoring, and public outreach and education. The project involves no ground disturbance, grading, grubbing, vegetation removal, or other physical modifications to the environment. The project is within the Recreation land use category and is located at Lopez Lake Recreation Area, 6800 Lopez Drive, approximately 10 miles east of the community of Arroyo Grande, in the Huasna-Lopez Sub Area of the South County Planning Area.

ceqa-8c6ddc473605ad463e.name: San Luis Obispo County Parks, Environmental Determination ED26-0105
ceqa-8c6ddc473605ad463e.projectTitle: San Luis Obispo County Parks, Environmental Determination ED26-0105
ceqa-8c6ddc473605ad463e.description: A request by San Luis Obispo County Parks, Central Coast State Parks Association and Xerces to repair existing irrigation at Monarch Grove including replacing the irrigation controller, fix or replace drip lines, T-pipes and sprinklers. All work will be completed with hand tools. This project will disturb less than 100 square feet and there will be no grading, grubbing, or tree limbing. This effort is based on the recommendations from the Monarch Lane Habitat Assessment to enhance Monarch butterfly habitat. This repair will be completed before the arrival of the Monarch butterflies. The project is within the Open Space land use category and is located at Monarch Lane, Los Osos, CA 93402 in the Estero Planning Area of the Coastal Zone.

ceqa-18844fcf5856afc468.name: Arroyo Grande General Plan
ceqa-18844fcf5856afc468.description: As part of a comprehensive planning process, the City of Arroyo Grande (City) proposes to adopt an updated Arroyo Grande General Plan. The General Plan Update would serve as a long-term framework for future growth, reflect issues identified from community input and changes in State law, and update all elements of the General Plan, including the Land Use Element, Natural and Cultural Resources Element, Safety Element, Noise Element, Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Element, Circulation Element, Economic Development Element, and Health and Equity Element. The General Plan Update would include, but is not limited to, revisions to policies, narratives, data, and figures to reflect the new buildout period through 2050. The General Plan Update would also identify specific areas--referred to as Focus Areas, including the East Grand Corridor, North Fair Oaks, Frederick--as having the potential to accommodate growth and development through 2050. The General Plan Update would also include updates to the existing noise contours and an update to the City's 2013 Climate Action Plan. The Development Code would also be amended in concurrence with the General Plan Update to ensure consistency with the Arroyo Grande General Plan.

ceqa-5447e4ee318c834acb.name: Vesting Tentative Parcel Map (N-SUB2025-00061/ CO25-0044)
ceqa-5447e4ee318c834acb.description: Hearing to consider a request by Monarch Village Nipomo, LLC for a mixed-use project consisting of Phased Vesting Tentative Parcel Map (N-SUB2025-00061 /CO 25-0044) to subdivide and reconfigure three existing parcels totaling 2.54 acres into ten parcels ranging from 11,525 sq. ft. to 27,085 sq. ft., including eight vertically configured airspace parcels consisting of four ground-floor commercial airspace parcels containing commercial condominium units and common areas, and four corresponding second story residential airspace parcels containing residential condominium units, and a Conditional Use Permit for site development that includes two commercial retail buildings and four mixed-use commercial/residential buildings containing 28,259 sq. ft. of commercial space, 40 second-floor two-bedroom condominiums and support areas (e.g. circulation, storage, electrical, etc.) totaling 96,019 sq. ft. of total floor area, along with associated grading and drainage improvements, on-site utilities and circulation, parking, and common area landscaping. The project includes on and off-site parking. The project will result in the disturbance of approximately 3.82 acres of the 4.6 acre site (which includes three off site parcels). The site is located within the Commercial Retail, and the Recreation-Resort land use categories and is located in the center of Monarch Dunes Village bounded by the following streets: Center Point Place, Trilogy Parkway, and Via Concha across from the Monarch Club at Trilogy. The site is located approximately 0.52 miles east of Highway 1 and 4.12 miles west of Highway 101. The project site is located within the Village of Monarch Dunes within the South County Sub Area of the South County Planning Area.

ceqa-92388ddef1577be71e.name: U.S. 101 Paso Robles Barrier Project Barrier Separation to Adjacent System
ceqa-92388ddef1577be71e.projectTitle: U.S. 101 Paso Robles Barrier Project Barrier Separation to Adjacent System
ceqa-92388ddef1577be71e.agencyName: Caltrans, District 5 - San Luis Obispo/Santa Barbara
ceqa-92388ddef1577be71e.description: The project is located in San Luis Obispo County on State Route 101 in Paso Robles North of the SR 46 and US 101 North interchange. The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) proposes to install a positive barrier on the right side of the northbound (NB) freeway lanes on US101 in San Luis Obispo County (SLO), between Post Miles (PM) 54.33/54.82. This Safe System project is proposed to be funded from the State Highway Operation Protection Program (SHOPP) Minor A Proactive Safety – Collision Severity Reduction Program (201.015) in the 2026/27 fiscal year (FY). The proposed safety improvements include installing 500 linear feet of Midwest Guardrail System (MGS), and installing 2,100 linear feet of Type 60M concrete barrier with openings incorporated at the overside drains at PM 54.47 and 54.65. Additional improvements include installation of two gates at the existing right-of-way fence. All proposed work will be done within the existing Caltrans right-of-way.

ceqa-ab478f72911bd48c7a.name: Cal Poly Pier TEAMER Wave Measurement Project
ceqa-ab478f72911bd48c7a.projectTitle: Cal Poly Pier TEAMER Wave Measurement Project
ceqa-ab478f72911bd48c7a.agency: California State Polytechnic University, San Luis Obispo
ceqa-ab478f72911bd48c7a.agencyName: California State Polytechnic University, San Luis Obispo
ceqa-ab478f72911bd48c7a.description: Facilities Planning and Capital Projects at the Califorina Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo, is lead agency carring out the project. Caifornia Polytechnic State University (Cal Poly) CCMS administers the Cal Poly Pier, which operates as a marine research and educational facility. The Cal Poly Pier and surrounding waters have been approved to be a part of the U.S. Department of Energy’s Testing Expertise and Access for Marine Energy Research (TEAMER) facility network as an open water test site. The Cal Poly Pier Wave Measurement Project consists of the deployment of a wave measurement buoy to measure existing wave conditions at the Cal Poly Pier testing facility. The deployed buoy measures vertical wave movement. In addition to wave measurements, the buoy transmits information through HF radio link on sea surface temperature, GPS coordinates, and battery life. Data collected on the Waverider follows a long-utilized and reliable path to public access.
ceqa-ab478f72911bd48c7a.crossStreets: Avila Beach Drive & Cal Poly Pier

ceqa-a946b7efc08c096b92.name: Cerro Alto Ranch Headcut Repair (Request No. 1652-2026-096-001-R4)
ceqa-a946b7efc08c096b92.projectTitle: Cerro Alto Ranch Headcut Repair (Request No. 1652-2026-096-001-R4)
ceqa-a946b7efc08c096b92.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Central Region 4
ceqa-a946b7efc08c096b92.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 4 - Central, Fresno
ceqa-a946b7efc08c096b92.description: Pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 1652, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife has approved the Cerro Alto Ranch Headcut Repair Project as submitted by the Coastal San Luis Resource Conservation District as represented by Hayley Barnes. The 950 square-foot Project will stabilize an existing headcut to curb erosion within the unnamed tributary and abate sedimentation into Warden Creek. Specifically, the Project includes the grading of the headcut, installation of a rock grade control structure, and revegetation of the disturbed area with a native seed mix. A total of 43 linear feet of stream will be affected by the Project. The Project does not include the removal of mature trees or shrubs, and Project activities will be conducted when the stream is dry. California red-legged frog (Rana draytonii) and south-central California coast steelhead (Oncorhynchus mykiss) are expected to benefit from the water quality improvements the Project will provide to the receiving watershed. Monarch butterfly (Danaus plexippus plexippus) and Crotch’s bumble bee (Bombus crotchii) are expected to benefit from the enhanced foraging opportunities provided by the Project’s seed mix, which will establish floristic species with bloom periods throughout the year.

ceqa-ec53b80d25b48e0a8a.name: San Luis Obispo County Sheriffs Office - ALPR/Live Video Camera Installation - CEQA NOE
ceqa-ec53b80d25b48e0a8a.projectTitle: San Luis Obispo County Sheriffs Office - ALPR/Live Video Camera Installation - CEQA NOE
ceqa-ec53b80d25b48e0a8a.description: The project consists of the installation of Flock Safety automated license plate reading (ALPR) cameras on behalf of the San Luis Obispo County Sheriff's Office at multiple locations within public right-of-way. The project includes (1) mounting ALPR camera and solar equipment to existing traffic signal or streetlight poles at certain locations, and (2) installation of new breakaway support poles with small concrete foundations at other locations where existing infrastructure is not available. The purpose of the installation is to assist law enforcement in identifying vehicles associated with criminal activity. The beneficiaries of the project include law enforcement and the public at large, as the installation supports public safety objectives within the County of San Luis Obispo.

ceqa-b20e263e9171615a22.projectTitle: San Luis Obispo/Santa Barbara Centerline and Edgeline Rumble Strips
ceqa-b20e263e9171615a22.agencyName: Caltrans, District 5 - San Luis Obispo/Santa Barbara

ceqa-d3ceaab8d13e293cd7.name: Leffingwell Boat Launch Repair Project
ceqa-d3ceaab8d13e293cd7.projectTitle: Leffingwell Boat Launch Repair – Geotech Investigation
ceqa-d3ceaab8d13e293cd7.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-d3ceaab8d13e293cd7.description: This project will repair the Leffingwell boat launch at Leffingwell Landing in Hearst Sam Simeon State Park to extend the life of an existing facility that provides water access to park visitors. The Launch is an approx. 14-ft wide concrete structure supported by native underlaying rock. Repairs to the Launch will be as follows: *Core through the existing concrete ramp to access three (3) known existing voids on the front side of the ramp. *Embed dowels (secured with an approved cementitious grout) into the concrete retaining wall adjacent to the boat ramp or rock to support the ramp during void repair. *Pump approx. 50 cubic yards of concrete into the voids and patch original core locations; and *Install expanded rock slope protection along the beach side profile of the ramp to protect the ramp from further erosion.

ceqa-e22ff366a25178d1b7.name: Ken-Mar Gardens, Halcyon Water System, Halcyon Estates, and Grande Mobile Manor Consolidation Project
ceqa-e22ff366a25178d1b7.projectTitle: Ken-Mar Gardens, Halcyon Water System, Halcyon Estates, and Grande Mobile Manor Consolidation Project
ceqa-e22ff366a25178d1b7.description: OCSD is a multi-service special district providing sewer collection and water services, solid waste, parks and recreation, and street lighting to residents and businesses in the communities of Oceano and Halcyon in San Luis Obispo County, California. This Draft Subsequent IS-MND describes the details of several additional improvements (“proposed modifications”) that have been identified as necessary to resolve potable water quality violations and concerns and bring the Ken-Mar Gardens, Halcyon, Halcyon Estates, and Grande Mobile Manor water systems back into compliance, which have resulted in new impact areas beyond those identified and evaluated in the adopted Final IS-MND for the Original Project. The proposed modifications evaluated in the Draft Subsequent IS-MND involve consolidating Ken-Mar Gardens Mobile Home Park, Halcyon Water System, Halcyon Estates, and Grande Mobile Manor into the OCSD system. Improvements would include installation of new pipelines, meters, valving, fire hydrants, and service laterals as well as removal and re-purposing of existing water system components. Construction of the proposed modifications is expected to begin as early as summer 2027 and would require approximately 12 months to complete.

ceqa-f54445cad94fd8e15c.name: Atascadero Creek Lake Fill Pipeline Repair Project
ceqa-f54445cad94fd8e15c.projectTitle: Atascadero Creek Lake Fill Pipeline Repair Project
ceqa-f54445cad94fd8e15c.description: The City of Atascadero owns a pipeline that carries water from Atascadero Creek to Atascadero Lake during high-flow events. Approximately 350 linear feet of that pipeline (beginning at the inlet) have degraded, become impacted with sediment, and require repair for the pipeline to function. The project involves a pipeline replacement and repair of the approximately 350-foot segment of the degraded pipeline and associated concrete hold-downs, and maintenance of existing intake structures and diversion boxes. The replacement pipeline will be of equivalent capacity in the same alignment as the existing pipe to restore functionality to the pipeline. The project will require approximately 96 cubic yards of excavation to remove the existing pipe and removal of riparian vegetation adjacent to and above the existing pipeline.

ceqa-61ef7de4eacb009494.name: Mahaffey Minor Use Permit N-DRC2024-00034 / ED25-0271
ceqa-61ef7de4eacb009494.description: Request by Patti Mahaffey for a Minor Use Permit (“MUP”) to authorize the use of existing facilities for the purpose of hosting of up to 35 temporary outdoor events per year with up to 200 attendees per event. Events would be held in two contiguous outdoor areas currently occupied by ornamental landscaping and walkways; temporary parking will be provided in two areas currently used to support equestrian activities. The total area to be repurposed for temporary events is about 1.7 acres. The project will not require any new grading or structures except for driveway improvements on Geneseo Road. Temporary water and sanitary facilities will be brought to the site for events. Outdoor amplified speech and music is also proposed. The project site is located about five miles east of the City of Paso Robles at 5750 Eagle Oak Ranch Way within the Agriculture land use category. The project site is in the El Pomar Estrella Sub Area of the North County Planning Area.

ceqa-f7abd55d5c5dbda43d.name: Cecchetti Road MP 0.218 Storm Repair Project (300711/ED26-0073)
ceqa-f7abd55d5c5dbda43d.projectTitle: Cecchetti Road MP 0.218 Storm Repair Project (300711/ED26-0073)
ceqa-f7abd55d5c5dbda43d.description: The proposed project involves the construction of a permanent replacement bridge to restore vehicular access to the Cecchetti Road crossing over Arroyo Grande Creek. The project includes restoring the crossing with a new open-bottom. single-span concrete bridge and reconstructing the adjacent roadway approaches. The project includes removal of the remaining portion of concrete roadway, installation of the new bridge structure, and raising the roadway profile to reduce the frequency of overtopping during future storm events. Associated improvements would include drainage and erosion control measures to enhance the crossing's resilience to hydraulic and geotechnical hazards. These upgrades are intended to improve roadway safety, reduce maintenance needs. support fish passage. and enhance the environmental performance of the crossing.

ceqa-72ad2ba9937e0bfd2a.name: AT&T Japan-U.S. Cable Network Decommissioning (JUS S8 and JUS S9 Cables) Project
ceqa-72ad2ba9937e0bfd2a.projectTitle: AT&T Japan-U.S. Cable Network Decommissioning (JUS S8 and JUS S9 Cables) Project
ceqa-72ad2ba9937e0bfd2a.description: The proposed Project would remove two fiber optic cable segments from the seafloor (JUS S8 and JUS S9) that are no longer in-service, and are offshore of San Luis Obispo and Mendocino Counties. The cables would be removed using a dive team to expose and cut the cables at the conduit exit points on the seafloor, and the cable would then be recovered by a cable recovery vessel (CRV) that would store and transport the cable for recycling. The conduit cable connected to the utility access point in Montaña de Oro State Park would also be cut by an onshore work crew and pulled from the conduit using a tugboat and later removed by the CRV. The conduit cables connected to the cable landing station in Manchester would remain inside the conduits. The State Lands Commission action is adoption of a Final Mitigated Negative Declaration, adoption of a Mitigation Monitoring Program, and issuance of two 10-year General Leases – Right-of-Way Use beginning July 1, 2026.

ceqa-55e6b96cd681dc6e98.name: Chorro Valley Access Road Repair Project. Project No. 300716/ ED26-0091
ceqa-55e6b96cd681dc6e98.projectTitle: Chorro Valley Access Road Repair Project. Project No. 300716/ ED26-0091
ceqa-55e6b96cd681dc6e98.description: The County of San Luis Obispo Flood Control and Water Conservation District is conducting the Chorro Valley Access Road Repair Project to stabilize an eroded section of Chorro Valley Access Road and to protect an adjacent buried water pipeline. Storm events in January 2023 eroded approximately 300 feet of embankment supporting the roadway, creating an unstable slope and increasing the risk of future damage to both the road and pipeline. The Project would construct a soldier pile retaining wall along the eroded roadway segment and include installation of a guardrail, repair of existing culverts, and roadway surface repairs. Construction is expected to take approximately three months. The project is not expected to alter habitat and is not within jurisdictional waterways.

ceqa-80fa3625c4fadfc8c6.name: Big Sandy Wildlife Area Grassland Restoration
ceqa-80fa3625c4fadfc8c6.projectTitle: Big Sandy Wildlife Area Grassland Restoration
ceqa-80fa3625c4fadfc8c6.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Central Region 4
ceqa-80fa3625c4fadfc8c6.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 4 - Central, Fresno
ceqa-80fa3625c4fadfc8c6.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife, with the assistance of Cal Fire and the California Conservation Corps plans to apply prescribed fire on approximately 350 acres of the Big Sandy Wildlife Area to achieve ecological restoration and enhancement goals and to reduce fuel loading to minimize wildfire risk. The prescribed burn area is the grasslands between Indian Valley Road and Highway 101. Tall fuels, comprised of yellow star thistle and other invasive weeds, will be cut and piled or crushed prior to burning to ensure combustion when necessary. Fire control lines will be created with and tie into existing features that function as fuel breaks, such as the existing roads.
ceqa-80fa3625c4fadfc8c6.crossStreets: Four miles northwest of San Miguel on the east side of Highway 101

ceqa-73ad26e078469056ac.name: San Luis Obispo Creek at San Luis Bay Drive near Avila Beach Stream Gage Project No. 455R277613/ ED No. 26-0081
ceqa-73ad26e078469056ac.projectTitle: San Luis Obispo Creek at San Luis Bay Drive near Avila Beach Stream Gage Project No. 455R277613/ ED No. 26-0081
ceqa-73ad26e078469056ac.description: The proposed project involves the installation of a stream gage along San Luis Obispo Creek near Avila Beach in San Luis Obispo County. The stream gage will include both bridge-mounted and bank-mounted components on and in the immediate vicinity of San Luis Bay Drive Bridge No. 3. A non-contact radar stage sensor and a co-located small wire-weight reference gage will be installed on the existing bridge structure. Bridge-mounted components will be secured to the bridge railing to avoid drilling into or otherwise modifying the bridge. The bank-mounted installation will consist of a gage shelter located along the top of the left (south) bank of San Luis Obispo Creek, near the northwestern corner of the intersection of San Luis Bay Drive and Avila Beach Drive. Additional equipment will include a pressure transducer and a water temperature sensor, which will be routed along existing rock slope protection on the bank and placed within the creek bed. The equipment will be secured using drive pins and rock anchors. In-channel work is expected to be completed using hand tools. Limited excavation above the ordinary high-water mark is proposed, along with minor vegetation trimming. No tree removal or habitat alteration is proposed as part of the project. Vehicle parking and staging of supplies and equipment will occur within previously disturbed areas or on existing paved surfaces.

ceqa-b7751ac3b43209844a.name: Issue a Right of Entry Permit to Verizon for Fiberoptic Conduit Repair Project
ceqa-b7751ac3b43209844a.projectTitle: Issue a Right of Entry Permit to Verizon for Fiberoptic Conduit Repair Project
ceqa-b7751ac3b43209844a.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-b7751ac3b43209844a.description: The project will repair and replace the existing articulated steel conduit connecting a horizontal directionally drilled (HDD) pipe to a Verizon manhole in the sandspit beach parking lot at Montaña de Oro State Park and will issue a Right of Entry permit to the contractor to perform the work. This activity is expected to last 14 days, during which time construction work zone will be fenced off from the public. Work will: - Locate existing telecommunication utilities by potholing; - Saw cut to remove asphalt surface over the ducts; - Reinforce and shore-up soils around the end of the existing HDD pipe with steel beams to create a secured access point 8-ft long x 4-ft wide x 6-ft deep; - Dig using an excavator, except within 5 feet of any working fiber, which then shall be dug by hand. - Detach and remove the existing articulated steel pipe for disposal; - Seal and cap end of the HDD pipe; - Install a 1-4-in. inside diameter schedule 40 PVC conduit at a typical depth of 4-ft from the beach manhole wall and stub at the wall of the shoring plates; - Backfill and compact soils around duct, compacting in 6-in. lifts with appropriate fill material; - Cover the 8-ft x 4ft x 6-ft secured access point with a 10-ft long x 6-ft wide x 1.25-in. thick steel plate, flush mounted to the existing asphalt elevation; and - When future cable is installed, the steel plate will be removed and secured access point will be restored to prior conditions with asphalt.

ceqa-8fa8b63d1fac5a481a.name: Water Treatment Plant Access Road/Asphalt Maintenance
ceqa-8fa8b63d1fac5a481a.projectTitle: Water Treatment Plant Access Road/Asphalt Maintenance
ceqa-8fa8b63d1fac5a481a.description: The Central Coast Water Authority (CCWA) is a joint powers agency formed to construct, own, and operate certain facilities needed to treat, convey, and deliver State Water Project (SWP) water to its project participants retail water providers and end users located within the County. The Polonio Pass Water Treatment Plant (WTP) is one of CCWA's facilities and stores treatment chemicals in chemical tanks. The pavement of the WTP access road is constantly exposed to the elements and traffic loading. This results in a wearing of the pavement surface and the oxidation of the pavement materials. Cracks will form, which will allow water to penetrate beneath the pavement and this creates an accelerated degradation process. Through crack sealing and slurry sealing, the service life of the pavement will be greatly extended, which postpones full reconstruction. CCWA intends to repair the WTP access road.

ceqa-5e766e221e0d19f904.name: Filter Multimedia and Underdrain Nozzle Replacement Project
ceqa-5e766e221e0d19f904.projectTitle: Filter Multimedia and Underdrain Nozzle Replacement Project
ceqa-5e766e221e0d19f904.description: The Central Coast Water Authority (CCWA) is a joint powers agency formed to construct, own, and operate certain facilities needed to treat, convey, and deliver State Water Project (SWP) water to its project participants retail water providers and end users located within the County. The Polonia Pass Water Treatment Plant (WTP) is one of CCWA's facilities and stores treatment chemicals in chemical tanks. The condition of the multimedia filters at the WTP is a high priority due to their critical role in the treatment process and regulatory compliance. Proper filter performance is essential to prevent clogging, excessive head loss, and inefficient backwash cycles, all of which can adversely affect WTP operations. Filtration of settled water is a core component of overall treatment capacity and is achieved through eight multimedia filters, within the system. Water percolates from the top of each filter through a layer of granular activated carbon and sand and flows through an underdrain system to the chlorine contact basin. CCWA intends to remove and replace both layers of filter media and the underdrain nozzles in four of the filters, repairing filter basin concrete surfaces, and leveling backwash troughs to extent feasible.

ceqa-9a84c5c4fea150289e.agency: Coastal San Luis Resource Conservation District
ceqa-9a84c5c4fea150289e.agencyName: Coastal San Luis Resource Conservation District
ceqa-9a84c5c4fea150289e.description: The project is to implement management practices (MPs), including headcut repair and associated streambank stabilization measures, to reduce sediment and nutrient loading to Chorro Creek and support implementation of the Los Osos Creek, Warden Creek, and Warden Lake Wetland Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL). Treatments at Tomorro Farm will use low-tech, process-based restoration (LTPBR) techniques to stabilize headcuts and restore natural hydrologic function. These treatments may include Small Habitat Restoration Projects, less than five acres, that ensure a positive impact for fish, plants, or wildlife (as eligible for an exemption listed below), such as beaver dam analogs (BDAs), native streambank and upland revegetation, and temporary cattle exclusion fencing to support vegetation establishment and protect restored areas. In addition to reducing sedimentation and nutrient loading, project benefits include enhanced wildlife habitat, improved soil health, and increased groundwater recharge.

ceqa-627cec6d8306480195.name: Pismo Beach General Plan/Local Coastal Plan (GP/LCP) Update
ceqa-627cec6d8306480195.projectTitle: Pismo Beach General Plan/Local Coastal Plan Update Recirculated EIR
ceqa-627cec6d8306480195.description: The Draft EIR for the Pismo Beach General Plan/Coastal Land Use Plan (GP/LCP) Update was circulated for a 45-day public review period that began on February 1, 2022 and ended on March 18, 2022. Following the end of the public review period for the Draft EIR, the City prepared an Administrative Draft Final EIR. In addition to addressing public comments, the Administrative Draft Final EIR reflected removal of the Facilities Element from the GP/LCP Update and incorporation of Facilities Element policies into other elements. The Planning Commission hearings for the Final EIR were held on July 25 and August 22, 2023. The City Council hearing for the Final EIR was scheduled for October 2023. However, prior to the City Council hearing, the City determined that the Safey Element would also be removed from the GP/LCP Update. In accordance with Public Resources Code Section 21092.1 and California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Section 15088.5, the City of Pismo Beach (City) has elected to recirculate a portion of the Pismo Beach General Plan/Local Coastal Plan Update (GP/LCP Update) Draft Program Environmental Impact Report (SCH #2021010158). The changes disclosed within this Recirculated Draft EIR are made to address changes that have occurred following the closure of the 45-day public review period of the Draft EIR in March 2022, including: (1) the removal of the Facilities Element and incorporation of Facilities Element policies into other elements, (2) the removal of the Safety Element from the GP/LCP Update, and (3) changes to the GP/LCP Update, including to the goals, policies, and actions within the GP/LCP Update. The changes to the policies and actions within the GP/LCP Update are primarily changes made to their numbering and lettering as a result of the reordering of policies and actions within the GP/LCP Update to more clearly define which policies and actions are applicable to the Local Coastal Program. These changes also include minor language changes to specific goals, policies, and actions within the GP/LCP. In addition, these changes include the addition of new goals, policies, and actions added to the Conservation and Open Space Element as a result of Senate Bill 1425 and the addition of new goals, policies, and actions added to the Circulation Element as a result of the reorganization of the GP/LCP Update. Language changes to existing policies and additional goals, policies, and actions within the GP/LCP are intended to provide a similar, and in some cases enhanced, level of environmental protection as the goals, policies, and actions within the GP/LCP Update at the time of the release of the Draft EIR. Accordingly, the changes to the goals, policies, and actions do not result in new or substantially more severe environmental impacts than what was evaluated within the Draft EIR. The project analyzed is the proposed City of Pismo Beach GP/LCP Update, which includes updates to the Land Use, Conservation and Open Space, Noise, and Circulation Elements of the City’s 1992 GP/LCP. The GP/LCP Update does not include updates to the Parks, Recreation, and Access Element, Safety Element, and Housing Element. The Facilities Element is being eliminated and incorporated into other elements. The Design Element is being eliminated and incorporated into the Land Use Element. The Growth Management Element is being removed due to updates to California Housing Element Law and implementation of Senate Bill 330. With the GP/LCP Update, the City GP/LCP will consist of the following seven elements: 1) Circulation, 2) Conservation and Open Space, 3) Housing, 4) Land Use, 5) Noise, 6) Parks, Recreation, Access, and 7) Safety.
