The Project will provide approximately 108,000 square feet of office and conference room space, three classrooms with a training kitchen totaling 6,200 square feet, and approximately 35,000 square feet of warehouse space. All buildings on this portion of the site will be single-story in height. A stormwater ponding basin will be constructed along the southern boundary of the property for on-site drainage. Parking facilities surrounding the development will provide 388 parking stalls, including 17 accessible spaces. Vehicular access to the site will be provided from South Mooney Boulevard/SR 63 to the west and Avenue 264/Liberty Road to the south. The primary use of this facility will be to host professional development training and workshops for District employees.

ceqa-73eedbe8cd00934090.name: Grandview Gardens and East Plano Water Consolidation Project
ceqa-73eedbe8cd00934090.projectTitle: Grandview Gardens and East Plano Water Consolidation Project
ceqa-73eedbe8cd00934090.description: The project proposes to correct two failing water systems by installing water delivery infrastructure and connecting 97 existing homes to the City of Porterville's community water system. The project encompasses two physically separate areas: East Plano and Grandview Gardens. The East Plano component would begin at the existing City of Porterville 8” water main in E. Worth Avenue, installing approximately 600 feet of 8-inch PVC water main and 80 feet of 4-inch PVC water main in Paul Street heading south. It would include 14 1-inch water services, meters, and meter boxes, fire hydrants, and an appurtenant tie-in assembly plus elbows, tees, and valves. It would cut, cap, and abandon in place the existing water main (size unknown) in Paul Street and demolish the existing well station at the southern end of Paul Street. All existing water meters and meter boxes would be removed. Grandview Gardens currently has a temporary City water connection feeding the system. The Grandview Gardens component the project would install a total of approximately 3,320 feet of 8-inch PVC in S. Matson Avenue, N. Prospect Street, and W. Meril Avenue, W. Baker Street, and N. Westside Street and 25 feet of 6-inch PVC water main in N. Prospect Street. Tie-ins would be made to the existing 12-inch water main in W. North Grand Avenue and the existing 10-inch water main in W. Meril Avenue. The project would install 83 1-inch water services with meters and meter boxes. Of those, 19 would connect to the existing 10-inch water mains in W. Meril Avenue and N. Douglass Street. The remainder would connect to the new 8-inch and 6-inch water mains: 28 in N. Matson Street, 28 in N. Prospect Street, 3 in W. Baker Street, 2 in N. Westside Street, and 1 in W. Meril Avenue. The project also includes hydrants and appurtenant tie-in assemblies, elbows, tees, and valves. Existing 4-inch water mains throughout the project area would be cut, capped, and abandoned in place and the existing well station on the west side of S. Matson Street approximately 220 feet north of W. Grand Avenue would be demolished. Existing blow-offs throughout the project area would be removed.

These processes pertain to one (1) approximately 11.47-acre parcel located at the southwest corner of North Newcomb Street and West Linda Vista Avenue in Tulare County, CA (APN 243-130-042). The TSM proposes to subdivide the Project Site into 30 single-family lots (Lots 1 to 30), ranging from 10,762 square feet (sf.) to 17,011 sf., with an average lot size of 12,630 sf. Each lot is proposed to be developed with one unit (2.61 du/ac). The Project proposes an internal network of local streets with one (1) point of ingress/egress on N. Newcomb Street, one (1) point of ingress/egress on W. Linda Vista Avenue, and one (1) street stub to the south in the southwestern portion of the site. All roadways within the proposed subdivision would be designed in accordance with City standards and would have curb, gutter, and sidewalk. In addition, N. Newcomb Street and W. Linda Vista Avenue in proximity to the Project site would be improved to their ultimate rights-of-way, with curb, gutter, and sidewalk, in addition to landscaping. The Annexation would annex the one-parcel Project site from the County of Tulare into the City of Porterville.

ceqa-f92cf137e51d8817cb.name: MHDSF EPP
ceqa-f92cf137e51d8817cb.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ceqa-f92cf137e51d8817cb.agencyName: Forestry and Fire Protection, Department of
ceqa-f92cf137e51d8817cb.description: Mountain Home Demonstration State Forest is approximately 5,137 acres of public timberland 18 miles east of Springville, CA in Tulare County. The project area encompasses 538 acres of the State Forest in the Sierran mixed-conifer and associated brush timber types. The main tree species include white fir, incense-cedar, red fir, ponderosa pine, sugar pine, giant sequoia, and black oak. The understory is mainly of Ceanothus spp., hazel, elderberry, and cherry. The project area includes areas that were severely damaged by the 2020 SQF Complex, and there are numerous dying, dead, and down trees threatening public safety; as well as, creating a dangerous fuel load. Mechanical and manual cutting, pile and broadcast burning, and herbicide shall be used to complete the treatments. Some areas will receive tree planting following treatments to aid in forest rehabilitation

ceqa-4ae309a40a7dcd117f.name: Tulare 190 Emergency Landslide Repair
ceqa-4ae309a40a7dcd117f.description: This emergency project repaired the damaged roadway and drainage system that resulted from heavy rains that caused multiple landslides. Replaced failed pavement and culverts, rebuilt failed washouts, and added slope protection.

ceqa-f33a3e5cf62f445907.name: Yokohl Creek Recharge Project
ceqa-f33a3e5cf62f445907.description: The Proposed Project consists of the construction of a new concrete check structure in Yokohl Creek to increase the recharge capacity of the reach. The Proposed Project also includes a discharge structure along Yokohl Creek that will enable the delivery of surplus surface water to the creek for recharge purposes. The Proposed Project consists of the construction of concrete headwalls and support structure for water level control boards. The Proposed Project features will be located above grade within the stream bank of Yokohl Creek and maintain the current channel elevation. Construction activities will include concrete placement, control board installation, excavation, backfill, compaction and surface restoration efforts to complete the new structures.
ceqa-f33a3e5cf62f445907.developmentType: Other (Water Check Structure and Discharge Structure)

ceqa-2e69ee99d90f7f20fc.description: The proposed Project involves the development of 285 new residential units consisting of 209 single-family homes and 76 units of multi-family apartments on approximately 59.30 acres in the City of Tulare. The proposed General Plan designation is Residential Low Density with a portion of the Site designated as Medium Density Residential. The Project's proposed zoning is R-1-4 and RM (Medium Family Residential). The single-family lots will average 5,000 square feet (50' by 100') while the multi-family lots will average 12,075 square feet (69' x 175') with over 19 lots. The Project also includes a 2.76-acre park and storm drainage basin.

ceqa-cdd2d5b3c471e664f1.name: Three Rivers Creating a Wildfire Resistant and Resilient Community
ceqa-cdd2d5b3c471e664f1.projectTitle: Three Rivers Creating a Wildfire Resistant and Resilient Community
ceqa-cdd2d5b3c471e664f1.description: The Three Rivers Creating a Wildfire Resistant and Resilient Community Project (project) is a strategic, community-driven initiative designed to reduce wildfire risk and enhance public safety in and around the community of Three Rivers, Tulare County, California. This project directly supports the implementation of the Three Rivers Community Wildfire Protection Plan (CWPP), completed in fall 2022, which identified the urgent need for fuel management on both public and private lands within the wildland-urban interface (WUI). The project aligns with the National Cohesive Wildland Fire Management Strategy and advances the goal of developing Fire Adapted Communities (FAC). It was collaboratively developed with input from CAL FIRE’s Three Rivers Unit, Tulare County Fire, the Tulare County Resource Conservation District, the National Park Service, and numerous local residents and business owners. The primary purpose of the project is to reduce hazardous fuels near the community’s boundaries, thereby protecting lives, homes, critical infrastructure, and natural resources. The project builds upon the community’s successful Stage One efforts—focused on defensible space and home hardening education—and now moves into Stage Two—the creation of a strategic fuel break around the most densely populated and high-value areas of Three Rivers, including the Cherokee Oaks Subdivision and the Heidi Road and Old Three Rivers Road residential zones. The beneficiaries of the project include the residents, property owners, and business operators of Three Rivers, as well as critical infrastructure such as water storage systems, Southern California Edison (SCE) powerlines and repeaters, and the Three Rivers Community Cemetery. By reducing wildfire risk and enhancing community resilience, the project would protect not only physical assets but also the safety, well-being, and long-term sustainability of the Three Rivers community.

ceqa-499f25fb4fddb36ef6.name: London West Pond Project
ceqa-499f25fb4fddb36ef6.description: Project Description: The District proposes to develop an approximately 80-acre recharge facility known as the London West Pond located northwest of the community of London in Tulare County. The proposed Project would be situated immediately to the west of the existing London Pond recharge facility. The new 80-acre basin would consist of several cells and would connect to the existing Kennedy Schoolhouse Ditch pipeline. The pipeline would be replaced with an open ditch through the site. The proposed Project also includes a diversion, or spillway, on the east side of the property to allow for spill to the existing London Pond recharge facility. There are two existing wells on the Project site that would be available for use as recovery or monitoring wells. Construction: Construction of the recharge facility would be completed over approximately six months, with construction beginning in the spring of 2026. The Project site would be cleared of the existing stone fruit crops located in the northern and southern portions of the site. Construction equipment would likely include the following: • Excavators, • Bulldozers, • Skid steers, • Dump trucks, • Loaders, • Concrete pump truck, • Graders, and • Water truck. Post-construction activities would include system testing, commissioning, and site clean-up. Construction would require temporary staging and storage of materials and equipment. Staging areas would be located onsite. Operation and Maintenance: The District’s operation of the new recharge facility would be consistent with the District’s other similar facilities in that groundwater conditions would be monitored to minimize negative impacts on the surrounding areas (such as nearby wells, crops, and septic systems). Maintenance would be on an as needed basis.

ceqa-e4b23c2c90d3056caf.name: Paregien Basin Project
ceqa-e4b23c2c90d3056caf.description: The District plans to develop an approximately 50-acre recharge facility known as the Paregien Basin located directly south of Highway 198, northeast of the City of Farmersville. The new groundwater basin would include a new turnout connection from Deep Creek. The Project would also include approximately 350 feet of pipeline connecting the new turnout to the proposed basin. The pipeline connection from the proposed recharge basin to Deep Creek will be located on the south side of the existing West Pond, which is not a part of the Project. The area to the north and east of the existing pond will be avoided as it has been identified as a potentially sensitive habitat area. No Project activities will occur in this area. The proposed turnout would be developed with a capacity for approximately 20 cubic feet per second (CFS). The proposed turnout facility would consist of cast-in-place concrete structure, control gate(s), trash rack, and related appurtenances from the west bank of Deep Creek to divert to the proposed basin. The turnout structure would connect to an inlet pipeline approximately 350 linear feet (LF) from Deep Creek into the proposed Paregien Basin. The turnout structure would have a maximum excavation depth of 15 feet below ground surface for establishing proper compaction under the structure and pipeline. All excavation material would be balanced on site. Construction would include equipment mobilization, excavation of earthwork for the recharge basin and construction of basin perimeter berms. The Project site would contain temporary staging areas for construction equipment and material storage during the construction effort. Basin construction would include performance testing (i.e. compaction testing) and demobilization. Excavation material would be used on site for berm construction along the perimeter of the basin. New berm construction would not exceed six feet in height, measured from the exterior toe to the top of new berm. The maximum depth of ground disturbance for the basin would be as much as nine (9) feet. Through the improvements of this proposed multi-cell recharge basin, it is anticipated to recharge approximately 1,260 acre-feet (AF) on an average annual basis. However, the site is capable of recharging more in wet years when surplus water is available for longer durations. The 1,260 AF estimate is derived based on an estimated recharge rate of 0.5 AF per acre across the approximately 50 acres of wetted area for an estimated duration of 50 days, which is an approximate average of historical water availability on the Kaweah system. Typical surplus surface water availability is generally between March and June. However, in very wet years, water could be diverted for recharge whenever excess supply is available, which could occur from January to September or October.

ceqa-9d519176aedda572dd.name: Ordinance updates amending Chapter 15 of Part VII of the Tulare County Ordinance Code, pertaining to building regulations in Tulare County.
ceqa-9d519176aedda572dd.projectTitle: Ordinance updates amending Chapter 15 of Part VII of the Tulare County Ordinance Code, pertaining to building regulations in Tulare County.
ceqa-9d519176aedda572dd.description: The Resource Management Agency (RMA) and the Tulare County Fire Department have comprehensively updated Chapter 15 of Part VII of the Tulare County Ordinance Code regarding building regulations based upon the 2024 International Code Editions prepared by the California Building Standards Commission, state statutes, and local conditions. Chapter 15 of Part VII of the Tulare County Ordinance Code addresses building regulations in Tulare County. Through collaborative efforts by Tulare County Fire Department, County Counsel and RMA, Chapter 15 has been updated to reflect the new regulations in the California Building Standards Code. The references to the 2022 Building Standards Code have been replaced with language conforming to the 2025 Building Standards Code, which goes into effect at the beginning of 2025. This update will also include the new Article 33 Adoption of California Wildland Urban Interface Code, Title 24, Part 7; Significant increase to Section 320 Battery Storage: General Requirements & Entire Section additions; Section 1207 – Electrical Energy Storage Systems (ESS); Amendment for Sprinklered Mobile Homes and Premanufactured homes: Only those that have been manufactured after January 1, 2026, On private properties only, not applicable to mobile home parks; Appendix A-Employee Qualifications, of the California Building Codes; Appendix CJ- Emergency Housing and numerous text/verbiage changes throughout the codes as needed. The amendment to the Ordinance Code is on file at the Clerk of the Board’s Office, the RMA and the Tulare County Fire Chief Office and is available for public review during normal business hours.

ceqa-139bd788137a9fcb7a.name: Sanitary Sewer Master Plan
ceqa-139bd788137a9fcb7a.description: The Sanitary Sewer Master Plan is a comprehensive strategic framework designed to guide the sustainable development and management of the City of Visalia’s sanitary sewer collection system, located throughout the City’s General Plan Area. Its primary objective is to ensure the sewer collection system has adequate capacity to support the community growth as planned for in the Visalia 2030 General Plan. The Sanitary Sewer Master Plan assesses existing infrastructure and identifies necessary upgrades and expansions based on development anticipated pursuant to the General Plan and which was previously reviewed, considered, and subject to the Visalia 2030 General Plan EIR. By focusing on long-term planning and resource management, the Sanitary Sewer Master Plan aims to maintain high standards of environmental protection, public health, and operational reliability while accommodating the increased wastewater flow and community growth anticipated in the General Plan. The Sanitary Sewer Master Plan is for the purpose of planning potential projects that might be needed to accommodate the development called for under the General Plan. Prior to the authorization for construction of any project described in Sanitary Sewer Master Plan, each project will be separately reviewed to determine if there are specific significant effects which are peculiar to the project or its site.

ceqa-4e4bb05066a1446210.name: International Agri-Center Annexation and Master Plan
ceqa-4e4bb05066a1446210.projectTitle: International Agri-Center Annexation and Master Plan
ceqa-4e4bb05066a1446210.description: The annual World Ag Expo is the largest farm show in the world and attracts international attendees, as well as exhibitors. In 2019, this 3-day event attracted 106,357 attendees and 1,442 exhibitors from 46 states and 56 countries. This show is unique in offering networking opportunities as it showcases the latest technology in the agricultural industry and offers hands on interaction through tours, seminars and special events. Many sectors of the agriculture industry represented include: Dairy/Livestock, Vine/Trees, Machinery/Implement, Tools/Supplies, Row Crops, Processing/Manufacturing, Government, Technology, Hay/Forage, Irrigation, Financial/Insurance, Media and Alternative Energy. Over 90% of the attendees are directly related to the Agricultural Industry and attend to buy products, network and discover new technology. The World Ag Expo is a key support and promoter of the Agricultural Industry as a whole. This event alone has a positive economic, fiscal, and social impact on California particularly strong in the Tulare County and surrounding counties (Kern, Fresno, and Kings Counties). In addition to the World Ag Expo, the Agri-Center facility is host to over 300 events annually such as community events, wedding, receptions, business and governmental meetings, gun shows and equestrian events. Environmental analysis is being prepared to analyze potential impacts of implementation and development consistent with the International Agri-Center's Master Plan including: Expansion of the Heritage Complex, construction of a Equestrian Center, a convention center, and hotels. The master plan also calls for several improvements to the existing site to improve and expand the Ag Expo and other events annually including construction of parks and parklets, additional parking, establishment of parking for recreational vehicles, deployment of roof top solar and parking shade structure solar, and construction of additional food service and restrooms. The environmental analysis is also intended to analyze the impacts of entitlement applications related to the implementation of International Agri-Center's Master Plan including a General Plan Amendment, Zone Amendment, Conditional Use Permit, Annexation and Sphere of Influence amendment. The Project would result in onsite and offsite infrastructure improvements including new and relocated utilities, and new private street improvements. The project is located at 4500 S. Laspina Street Tulare, CA 93274. The study area for the Master Plan located east of State Route 99. The area is bound by State Route 99 to the west, Paige Avenue to the north, Turner Drive to the northeast, and the southern boundary is the Elk Bayou. The majority of the study area is located within the City of Tulare City Limits. The study area includes the area owned by the Agri-Center. Figure 1 of the initial study provided shows the study area boundaries for the Master Plan. A majority of the master plan area is within the City of Tulare Urban Development Boundary and Spere of Influence. A portion is within the unincorporated area of Tulare County.
ceqa-4e4bb05066a1446210.crossStreets: Southeast corner of Laspina Street and International Agri-Center Way

ceqa-687e0a1d420be2876a.name: Ordinance updates amending Chapter 15 of Part VII of the Tulare County Ordinance Code, pertaining to building regulations in Tulare County.
ceqa-687e0a1d420be2876a.projectTitle: Ordinance updates amending Chapter 15 of Part VII of the Tulare County Ordinance Code, pertaining to building regulations in Tulare County.
ceqa-687e0a1d420be2876a.description: The Resource Management Agency (RMA) and the Tulare County Fire Department have comprehensively updated Chapter 15 of Part VII of the Tulare County Ordinance Code regarding building regulations based upon the 2024 International Code Editions prepared by the California Building Standards Commission, state statutes, and local conditions. Chapter 15 of Part VII of the Tulare County Ordinance Code addresses building regulations in Tulare County. Through collaborative efforts by Tulare County Fire Department, County Counsel and RMA, Chapter 15 has been updated to reflect the new regulations in the California Building Standards Code. The references to the 2022 Building Standards Code have been replaced with language conforming to the 2025 Building Standards Code, which goes into effect at the beginning of 2025. This update will also include the new Article 33 Adoption of California Wildland Urban Interface Code, Title 24, Part 7; Significant increase to Section 320 Battery Storage: General Requirements & Entire Section additions; Section 1207 – Electrical Energy Storage Systems (ESS); Amendment for Sprinklered Mobile Homes and Premanufactured homes: Only those that have been manufactured after January 1, 2026, On private properties only, not applicable to mobile home parks; Appendix A-Employee Qualifications, of the California Building Codes; Appendix CJ- Emergency Housing and numerous text/verbiage changes throughout the codes as needed. The amendment to the Ordinance Code is on file at the Clerk of the Board’s Office, the RMA and the Tulare County Fire Chief Office and is available for public review during normal business hours.

ceqa-780b18a2a07956d4ad.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-780b18a2a07956d4ad.description: The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), pursuant to authority granted under California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 22, Division 4.5, Chapter 20, Sec. 66270.61, has issued an Emergency Permit to EMD Millipore Sigma Company, (EPA ID# CAR000301093) to treat hazardous waste through a controlled reaction with chemical solutions. Specifically, three (3) 500-milliliter containers of Ethyl Ether; one (1) 1-liter container of Ethyl Vinyl Ether; one (1) 1-liter container and one (1) 2-liter container of Tetrahydrofuran; one (1) 100-milliliter container of Cyclopentyl Methyl Ether; one (1) 100-milliliter container of Acetaldehyde; seven (7) 4-liter containers, eight (8) 1-liter container, two (2) 500-milliliter containers, and sixteen (16) 5-milliliter containers of Styrene; and one (1) 3-kilogram container, two (2) 500-gram containers, and twenty (20) 100-gram containers of Acrylic Acid must be stabilized prior to transport to an authorized hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facility. These chemicals are currently being stored at EMD Millipore Sigma Company located at 8511 West Riggin Avenue, Visalia, California 93291. DTSC has determined as a safety precaution to prevent an accident or severe injury, an Emergency Permit should be issued for Clean Harbors Environmental Services (Clean Harbors) to chemically stabilize the hazardous waste prior to storage and eventual transportation off-site.

ceqa-283356d91537a67e93.name: CDFA Glassy Winged Sharpshooter Program FY 25/26 & 26/27
ceqa-283356d91537a67e93.projectTitle: CDFA Glassy Winged Sharpshooter Program FY 25/26 & 26/27
ceqa-283356d91537a67e93.description: On October 14, 2025, the Tulare County Board of Supervisors entered into an Agreement with the State of California Department of Food & Agriculture (CDFA) to provide funding for the County of Tulare Agricultural Commissioner’s Office to offset costs of providing and continuing the pest management and detection program to detect and mitigate the presence of Glassy-winged Sharpshooter (GWSS). The continuation of this program is important to substantially reduce populations of GWSS in order to decrease the potential for the spread of Pierce’s Disease. The detection and treatment of this invasive Pest is critically important to the agricultural industry within Tulare County and State of California. Implementing the programs as provided by CDFA (i.e., detect/identify/control new GWSS infestations through insect trapping, visual inspections, and surveys) would mitigate the spread of the invasive GWSS Pest that threatens the Agricultural Industry. As such, the funds will result in a public benefit by supporting the actions necessary to mitigate the invasive GWSS Pest and protect the Agricultural Industry as noted above.

ceqa-aef8a4263743f287d9.name: Pacific Rock Quarry Expansion Project, Case No. LU10-0003
ceqa-aef8a4263743f287d9.description: Pacific Rock requests that a modified CUP be granted, and an amended Reclamation Plan be approved, to authorize the continued operation and expansion of the existing Pacific Rock surface mining facility for a 60-year period. The proposed expanded mining facility involves the excavation and export of approximately 13.2 million tons (19.8 million cubic yards) of mined material. The reclamation plan maps, and cross sections depict the volume of material to be excavated and the proposed finished slope contours after each phase of the mining operations are completed. The ultimate configuration of the Final Reclaimed Surface (FRS) of the mine will include three large, graded pad areas. The finished grades of these pads will be at elevations of approximately 190-feet, 250-feet, and 300-feet. The FRS will include slopes of 1:1 (horizonal: vertical) slope ratio with a maximum slope height of approximately 750-feet along the northerly side of the mine. Detailed information on the configuration of the FRS, and on all other requirements for reclamation of the mined lands at the Pacific Rock Mine are included in the proposed amended Reclamation Plan (Exhibit 9). The proposed project to expand the mine includes the eventual removal of protected trees. Authorization for this tree removal is requested as part of the project and must comply with the County Tree Protection Regulations as described in Mitigation Measure BIO-6. Surface mining activities will continue to be conducted at the facility using explosives to lift and loosen exposed bedrock. This material will continue to be initially sorted into size classes by pushing the material over a steep slope with a front-end loader or a bulldozer. The heavier (larger) pieces of rock are collected from the base of the working slopes for sale as rip-rap or to be crushed for use as road base or other customer specified materials. Material will be further sorted by passing through vibrating scalp screens. Material that does not pass through the screens will be crushed and conveyed back to the screens for additional sorting. Materials will continue to be placed in stockpiles on the mining site and segregated by material type and grain size. In addition to the production and export of mined materials, the facility will also import concrete, asphalt, and soil to the site to be processed and recycled. Mined materials will continue to be exported from the site to market using heavy haul trucks. Such trucks are also used to haul concrete, soil, and asphalt materials to and from the site. All project-related hauling truck traffic is subject to all applicable provisions of the California Vehicle Code and Streets and Highways Code. The authorized mining facility is subject to the operational limitations summarized as follows: Facility Component or Activity To be authorized CUP LU10-0003 CUP Area: 204.4 acres Mining (Excavation) Area and Facilities: 172.8 acres Reclamation End Use: Open Space and Agriculture Annual Production: 468,000 tons Maximum Production (Export) Per Day: 1,500 tons Surface Mining and Processing Methods: Blasting, sorting, processing (crushing) and stockpiling. Structures and Equipment: Aggregate processing facilities, mobile equipment, bunkers, scale, scale house, storaqe bins, etc. Soils Imports and Exports: A maximum of 100,000 cubic yards per year Concrete and Asphalt Recycling: A maximum of 30,000 cubic yards per year Day and Hours of Operation, Mining Excavation and Processing: Monday through Saturday, 7:00am to 4:00pm Maximum Daily Haul Truck Traffic (combined trips for the hauling of aggregate, soil, concrete and asphalt): 120 one-way trips (60 truckloads) per operating day (no change from previous CUP). Maximum material volume excavated and exported from the site under this permit and associated Approved Reclamation Plan: 29,700,000 tons (19,800,000 cubic yards) Vehicle Parking Spaces: 10, including one ADA space Overnight parking of material haul trucks and storage of mobile mining equipment: Mobile mining equipment appurtenant to the subject mining facility and hauling trucks are authorized to be stored overnight on the project site. CUP term limit: 60-years, expiring on June 18, 2086. The mined lands at the site will be reclaimed to an end use of open space and agriculture in accordance with the proposed amended Reclamation Plan. This mining expansion authorized by this project description is anticipated to occur in phases by quadrants. Condition No. 32, Mine Expansion Phasing Plan, requires the development of a Mine Expansion Phasing Plan which identifies the geographic quadrants for expansion of the mined area within the CUP boundary. Prior to the issuance of a Zoning Clearance authorizing expansion and ground disturbing activities within an identified quadrant, the Permittee must submit to the Planning Division for review and approval a Permit Conditions of Approval/ Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program (COAs/MMRP) Report demonstrating compliance with the applicable permit COAs/MMRP for the requested quadrant.

ceqa-81cb69f6bc2372ef96.name: Site Prep and Reforestation
ceqa-81cb69f6bc2372ef96.description: Ventura County RCD plans to plant 4000 native trees and 2180 native companion plants within degraded oak and riparian sites. The purpose of this project is to restore native tree canopy to areas that were historically covered in riparian and oak forest. Oak woodland sites have lost tree canopy from 21 century wildfires (i.e. Thomas Fire) and from oak logging that occurred between 1800--1950's, particularly Valley oak logging in upper Ojai. Valley oak woodlands were cut down to make way for non-native walnut orchards. This project seeks to restore valley oak and coast live oak trees to these sites. Riparian forests have been degraded as a result of Arundo donax, a non-native invasive bamboo like plant. This project will include staking native willow, cottonwood, and sycamore tree plantings into upland riparian banks to increase soil stabilization and restore native tree species canopy to areas that were historically native riparian forest. Beneficiaries of this project will include human residents, native birds, deer, and various other organisms that rely on native oak and riparian forests of Ventura County.

ceqa-0152cdca914ffdbb09.name: Arroyo de la Rana
ceqa-0152cdca914ffdbb09.projectTitle: Ventura River Watershed Riparian Resilience Program
ceqa-0152cdca914ffdbb09.description: The Ojai Valley Land Conservancy plans to conduct ~1 acre of initial treatment and removal of sparse Arundo donax and other target species from 8 parcels on San Antonio Creek. Cut and daub and foliar methods will be used. Following removal, the area will be revegetated with site-specific native plants.

ceqa-4c078e168f171a47be.name: Camp Comfort
ceqa-4c078e168f171a47be.projectTitle: Ventura River Watershed Riparian Resilience Program
ceqa-4c078e168f171a47be.description: Ojai Valley Land Conservancy plans to conduct re-treatment and removal of ~.2acres of sparse giant reed and other non-native species from one parcel along San Antonio Creek adjacent to Camp Comfort. ceqa-66cf2f879e715ebaa8.name: Grapes and Granary
ceqa-66cf2f879e715ebaa8.projectTitle: Ventura River Watershed Riparian Resilience Program
ceqa-66cf2f879e715ebaa8.description: Ojai Valley Land Conservancy plans to remove ~5 acres of Arundo donax and other invasive species from a section of San Antonio Creek across 17 parcels. This sub project is a part of the overall Ventura River Watershed Riparian Resilience Plan. Cut and daub and drill and fill methods will be used. Following removal, the area will be revegetated with site-specific native plants.

ceqa-ec016e8429fbf810dc.name: Devil's Gulch
ceqa-ec016e8429fbf810dc.projectTitle: Ventura River Watershed Riparian Resilience Program
ceqa-ec016e8429fbf810dc.description: The Ojai Valley Land Conservancy will conduct initial treatment and removal of -8 acres of giant reed and other invasive species across 6 parcels along the Ventura River adjacent to Devil's Gulch hiking area. Cut and daub and mastication in certain approved areas will be utilized to treat dense stands of giant reed. Revegetation with native riparian stakes will be completed following treatment.

ceqa-24a9b36eeee06317be.name: Grazing of Yellow Star Thistle
ceqa-24a9b36eeee06317be.description: This project includes goat and sheep grazing within non-native invasive grassland/forbland at Happy Valley Foundation (Besant). The purpose of this project is to reduce thatch and biomass of yellow star thistle (Centaurea solstitialis [Cal-IPC rating: High]) and other non-native invasive plants: Centaurea melitensis (Cal-IPC rating: Moderate), Carduus pycnocephalus (Cal-IPC rating: Moderate; CDFA rating: C), and Festuca perrenis (Cal-IPC Rating: Moderate) through targeted grazing. Beneficiaries of this project include the human and non-human citizens of Upper Ojai. This project will reduce 6 ft tall non-native invasive flashy fuel, increasing fire safety for Upper Ojai community of humans and non-humans before the Santa Ana Wind season (October--January).

ceqa-094d94d1e368afd622.description: Amgen proposes to construct Building 50, a technology and life sciences facility within the southern boundary of the Amgen Thousand Oaks (ATO) Campus, located at 701 Pauling Drive in the City of Thousand Oaks. Building 50 would be comprised of 377,256 square feet of floor area on a 4.27-acre Development Area. Building 50 would include research and laboratory facilities, consisting of chemical and biological lab space, collaboration areas, office space, and a range of supporting functions such as hazardous -materials storage, locker rooms, IT rooms, supply areas, and general storage. A ground-floor lobby and cafés on several floors would also be provided to serve the campus only. Collectively, these uses would establish Building 50 as a modern, purpose-built facility designed to support scientific research and innovation. Building 50 would include four above-grade stories (approximately 70 feet above grade, and 98 feet to the top of the rooftop equipment), and an additional one below-grade level.

ceqa-59c5ab35b2206d78d9.name: TD2222411 Westlake Blvd Eleanor Deteriorated Pole Replacement Project (Notification of Streambed Alteration, No. EPIMS-VEN-56908-R5)
ceqa-59c5ab35b2206d78d9.projectTitle: TD2222411 Westlake Blvd Eleanor Deteriorated Pole Replacement Project (Notification of Streambed Alteration, No. EPIMS-VEN-56908-R5)
ceqa-59c5ab35b2206d78d9.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, South Coast Region 5
ceqa-59c5ab35b2206d78d9.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 5 - South Coast, San Diego
ceqa-59c5ab35b2206d78d9.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. EPIMS-VEN-56908-R5, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to Southern California Edison (Permittee), as represented by Warnetta Logan. The project consists of vegetation trimming and trampling to facilitate access to Pole 1848419E, and the replacement of Pole 1848419E and its associated rock-filled corrugated steel caisson. Project activities will result in 0.014-acre of temporary impacts, and less than three square feet of permanent impacts, to California sycamore woodlands and disturbed vegetation. Project site access will require traversing approximately 55 feet of Lake Eleanor Creek’s bed, banks, and channel, which includes crews accessing the project location on foot, equipment and vehicle operation, and operation of hand tools. Project activities will require crushing and trampling of herbaceous and subshrub vegetation and trimming of two California sycamore trees to facilitate access, as well as ground disturbance associated with the pole and caisson replacement processes. The project also includes the restoration of all project areas, including the regrading of channel areas back to their pre-project contours where applicable, removal of project generated wastes, and the restoration of channel ecology and morphology upon completion of the project. The amendment approved on September 22, 2026 modifies the Project Description to include the use of four four-feet-wide by eight-feet-long steel plates to facilitate access over Lake Eleanor Creek and updates to CDFW staff contact information. No additional impacts will result from the amended project. No additional restoration will be required from the amended project. The second amendment modifies the restriction for nighttime work to allow nighttime work if lane closures prevent daytime construction. It also adds protections to limit nighttime lighting impacts to wildlife. No additional impacts will result from the second amendment and no additional restoration will be required.

ceqa-5db53ef06e59774822.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, South Coast Region 5
ceqa-5db53ef06e59774822.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 5 - South Coast, San Diego
ceqa-5db53ef06e59774822.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-VEN-33011-R5, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the Southern California Regional Rail Authority, as represented by Aaron Azevedo. The whole of the Arroyo Simi Four Bridges Scour Mitigation Project involves the installation of scour countermeasures at four railroad bridges that pass over Arroyo Simi Creek. Scour countermeasures for each bridge include the following, removal and in-kind replacement with rock slope protection and extension of riprap at the bridge abutments; extension of concrete casings around existing steel piles at each pier; installation of filter fabric at the bottom of the channel below riprap apron; backfill of native soil over riprap; and restoration of impacted areas upon completion of construction. The existing single-track configuration at each bridge location would remain upon implementation of the proposed scour countermeasures. Prior to construction, the proposed access road will be graded, vegetation within the project area will be removed, and any remnant concrete collars, piles, caps, footings, and existing rock slope protection will be removed. The project will utilize equipment such as excavators, loaders, haul trucks, water trucks, concrete pumper trucks, chainsaws, generators and pumps, and a backhoe with a hydraulic hammer. A water diversion will be needed to complete the proposed work.

ceqa-0887970be80e943336.name: Santa Paula Creek Spur Dike-2026 Emergency Repair Maintenance Project
ceqa-0887970be80e943336.projectTitle: Santa Paula Creek Spur Dike-2026 Emergency Repair Maintenance Project
ceqa-0887970be80e943336.description: In 2007/8, the Santa Paula Creek Spur Dike Project (Project) was constructed to protect the neighborhoods and communities along Santa Paul Creek from damage caused by storm and debris flows that can occur in Santa Paula Creek during and after significant storms and precipitation. In 2025, the Ventura County Watershed Protection District (WPD), in collaboration with USDA Natural Resource Conservation Service, repaired seven of the spur dike structures in Santa Paula Creek (2025 Santa Paula Creek Spur Dike Replacement Project). However, in December 2025, California experienced significant storms and precipitation, prompting the Governor to declare a State of Emergency (Proclamation No.CA26-1). The storms and precipitation resulted in high flows and debris in Santa Paula Creek damaging the spur dike structures repaired as part of the 2025 Project, reducing the flood control protection for surrounding neighborhoods and communities. As a result of the damage, to protect the surrounding neighborhood, and in preparation of the upcoming El Niño season, WPD is proposing to repair the four damaged spur dike structures. All impacts will be temporary, such as equipment in the creek bed and rearranging rocks/sediment in the creek bed to be placed in the spur dike footprints. The temporary impacts are within the footprint of the 2025 Project.
ceqa-0887970be80e943336.crossStreets: Ojai Road and Fair Weather Crossing

ceqa-3cfa24fd0dc24f7e83.description: Proposed Project: CalNRG proposes to rework Scarlett 4 (04-111-00834) located in the Montalvo West Oil Field in Ventura County, California. This well was drilled and completed as a producer in 1962 and is currently active. The well is located within an established oilfield boundary, on a well-maintained existing well pad, and a well-maintained access road. Proposed project execution will require no new disturbance. No changes to the existing infrastructure will take place. The job will require approximately 10 to 15 days to complete. Produced water will be utilized for all well work by way of existing lines from the facilities to the well and fresh water will be transported in for cement blending. No new facilities are needed. Environmental Setting: Established oil field. Environmentally sensitive as they meet the definition of being within the Coastal Zone, or less than 1000 yards from the ocean. The surrounding land use around the proposed project consists of a developed oil field. Potential Environmental Impacts: Operation of the wells has been subject to all provisions of Senate Bill 1137 for existing wells located within designated health protection zones since June 2024 and would continue to operate in accordance with these regulations. Therefore, no unusual circumstances exist that would present a reasonable possibility of significant environmental effects. No vegetation will be disturbed by this project. There will be no increase in either the number or the capacity of flowlines. The proposed project consists of the California Department of Conservation, Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM) approving 1 permit for CalNRG Operating, LLC to rework the well(s) listed below, in the West Montalvo Oil Field. \API # 0411100834 Well Name Scarlett 4 Exempt Status: As the Lead Agency, CalGEM has determined that the proposed project is exempt from full environmental review requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to the specified exemptions marked in the section below. CalGEM further finds that the proposed project would not result in a significant adverse impact to the environment, or that any of the exceptions to the application of the exemptions apply (14 CCR § 15300.2).

ceqa-a3a44880007aebe9c1.name: Santa Paula Creek Flood Risk Management Facility 2026 Emergency Sediment Removal Project
ceqa-a3a44880007aebe9c1.projectTitle: Santa Paula Creek Flood Risk Management Facility 2026 Emergency Sediment Removal Project
ceqa-a3a44880007aebe9c1.description: Excessive sediments accumulated within the downstream portion of the Santa Paula Creek Flood Risk Management Facility (Facility), constructed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and maintained by the Ventura County Watershed Protection District (VCWPD), due to the significant rainstorms that occurred late December 2025. The Governor of California issued a Proclamation of a State of Emergency (SOE) on December 24, 2025, and a follow-up on April 17, 2026, clarifying that “the Office of Emergency Services has validated additional damages and costs attributable to the Late December 2025 Storms, including…flooding and a heightened risk of debris flows and mudslides in Ventura County”. In addition, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration issued an El Niño Advisory, clarifying on September 10, 2026, that “During the October-December 2026 season, there is a 75% chance of a historic event that would exceed the strength of previous El Niño events dating back to 1950.” In response, the Governor issued another SOE on September 21, 2026, for the 2026-2027 wet season. To address these risks, VCWPD proposes the Santa Paula Creek Flood Risk Management Facility 2026 Emergency Sediment Removal Project (Project), which will remove up to 70,000 cubic yards of sediment. Between the railroad and just upstream of the Santa Clara River confluence, the work would occur over up to 3,900 linear feet, weather and time permitting. An estimated maximum 12 feet of sediment depth would be removed from the channel, with the excavation depth gradually becoming shallower to daylight at the upstream end. The Project would maintain adequate capacity, prevent overtopping of the concreted rock riprap facility banks, prevent erosion of the east maintenance access road, and prevent undermining and flooding of adjacent commercial and residential properties and roads. The Project would also remove sediments accumulated within the fish ladder at the upstream end of the Facility, and would ensure suitable connection to the low flow channel immediately upstream and downstream of the fish ladder, as specified in the Facility’s Operations, Maintenance, Repair, Replacement, and Rehabilitation (OMRR&R) Manual. This work would occur over about 800 linear feet. Combined total work area within the Facility is up to 14 acres. All materials removed from the site would be transferred to the VCWPD stockpile location on uplands immediately west of the channel and south of Hwy 126. Work would include installation of temporary stream crossings utilizing six 40-ft-lengths of 3-ft-diameter pipes placed side by side to avoid operating heavy equipment in flowing water. Earthen coffer dams comprised of dry alluvium would be placed as needed to divert surface water and allow excavation of accumulated sediment under dry conditions. A team of qualified biologists would relocate aquatic organisms to suitable habitat within flowing water before, during, and immediately following each diversion. Proposed work may take about 90 working days to complete. The work area is currently largely devoid of mature vegetation due to the scouring flows received during the previous three winter storm seasons. Biological surveys would be conducted before work and each morning during work activities to identify and avoid or relocate sensitive biological resources. Work would occur outside the bird nesting season. The temporary diversion channels and final graded channel would be configured to allow successful fish passage. Boulders would be placed in the final channel with guidance from qualified biologists to provide resting areas and cover for aquatic species.

ceqa-2329b82290b726ddc7.name: Eriogonum Phylogenetic Study (Project)
ceqa-2329b82290b726ddc7.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Habitat Conservation Planning
ceqa-2329b82290b726ddc7.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife (Headquarters), Habitat Conservation Planning Branch - Sacramento
ceqa-2329b82290b726ddc7.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife is issuing a California Endangered Species Act and Native Plant Protection Act scientific, educational, or management permit pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 2081, subdivision (a), and California Code of Regulations, Title 14, section 786.9, subdivision (c) to Charles Boissavy (Permit No. 2081(a)-26-008-RP) for a project to collect Ione buckwheat, Irish Hill buckwheat, and San Nicolas Island buckwheat plant tissue, voucher specimens, and seed for a phylogenetic study investigating trait diversification and biogeographic adaptations in Eriogonum. Between 2026 and 2027, up to five leaves will be collected for DNA analysis from at least one population each of Ione buckwheat, Irish Hill buckwheat, and San Nicolas Island buckwheat. Additional populations may also be sampled, with up to five leaf samples collected from each population. Three to four involucres will be collected from each population for color analysis. Stem segments, flowers, and fruits (when present) will be collected from up to two individuals per population and preserved in liquid for morphological and anatomical analyses. One voucher specimen of Ione buckwheat and San Nicholas Island buckwheat will be collected from each population visited. Up to five percent of the available seed will be collected from visited Irish Hill buckwheat occurrences for long-term conservation storage at the California Botanic Garden seed bank. All leaf tissue will be silica-dried in the field prior to DNA extraction and analysis. Microscope slides of leaf tissue will be prepared for each taxon to compare micromorphology of leaves between taxa. Resulting data will provide an understanding of the diversification and adaptation of Eriogonum, relatedness and gene flow between populations, and genetic diversity to support species recovery and conservation efforts.

ceqa-aee7f214848625f021.name: Camarillo Airport Runway 8-26 Pavement Rehabilitation Project
ceqa-aee7f214848625f021.projectTitle: Camarillo Airport, Airport Properties Limited (APL) Development Project
ceqa-aee7f214848625f021.description: The proposed project at Camarillo Airport consists of the rehabilitation of the existing Runway 8-26 pavement, including pavement milling and resurfacing/repair, and rehabilitation of the existing Runway 8-26 edge lighting system. The existing pavement has surpassed its usable life and continues to deteriorate. Deteriorating pavement creates foreign object debris (FOD) which can damage aircraft and presents a safety issue for pilots. The proposed project will allow the airport to make needed repairs to existing pavement and lighting, prevent continued deterioration, and provide a safer airfield environment.

ceqa-6a7a0aa1e0f1af685c.name: South Oxnard Connect Specific Plan
ceqa-6a7a0aa1e0f1af685c.description: The Proposed Project would establish a regulatory framework to guide transit-oriented growth in proximity to the approved Gold Coast Transit District High-Quality Transit Corridor, increase development capacity and allow residential and mixed-use development on 13 opportunity sites, and establish a development incentive program to expand mixed income housing opportunities and advance targeted community benefits on opportunity sites within the plan area. The Specific Plan would also establish environmental development standards, development standards, and design standards for the 13 opportunity sites and design standards for all Garden Apartment (R-3), High Rise Residential (R-4), and General Commercial (C-2) sites in the Specific Plan area regardless of being considered an opportunity site. The General Plan Land Use Element Amendment would allow increased land use densities consistent with the South Oxnard Connect Specific Plan; remove the 30-foot Scenic Highway setback/designation along Hueneme Road and Pleasant Valley Road adjacent to the project boundary; and amend the 2021-2029 Housing Element to reflect the MU-1 zoning designation and associated density increase on Housing Element sites 37, 39 and 40. The Zoning Map Amendment would: incorporate the South Oxnard Connect Specific Plan on the City Zoning Map, and direct development regulations for the 13 opportunity sites within the Specific Plan area, and change the zoning designation on 11 of the 13 opportunity sites from General Commercial (C-2) to Mixed Use (MU-1). The zoning on the remaining two (2) opportunity sites would not change from Garden Apartment (R-3).
ceqa-6a7a0aa1e0f1af685c.action: General Plan Amendment, Rezone, Specific Plan

ceqa-e9a559f6db960006b1.name: Peach Hill Wash Emergency Sewer Stabilization
ceqa-e9a559f6db960006b1.projectTitle: Peach Hill Wash Emergency Sewer Stabilization
ceqa-e9a559f6db960006b1.description: Peach Hill Wash transitions from concrete lined to natural unimproved channel and connects to the Arroyo Simi. The unimproved channel borders the City of Moorpark and unincorporated Ventura County. Peach Hill Wash has a Watershed Protection District (WPD) access road along the wash and a Ventura County Water and Sanitation sewer pipeline that runs beneath the access road. Portions of the bank and access road have eroded and put the sewer line at risk for exposure damage, and sewage spill once the large El Nino storms arrive. To alleviate this risk, about 150-175 linear feet of bank will be stabilized. The project consists of clearing and grubbing existing native and non-native vegetation along the bank, benching, and adding fill and ungrouted rock riprap to stabilize the bank and protect the sewer line and surrounding neighborhood. The work area is currently dry, and no surface water is anticipated to be encountered. A biologist and environmental Best Management Practices will be utilized for work activities.

ceqa-f44ca5b32e05facb9e.name: Santa Clara River Restoration
ceqa-f44ca5b32e05facb9e.description: Project involves restoring 70 acres of riparian habitat on TNC’s Prairie Pacific property. Project activities include invasive vegetation removal, trash and debris removal, native plant revegetation, enhancement of wetland features, and maintenance and monitoring of habitat restoration. This work will increase native biodiversity, repair hydraulic function and habitat connectivity, and will result in long-term habitat integrity, support endangered species recovery, and provide climate resiliency to the Santa Clara River ecosystem. WCB Project Tracker ID: 2025168.

ceqa-347c0f5c2d80c599c9.description: The project includes the annexation of APN 069-0-020-015 from unincorporated Ventura County land into the City of Ventura. The project also includes a zone change from the County’s Light Industrial zoning designation to the City’s Residential Planned Development (RPD)-7U zone, and approval of a Tentative Tract Map. The project involves the development of 117 residential units, including 24 two-story single-family units, 11 three-story single-family units, and 82 three-story two-family units in 41 buildings, totaling 76 residential buildings. Ten percent (12 units) would be affordable units for moderate-income households. The project would include 297 parking spaces (234 private garage spaces and 63 guest spaces). The project also includes recreational amenities for residents, including a community park, tot lot, dog park, paseo, greenbelt, and other common open spaces.

ceqa-6acc76b270aa23d0b5.name: Approval of Local Energy Efficiency and Conservation Standards Application Findings Submitted by the City of Ojai for the 2025 Energy Code Cycle
ceqa-6acc76b270aa23d0b5.projectTitle: Approval of Local Energy Efficiency and Conservation Standards Application Findings Submitted by the City of Ojai for the 2025 Energy Code Cycle
ceqa-6acc76b270aa23d0b5.description: The California Energy Commission (CEC) adopts and regularly updates regulations that define a process for local governments to apply to the CEC to make certain findings regarding locally adopted energy conservation or energy insulation standards (California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 24, Part 1, section 10-106 and section 10-110; Public Resources Code (PRC) section 25402.1(h)(2)). The local government’s proposed standards are often referred to as the Local Reach Codes and require local governments to submit an application to the CEC consistent with the requirements listed in section 10-106(b). Before the local standards may be enforced, the CEC must make the following findings pursuant to PRC section 25402.1(h)(2) and as listed in section 10-106(a): 1) The proposed local standards will require the diminution of energy consumption levels compared to the 2025 Energy Code, and 2) The local government has filed the basis of its cost-effectiveness determination with the CEC. On December 19, 2025, the City of Ojai (the City) submitted an application to the CEC that included: 1) the basis of its determination that the locally adopted energy efficiency standards contained in Ordinance No. 969 are cost-effective; and (2) documentation that the locally adopted energy efficiency standards contained in Ordinance No. 969 will require the diminution of energy consumption levels compared to the 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards (Energy Code), as required by PRC section 25402.1(h)(2) and by CCR, Title 24, Part 1, section 10-106. Based on the information submitted, staff analysis, and the Executive Director's recommendation, the CEC approved findings of the City of Ojai’s section 10-106 application at the CEC’s August 17, 2026, Business Meeting.

ceqa-633555fdd75c7f3775.name: Lost Canyons Addendum
ceqa-633555fdd75c7f3775.projectTitle: Whiteface Specific Plan Amendment 6: Lost Canyons Draft EIR
ceqa-633555fdd75c7f3775.description: The Proposed Project consists of the transfer of 180 dwelling units permitted within the Whiteface Specific Plan boundaries from the southern portion of the specific plan area to the northern portion of the specific plan area. Specifically, the 180 units would be relocated from the southern areas within Dry Canyon and Tapo Canyon to areas north of Lost Canyons Drive. Overall, the Proposed Project would result in a total of 364 residential lots, including 362 lots north of Lost Canyons Drive and two estate lots located south of Lost Canyons Drive, including one in Dry Canyon and one in Tapo Canyon , both of which would be accessible from existing easements. Instead of spreading the 364 units throughout a wider footprint in the Whiteface Specific Plan as was originally approved with the Approved Project, the Proposed Project would cluster 362 of the 364 units within the northern area of the Whiteface Specific Plan where the Shadow Canyon Golf Course previously operated. Also, the Proposed Project would not include the development of a new golf course, a clubhouse, or a private park as was approved with the Approved Project. Instead, the Proposed Project proposes to provide recreational amenities including a private recreation building for residents of the development as well as public recreational trails through the southern portion of the Project Site and public recreational trails on the golf course trails that exist within portions of the northern portion of the Project Site. The Proposed Project would retain the Residential Estate (RE) zoning designation on four areas in the Specific Plan boundaries that currently have this designation, and the Applicant proposes a maximum of sixteen residential estate lots that could be developed within these areas of the specific plan. Minimum lot sizes for RE lots are a minimum of 20 acres. The evaluation herein of biological resources and other resource topics does not account for any future development within these RE zoned areas given there are currently no plans for site-specific development in these areas. As such, the analyses herein assume that RE zoned areas are not disturbed or impacted by development. It should be noted that the CEQA documentation for the Whiteface Specific Plan as well as for the Approved Project evaluated the environmental effects of up to 1,211 residential units in the specific plan boundaries. The Proposed Project would result in 364 units in addition to the 847 units that were allowed to be built in Sand Canyon/Big Sky Ranch area of the specific plan boundaries, of which approximately 738 residential units have been built to date. Project Title: GP A-2024-0003, Z-S-2025-0003, SP-S-2025-0002, PD-S-2025-0003, AND TT-2025-0002 (Addendum No. 8 to the EIR for the Lost Canyons Specific Plan Project)
ceqa-633555fdd75c7f3775.crossStreets: Dry Canyon, Tapo Canyon, and Lost Canyons Drive

ceqa-77a3ea8caa8a22a826.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has amended Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. EPIMS-VEN-19609-R5, pursuant to section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to Southern California Edison Company (SCE), as represented by Victoria Parsons. The original Project consists of installing a temporary ramp into the Santa Clara River, vegetation removal within the channel, and removal of one wood H-frame structure (poles 4244682E and 4244683E). The activities covered by this Agreement include vegetation trimming, overland travel, grading, creation of a temporary berm, and partial removal of a wood H-frame structure. The Project’s activities result in 0.64 acre of temporary impacts to the streambed. The amendment changes the access route from the south of the Project area to directly north of the Project area via North Bank Drive, includes full removal of the H-frame structure, and adds removal of a steel caisson to 24 inches below grade. To support the modified access route, the Project adds a temporary culvert over Sudden Barranca and places heavy-duty composite ground protection mats along the access route. The amended Project reduces the total temporary impacts to 0.49 acre.

ceqa-2c263976333d6aaee7.name: Ventura 1 - Frontier Project
ceqa-2c263976333d6aaee7.description: Frontier proposes fiber-optic installation to provide improved broadband connectivity within the cities of Santa Paula and Ojai, in Ventura County, California. The proposed route begins just north of the City of Santa Paula and extends generally along State Route 150 (SR-150) to the City of Ojai. The current design follows existing utility pathways (i.e., where communications and/or other utility infrastructure is currently present) and proposes to install fiber using a combination of existing infrastructure including aerial installations (i.e., overlashing) and underground conduit installation. As currently designed, the route is primarily aerial, and no new overhead utility structures are proposed, although Frontier expects to underground some facilities. Given the nature of infrastructure projects, the mix of aerial vs. underground installation methods is subject to change up to and including through construction. Where underground installation is required, Frontier intends to utilize localized hand trenching and very limited horizontal directional drilling (HDD). Frontier expects new infrastructure to be installed within existing rights-of-way (ROW) and authorized utility easements in areas where previous ground-disturbance activities have occurred. Where ground disturbing activities are planned, they are expected to include placing conduit, installing handholes, and minor surface restoration. Frontier intends to use existing access routes to minimize disturbance and to limit work areas to graded road shoulders and other reasonably adjacent disturbed surfaces, to the extent practicable, to minimize new ground disturbance

ceqa-89bd77208075ccd730.name: 2025-CDP-02 Santa Paula East Shopping Center
ceqa-89bd77208075ccd730.description: Addendum (No. 2) to the East Gateway Project Final EIR (SCH #2011071068) addresses the development of an approximate 14.8-acre vacant site in the East Area 2 Planning Area at 18114 East Telegraph Road in Santa Paula (Project Site) with a new neighborhood retail commercial center. The Project Site has a General Plan land use designation of Commercial and is zoned C-LI (Commercial/Light Industrial). Pursuant to the Santa Paula Municipal Code, commercial uses are permitted by-right in the C-LI zone and this designation allows for heavy commercial and light industrial uses to stimulate economic development. The East Gateway Project Final EIR assumed the Project Site and adjacent properties would be developed with retail commercial uses at a floor area ratio (FAR) of 25 percent, equivalent to approximately 155,000 square feet of retail commercial development on the Project Site. Based on the information in the Addendum, the development of the proposed commercial uses within the East Gateway Planning Area would not result in any new significant impacts or any substantial increase in severity of the significant Impacts identified in the Final EIR. Additionally, no new information of substantial Importance has been identified that indicates the Project would result in any new significant impacts or any substantial increase in the severity of the significant impacts identified in the Final EIR.

ceqa-bc74c9bc6f479e0e28.description: The Oxnard Harbor District proposes to construct and operate a new approximately 455,900-square-foot, up-to-six-level aboveground vehicle parking structure at the Port of Hueneme (Port), just west of the Port office building located at 333 Ponoma Street, Port Hueneme. The parking structure would serve as the transfer point for automobiles unloaded from between ocean-going vessels, with vehicles subsequently driven to designated regional off-site processing centers for processing and distribution. An approximately 345,800-square-foot concrete parking pad would also be poured outside the parking structure for high-and-heavy cargo/vehicles, which may include oversized cargo, vehicles, or specialized equipment. This concrete pad would be designed to support existing operational requirements, including vehicle maneuvering, staging, and access. With project implementation, annual automobile imports could increase to approximately 700,000 vehicles by the year 2046.

ceqa-52b869c6f1216bf3f2.projectTitle: Permit Adjustment to Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 2032 (as adjusted by Case Nos. PL18-0034, PL20-0053 and PL23-0065) Permit Adjustment Case No. PL26-0009
ceqa-52b869c6f1216bf3f2.description: This Permit Adjustment is granted for the replacement of the existing temporary Health Center Modular trailers (2,880 square feet (sq. ft.)) with a new permanent Health and Wellness Center (5,300 sq. ft. of gross indoor building area) that will provide physical and mental health services to students, faculty and staff. One new van accessible/ambulance parking space will be provided at the Health and Wellness Center, connecting to the existing service driveway at the project's north edge. The 2,000 sq, ft. Fitness Center Expansion, which was previously approved, will no longer be constructed. Project construction will require removing the four existing tennis courts which are contributors to the historic district on campus the new Health Center. These courts are located northeast of the pool and north of the Gym building. A certificate of appropriateness has been obtained by the Ventura County Cultural Heritage Board. Removal of the tennis courts will allow the school to create a new, centrally located, large open landscape space for student use south of the new Health Center. New accessible pathways will connect the Health and Wellness Center to other adjacent buildings and spaces on campus. In addition, four new tennis courts will be added at the existing Tennis Center on the south end of campus (approved under Zone Clearance No. ZC25-1028). Removal of two non-heritage sized oak trees and encroachment into the Tree Protection Zone of 21 trees will be required to accommodate the construction of the health and wellness center. Proposed new landscaping includes trees that represent the loss of the two oak trees, and the planting of new trees in planted areas. The work required to complete this Permit Adjustment will be done in the following order: • Demolition of the site area required for the new building, and construction and occupancy of the new Health and Wellness Center (Zoning Clearance, Demo Permit, Grading Permit, Building Permits); 14 months • Demolition of the temporary medical modular and remaining tennis courts (Zoning Clearance, Demo Permit) 2 months • Construction of a new, centrally located, large open landscape space (Zoning Clearance, Grading Permit) 3 months • Construction of new accessible pathways and other hardscape features as identified on landscape plan (Zoning Clearance, Building Permit for site stairs and retaining walls) 3 months concurrent with construction of the landscape area noted above.

ceqa-7d8f3055a08c5f0b0e.name: 726-6US-1340 Pipeline Investigation
ceqa-7d8f3055a08c5f0b0e.description: Caltrans approves of the encroachment permit for Crimson Midstream, LLC to excavate and expose its pipeline to assess multiple reported anomalies as part of Crimson’s Integrity Management Program. This work will involve potholing and excavating within Caltrans right-of-way (ROW) along the State Route (SR) 23 southbound offramp at post mile (PM) R6.15. The proposed work will involve exposing the pipeline, removing any pipeline coating, cleaning the pipeline surface, inspecting and assessing the anomaly, performing the repair as necessary (welding may be required), applying pipeline coating, and backfilling and restoring the worksite to original conditions. Crimson Midstream, LLC is requesting a temporary encroachment permit to access Caltrans ROW to complete the above-mentioned maintenance and repair work. Excavation will have a depth of 5 feet, and an average width and length of 6 feet by 10 feet. No public utilities will be relocated, and no new ROW will be acquired.

ceqa-592668f26bc3ff4bf3.name: Pacific Rock Quarry Expansion Project, Case No. LU10-0003
ceqa-592668f26bc3ff4bf3.description: Pacific Rock requests that a modified CUP be granted, and an amended Reclamation Plan be approved, to authorize the continued operation and expansion of the existing Pacific Rock surface mining facility for a 60-year period. (See Notice of Determination for additional detail.) The proposed expanded mining facility involves the excavation and export of approximately 13.2 million tons (19.8 million cubic yards) of mined material. The reclamation plan maps, and cross sections depict the volume of material to be excavated and the proposed finished slope contours after each phase of the mining operations are completed. The ultimate configuration of the Final Reclaimed Surface (FRS) of the mine will include three large, graded pad areas. The finished grades of these pads will be at elevations of approximately 190-feet, 250-feet, and 300-feet. The FRS will include slopes of 1:1 (horizonal: vertical) slope ratio with a maximum slope height of approximately 750-feet along the northerly side of the mine. Detailed information on the configuration of the FRS, and on all other requirements for reclamation of the mined lands at the Pacific Rock Mine are included in the proposed amended Reclamation Plan (Exhibit 9). The proposed project to expand the mine includes the eventual removal of protected trees. Authorization for this tree removal is requested as part of the project and must comply with the County Tree Protection Regulations as described in Mitigation Measure 810-6. Surface mining activities will continue to be conducted at the facility using explosives to lift and loosen exposed bedrock. This material will continue to be initially sorted into size classes by pushing the material over a steep slope with a front-end loader or a bulldozer. The heavier (larger) pieces of rock are collected from the base of the working slopes for sale as rip-rap or to be crushed for use as road base or other customer specified materials. Material will be further sorted by passing through vibrating scalp screens. Material that does not pass through the screens will be crushed and conveyed back to the screens for additional sorting. Materials will continue to be placed in stockpiles on the mining site and segregated by material type and grain size. In addition to the production and export of mined materials, the facility will also import concrete, asphalt, and soil to the site to be processed and recycled. Mined materials will continue to be exported from the site to market using heavy haul trucks. Such trucks are also used to haul concrete, soil, and asphalt materials to and from the site. All project-related hauling truck traffic is subject to all applicable provisions of the California Vehicle Code and Streets and Highways Code. The authorized mining facility is subject to the operational limitations summarized as follows: Facility Component or Activity To be authorized CUP LU10-0003 CUP Area: 204.4 acres Mining (Excavation) Area and Facilities: 172.8 acres Reclamation End Use: Open Space and Agriculture Annual Production: 468,000 tons Maximum Production (Export) Per Day: 1,500 tons Surface Mining and Processing Methods: Blasting, sorting, processing (crushing) and stockpiling. Structures and Equipment: Aggregate processing facilities, mobile equipment, bunkers, scale, scale house, storaqe bins, etc. Soils Imports and Exports: A maximum of 100,000 cubic yards per year Concrete and Asphalt Recycling: A maximum of 30,000 cubic yards per year Day and Hours of Operation, Mining Excavation and Processing: Monday through Saturday, 7:00am to 4:00pm Maximum Daily Haul Truck Traffic (combined trips for the hauling of aggregate, soil, concrete and asphalt): 120 one-way trips (60 truckloads) per operating day (no change from previous CUP). Maximum material volume excavated and exported from the site under this permit and associated Approved Reclamation Plan: 29,700,000 tons (19,800,000 cubic yards) Vehicle Parking Spaces: 10, including one ADA space Overnight parking of material haul trucks and storage of mobile mining equipment: Mobile mining equipment appurtenant to the subject mining facility and hauling trucks are authorized to be stored overnight on the project site. CUP term limit: 60-years, expiring on June 18, 2086. The mined lands at the site will be reclaimed to an end use of open space and agriculture in accordance with the proposed amended Reclamation Plan. This mining expansion authorized by this project description is anticipated to occur in phases by quadrants. Condition No. 32, Mine Expansion Phasing Plan, requires the development of a Mine Expansion Phasing Plan which identifies the geographic quadrants for expansion of the mined area within the CUP boundary. Prior to the issuance of a Zoning Clearance authorizing expansion and ground disturbing activities within an identified quadrant, the Permittee must submit to the Planning Division for review and approval a Permit Conditions of Approval/ Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program (COAs/MMRP) Report demonstrating compliance with the applicable permit COAs/MMRP for the requested quadrant.

ceqa-4739a5071f394e4e93.name: Assistance for Management Practice Planning
ceqa-4739a5071f394e4e93.description: The goal of this project is to provide critical support to growers in Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL) areas by facilitating the development of targeted Management Practice Plans (MPPs) for addressing water quality constituents outlined in TMDL requirements, in response to Order R4-2023-0353 General Waste Discharge Requirements from Discharges from Irrigated Agricultural Lands within the Los Angeles Region (Ag WDRs). This Project focuses on growers who have chosen to fulfill the Irrigated Lands General Order through the development and implementation of targeted MPPs. The Ag WDRs incorporates seventeen TMDLs with load allocations for agriculture.

ceqa-7193a2fe6338603aa0.name: Assistance for Monitoring and Management Plan Implementation
