ceqa-00c28d24e9da962b3c.name: Downtown Thousand Oaks Project
ceqa-00c28d24e9da962b3c.description: The approximately 17.68-acre proposed project site is generally located at 2100 East Thousand Oaks Boulevard. The project site is currently designated Institutional and Commercial Neighborhood, and zoned SP-11 and SP-20. The site is specifically bound by Thousand Oaks Boulevard and commercial uses (i.e., Saremi and Johnstone Dentistry) to the north, Conejo School Road and commercial uses (i.e., The Lakes shopping center) to the east, Highway 101 to the south, and Oakwood Drive, commercial uses (i.e., Enhanced Landscape, a private landscape company), and single-family residential uses to the west. The site is located within the Civic Arts Specific Plan (SP-11) and Thousand Oaks Boulevard Specific Plan (SP-20), and consists of three public right-of-way segments (i.e., Thousand Oaks Boulevard, Dallas Drive, and Oakwood Drive). The proposed project would use the parking facilities at 265 South Rancho Road and 110 South Conejo School Road for satellite parking during peak demand times. These locations would also be utilized for off-site construction laydown areas. The proposed project involves a General Plan Amendment to change the land use designation of a 5.33-acre portion of the project area to Mixed-Use and increase the height within that area; amendment of the Civic Arts Plaza Specific Plan (SP No. 11) to facilitate development of a new pedestrian-oriented downtown, including mixed-use residential, a hotel, commercial, office, and entertainment uses; partial reconstruction of the existing City Hall; public amenities such as a park plaza and outdoor amphitheater; and supporting infrastructure, including new roadways, reconfigured utilities, and stormwater management improvements; a Tentative Tract Map consolidating 14 existing parcels into 9 new lots; a Development Permit for construction of four new buildings, including a seven-story, 142-key hotel; a seven-story, 161-unit mixed-use building (26 affordable units) with subterranean garage; a four-story, 79-unit mixed-use building (13 affordable units) with subterranean garage; a two-story restaurant building; and a public park with a children’s play structure, splash pad, interactive play equipment, informal stages and seating areas, and flexible open space; a Special Use Permit for the sale and consumption of alcohol; and a Protected Tree Permit for the removal and replacement of protected trees, as well as the encroachment into the protected zone of protected trees. The proposed project would be constructed in five phases, which are anticipated to commence in 2027 and be completed by 2032.
ceqa-00c28d24e9da962b3c.crossStreets: U.S. 101, Thousand Oaks Boulevard, Conejo School Road

ceqa-2f27b437fa750aaf77.name: Adoption of a Resolution to Acknowledge Receipt of, Accept, and Agree to the California Coastal Commission’s Suggested Modifications to the County’s Amendments
ceqa-2f27b437fa750aaf77.projectTitle: Adoption of a Resolution to Acknowledge Receipt of, Accept, and Agree to the California Coastal Commission’s Suggested Modifications to the County’s Amendments
ceqa-2f27b437fa750aaf77.description: [PROJECT TITLE CONTINUED]: to the Local Coastal Program Primarily Addressing Coastal Hazards and Sea Level Rise, and Adoption of an Ordinance into the Ventura County Coastal Zoning Ordinance (Pl20-0039). On May 20, 2025, the Ventura County Board of Supervisors approved modifications to the Local Coastal Program (LCP) that plans for coastal hazards and sea level rise in the Coastal Area Plan (Land Use Plan). Amendments to the Coastal Zoning Ordinance (Implementation Plan) implement the Coastal Area Plan. On March 11, 2026, the Coastal Commission conditionally approved the LCP Amendments with modifications that required County Board of Supervisors approval. On June 23, 2026, the Board of Supervisors adopted a resolution acknowledging receipt of, accepting, and agreeing to the Coastal Commission’s suggested modifications and adopted the LCP Amendments, as modified. The LCP Amendments, as modified, shall become effective after certification by the Coastal Commission.

ceqa-ae795ab5fdad43576f.name: Smith Road Tank
ceqa-ae795ab5fdad43576f.description: The Proposed Project includes the construction and operation of a 43 foot-tall by approximately 125-foot-diameter above-ground steel water storage tank with a total storage capacity of approximately 3.5 million gallons. The tank would connect to the CCSB and CCNB pipelines located beneath Smith Road, directly south of the project site. The Proposed Project's objectives are to provide additional water storage capacity to meet the peak hourly demands in the Simi Valley Region during short-term imported water supply outage conditions; provide operational benefits during normal and high-demand conditions; provide a reserve of water that can be used during supply interruptions, such as maintenance work, power outages, or natural disasters; help maintain consistent water pressure throughout the distribution system; and in case of emergencies, such as fires, provide an immediate source of water for firefighting and other critical needs. The tank would be constructed on top of an elevated pad, which would be created with imported fill material to reach a ground elevation of approximately 1,096 feet above mean sea level (AMSL), or approximately 35 feet above the existing ground surface, allowing the tank to operate by gravity without pumping. The Proposed Project would also include the construction and maintenance of inlet and outlet pipelines, pipeline connections, overflow and drain pipes, above-ground isolation valves, a paved access road with a driveway off of Smith Road, retaining walls, and cabinet(s) housing instrumentation and control components. An approximately 700-foot-long Southern California Edison (SCE) service line would be required from the SCE connection location to the tank.
ceqa-ae795ab5fdad43576f.developmentType: Water Facilities (3.5 MG Storage Tank)(Type Storage Tank, MGD 3.5)

ceqa-b0990bdfea184c8fff.name: TFX Aviation Incorporated Newbury Park Facility, Post-Closure Permit Renewal
ceqa-b0990bdfea184c8fff.projectTitle: TFX Aviation Incorporated Newbury Park Facility, Post-Closure Permit Renewal
ceqa-b0990bdfea184c8fff.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-b0990bdfea184c8fff.description: The Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) pursuant to authority granted under Chapter 14, Division 4.5, of Title 22, of the California Code of Regulations intends to approve a Post-Closure Permit Renewal (Renewal). The project is the issuance of a Renewal Permit for the Hazardous Waste Management Facility (HWMF) at TFX Aviation Incorporated Newbury Park Facility. The term of this Renewal will be 10 years and includes the continuation of post-closure care activities and a request to reduce ongoing groundwater monitoring frequency. Project Activities: The Renewal proposes continued post closure care activities at the Facility and the proposal to reduce the ongoing groundwater monitoring frequency. There are no other proposed changes to the Facility, or any of the waste being received or treated, or to any other operations or units. There will be no operational changes or ground disturbance. All previous Post-Closure Permit requirements will remain in effect. This Renewal will not result in any new or substantially more severe significant impacts on the environment. Background: The Facility was used for manufacturing civilian and military aircraft components between 1956 and 1989. During the manufacturing process, hazardous wastes that included metals, cyanide, chlorinated solvents, and wastes oils were generated. Soil and groundwater at the Facility were impacted from the on-site waste disposal practices that included use of a surface impoundment. As a result, 3,000 cubic yards of contaminated soil were removed, and groundwater and soil vapor treatment and extraction systems were installed. The former surface impoundment was acknowledged certified closed by DTSC on August 26, 1987. A final post closure permit was issued by DTSC on November 24, 1992. The post closure permit addressed water quality monitoring of the former impoundment and post-closure care of the former impoundment. The Post-Closure Permit was renewed/reissued on October 7, 2005, and was renewed again in 2016. The groundwater remedy is ongoing and is expected to continue throughout the permit cycle. The Facility has land use restrictions under a Land Use Covenant. There is a groundwater monitoring and extraction well network installed at the Facility. Groundwater treatment, which occurs at this Facility and is permitted by Ventura County, includes treatment of groundwater contaminated with metals (primarily Hexavalent Chromium) to reduce the metals to a lesser form (primarily Trivalent Chromium), and remove these metals from the water. Groundwater treatment also includes treatment of groundwater contaminated with chlorinated volatile organics through an air stripper and scrubber utilizing activated carbon. Hazardous waste is generated as a result of groundwater extraction, treatment and remediation activities, but is not a part of this permit. The hazardous waste generated by the treatment includes bag filters containing waste metals, small volumes of liquid waste, and accumulated rainwater (when the treatment system is non-operational) totals less than 500 kilograms of hazardous waste per month. No other industrial operations take place at the TFX Aviation Facility.

There will be no increase in either the number or the capacity of flowlines. ceqa-e0a2264b73d4d0001c.name: TD1367680 Lake Eleanor Pole and Anchor Replacement Project, (Notification of Lake or Streambed Alteration, No. EPIMS-VEN-42661-R5)
ceqa-e0a2264b73d4d0001c.projectTitle: TD1367680 Lake Eleanor Pole and Anchor Replacement Project, (Notification of Lake or Streambed Alteration, No. EPIMS-VEN-42661-R5)
ceqa-e0a2264b73d4d0001c.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, South Coast Region 5
ceqa-e0a2264b73d4d0001c.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 5 - South Coast, San Diego
ceqa-e0a2264b73d4d0001c.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. EPIMS-VEN-42661-R5, pursuant to section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to Southern California Edison Company (SCE). The Project consists of removing and replacing two wooden utility poles with lightweight steel poles, replacing three existing anchors in-kind in the same location at each pole, and installing new guy wires from each anchor to each pole. A crane will be used from the adjacent road to facilitate utility pole removal, hole excavation, and replacement with new utility poles. Impacts resulting from the Project include vegetation crushing and trimming and soil disturbance within Lake Eleanor Creek. The Project will result in 0.39 acre of temporary impacts to California sycamore woodlands, chamise chaparral, coast live oak woodlands, and mulefat thickets, and 0.01 acre of permanent impacts to coast live oak woodlands and mulefat thickets. SCE will restore the 0.39 acre of temporary impacts to stream bed, bank, and channel to pre-Project conditions. This will include recontouring and blading disturbed soils, returning topsoils to original locations, and raking and spreading duff over the disturbance footprint.

ceqa-a8edefaa1449c10158.name: American Jewish University – Camp Alonim Project, Case No. PL22-0032
ceqa-a8edefaa1449c10158.projectTitle: American Jewish University - Camp Alonim Project
ceqa-a8edefaa1449c10158.description: Major Modification to Conditional Use Permit No. 1776 and a Discretionary Tree Permit to authorize development of additional facilities at Camp Alonim. Proposed facilities include the following: • Welcome Center: a 4,460 sq. ft. building consisting of a lobby, staff lounge, offices, and meeting rooms; • Camper Cabins: 13 camper cabins, each consisting of 1,930 sq. ft. with two bunkrooms and two bathrooms; • Head Counselor Cabins: three cabins of 441 sq. ft. each; • Arts Pavilion: a 2,307 sq. ft. open-air shade structure for arts and crafts activities; • Parking Lot: a new 58-space parking lot adjacent to the Welcome Center; and • Landscaping: landscaping improvements around the new structures. Three housing trailers, two cottages, and a garage would be demolished to accommodate the new development. The Project would also require the removal of 74 trees, 15 of which are protected. The protected trees to be removed include nine coast live oaks, one sycamore, and five large ornamental trees that are classified as heritage trees. The heritage trees include four pepper trees and one eucalyptus tree. The Project would also encroach upon the protected zones of 67 trees, 42 of which are protected trees. These include 20 oaks, 18 sycamores, and four heritage-sized pepper trees. The total allowed number of camp attendees would increase from 472 (400 for Camp Alonim, 72 for the Brandeis Collegiate Institute) to 572 (500 for Camp Alonim, 72 for the Brandeis Collegiate Institute). The allowable number of events, which are presently limited to 15 days per year on Saturdays and Sundays with up to 300 attendees, would increase to the following: • up to 150 annual event days with attendance of up to 300 people; • up to ten annual event days with attendance of up to 500 people; and • up to six annual event days with attendance of up to 1,000 people. There would be no change to the maximum number of camp staff, which would remain at 200. Peppertree Lane, a private road, provides access to the camp. Peppertree Lane is the southern continuation of Tapo Canyon Road, a major thoroughfare in Simi Valley. Access would remain unchanged with the development of the Project. Water services are provided by the Brandeis-Bardin Mutual Water Company, which receives imported water through the Calleguas Municipal Water District. Wastewater is handled by the City of Simi Valley. As part of the Major Modification, the Conditional Use Permit’s scope will also be expanded to include authorization of all existing and proposed Brandeis-Bardin Mutual Water Company facilities. The proposed project would also extend the life of the Conditional Use Permit for the camp and associated uses. Presently, the Conditional Use Permit is set to expire in 2042. As proposed, the permit would be extended indefinitely and would not have an expiration date.
ceqa-a8edefaa1449c10158.crossStreets: Tapo Canyon Road and Guardian Street

ceqa-3227b9e9086e147e2e.name: Box Canyon Manhole and Road Improvements Project
ceqa-3227b9e9086e147e2e.projectTitle: Box Canyon Manhole and Road Improvement Project
ceqa-3227b9e9086e147e2e.description: The Project involves infrastructure upgrades and maintenance activities along the Box Canyon access road, which serves as a critical component of the City of Thousand Oaks Public Works Department wastewater conveyance system. The purpose of the Project is to improve long-term access for maintenance vehicles, improve side canyon drainage transport across the access road, and ensure the continued reliability of the City's wastewater infrastructure. Proposed improvements include the installation of a new manhole and replacement of approximately ten (10) feet of existing asbestos cement (AC) eight (8) - inch diameter wastewater piping at the proposed manhole structure to facilitate maintenance and inspection of the wastewater system, and the concrete paving of approximately 260 linear feet of roadway segment of the existing, steep unpaved access road to provide stable, year-round access. To address stormwater management and erosion control, the Project also includes the installation of five (5) new 18-inch storm drain pipelines across the unpaved access road, each with upstream and downstream headwalls, as well as the construction of three (3) additional upstream headwalls for three (3) existing storm drain culverts.

Agricultural cargo container (AG container #1) • 160 sq. ft. Agricultural cargo container (AG container # 2) In 2016 approximately 0.17 acres of Bigpod Ceanothus-Chamise Shrubland was cleared without a permit. The vegetation was removed to construct one of the plastic shade wood frame structures. After the 2018 Woosley fire, the agricultural land use was expanded in various locations. Approximately 0.30 acres of Bigpod Ceanothus-Chamise Shrubland, 0.13 acres of Bigpod Ceanothus Chaparral, and 0.18 acres of California Sagebrush-Ashy Buckwhet Shrubland was removed without a permit. The Permittee will be required to mitigate 0.78 acres of Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Areas (ESHA) at a 2:1 Ratio (1.56 acres total). ceqa-9b9343a157a34666fe.name: Ventura County Transportation Commission – Sespe Creek Railroad Bridge Reconstruction Project (CESA Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2025-078-05 (ITP)
ceqa-9b9343a157a34666fe.projectTitle: Ventura County Transportation Commission – Sespe Creek Railroad Bridge Reconstruction Project (CESA Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2025-078-05 (ITP)
ceqa-9b9343a157a34666fe.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, South Coast Region 5
ceqa-9b9343a157a34666fe.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 5 - South Coast, San Diego
ceqa-9b9343a157a34666fe.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has issued an ITP (No. 2081-2025-078-05), pursuant to Section 2081(b) of the Fish and Game Code to the Ventura County Transportation Commission. The Project includes repair of the railroad bridge over Sespe Creek through the out-of-kind replacement of two bridge spans and two bents (piers). Project activities include removal of damaged/washed away bridge elements; creek diversion and dewatering; construction of diversion dams; installation of new bridge spans, an associated abutment with wingwalls, bents, piles, and associated pile caps, rock slope protection, and a temporary access ramp; slope stabilization; use of temporary work areas within the creek; removal of damaged bridge elements/materials; site restoration and erosion control; and other activities. The Project will result in impacts to 1.59 acres of southern California steelhead (Oncorhynchus mykiss) habitat including temporary impacts to 1.54 acres; the Project will permanently remove 0.05 acres of southern California steelhead habitat. The Project is expected to result in incidental take of southern California steelhead, which is/are designated as an endangered species under the California Endangered Species Act (CESA). The ITP referenced above as issued by CDFW authorizes incidental take of species listed under CESA that may occur as a result of Project implementation.

ceqa-c9386a0085da44c98c.description: The project consists of construction and operation of a new aboveground water storage tank (the Crown Hill Tank) and associated piping and electrical infrastructure. ceqa-8642154c90743a7a08.name: Arroyo Simi Sewer Crossing Replacement Project (Specification No. WW26-24, Project No. P6032994)
ceqa-8642154c90743a7a08.projectTitle: Arroyo Simi Sewer Crossing Replacement Project (Specification No. WW26-24, Project No. P6032994)
ceqa-8642154c90743a7a08.description: Ventura County Waterworks Division No. 1 is proposing to replace a concrete-encased 8-inch sewer line that crossed Arroyo Simi in the City of Moorpark, CA. The concrete-encased sewer line became exposed after several years of erosion and was washed out as a result of the high stream flows generated during the December 24-27, 2025 storms event. The Project consists of installing two, 9-inch diameter High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) wastewater pipelines in inverted siphon configurations to a maximum depth of approximately 50 feet below the Arroyo Simi. Additionally, five precast concrete manholes will be installed to connect the new dual siphon system to the existing sewer line. The HDD borings entry location will occur approximately 20 feet south of the Arroyo Simi southern access road on the right of way owned by the Ventura County Watershed Protection District (VCWPD). The borings that exit temporary construction staging area will be approximately 590 linear feet downstream (west), on VCWPD fee parcel north of the Arroyo Simi northern access road. The existing 132 linear foot sewer line and manhole which connected to the damaged sewer line will be plugged using a slack slurry concrete mixture and abandoned in place. No concrete will enter the Arroyo Simi through the abandoned pipe sections. All work, excavation, and access will be conducted outside of Arroyo Simi and jurisdictional areas. No new permanent impacts to jurisdictions areas would occur as a result of the Project. The proposed actions are necessary to maintain safety and service to the public in this area, including more than 150 homes in the Peach Hill Neighborhood of Moorpark.
ceqa-8642154c90743a7a08.crossStreets: Leta Yancy Road and Arroyo Simi

ceqa-5797cd84584f58b060.description: The California Department of Parks and Recreation (State Parks) is a Responsible Agency for this project under CEQA. ceqa-ca739b808815d61653.description: The Conditional Use Permit (CUP) is approved for a 30 year term for the Rental and Leasing of Durable Goods and a Planned Development (PD) Permit is approved for Warehousing and Storage on an undeveloped, 2.25 acre portion of APN 090-0-110-300. The sales of durable goods are allowed as an accessory use to the principal use of renting and leasing durable goods (primarily scaffolding and construction equipment). The PD Permit authorizes the construction and use of a new building for the rental, leasing, and sales of durable goods and for warehousing and storage. The project includes the following components: 1) Construction of an approximately 16,938 sq. ft. (gross floor area) warehouse building with storage area, offices, conference room, restroom facilities, and mezzanine storage; 2) Construction of an approximately 267 sq. ft. trash enclosure; 3) Construction of a new 8-foot-tall masonry screening wall with entrance gate; 4) Construction of a segment of County Drive in accordance with County Road Plate B-3S[C]; 5) Proposed establishment of an approximately 33,870 sq. ft. outdoor storage, sales, and display area sited to the rear of the proposed warehouse. Items stored in the outdoor storage, sales, and display area shall not exceed 15 feet in height; 6) Installation of landscaping, parking areas, and other improvements as detailed on the proposed site plans and in the final conditions of approval for the project; and, 7) Installation of security measures (video surveillance and lighting). The proposed standing, pole-mounted lighting fixtures will be 30 feet tall (maximum), and all lighting must comply with the Ventura County Non-Coastal Zoning Ordinance (NCZO) lighting standards. The proposed hours of operation are Monday through Friday from 4:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and Saturdays from 5:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. The facility will be closed on Sunday. The following additional operational details are proposed: • 25 new employees. A maximum of 20 employees will work for/in the warehousing and the remaining five employees would work in the office for rental/leasing/sales of durable goods use. • 20 customer trips per day • 40 truck trips per day The existing masonry wall along the western/northwestern property line that will remain and reduce truck noise generated by the proposed project is nine and one-half feet tall as measured from the grade of the project site and is eight feet tall as measured from the neighboring property which is at a higher grade. A maximum of three trucks running simultaneously between 4:00 a.m. and 6:00 a.m. on or adjacent to the project site are allowed. Additionally, project-related truck travel is limited to County Drive to/from Los Angeles Avenue/SR 118. To avoid truck travel through the nearby residential area, truck travel into or west of the intersection of Amapola Avenue and Rosal Lane is prohibited. To identify and protect potential cultural resources, the applicant will retain a cultural monitor to monitor the following specific development activities during the construction phase of the proposed project: • For all development between 0 – 3 inches in depth, no monitoring will be provided. • For all development between 3 inches and 18 inches in depth, the applicant will notify the cultural monitor at least 24 hours before work begins and will invite the monitor to observe the development work on-site. The monitor will be able to determine if continued monitoring will be provided for the duration of work between 18 inches and 36 inches in depth. • For all development below 3 feet in depth, the applicant will hire a cultural monitor to determine whether sensitive Native soils would be impacted. If any cultural resources are uncovered during ground disturbance or construction activities, the cultural monitor and any construction-related personnel must stop work and comply with the Archaeological Resources Discovered During Grading condition. Ventura Water currently provides water to the project site. The applicant will implement reasonable water conservation measures including, but not limited to, low flow fixtures and equipment to minimize the proposed project's water demand. Saticoy Sanitary District currently provides sewage disposal service. For any required new water and sewage disposal services, the proposed project is conditioned to obtain the appropriate approvals from Ventura Water and the Saticoy Sanitary District. A paved driveway from the project site to County Drive will provide access to the project site.

ceqa-3782c3997bdc51488d.name: Oxnard Fire Station No. 2 Project
ceqa-3782c3997bdc51488d.description: The Project involves the demolition of the existing 4,145-square-foot fire station and adjoining community garden, and the construction of a 12,585-square-foot (gross) new fire station. The fire station would include a separate 312-square-foot trash enclosure, a 180 square-foot earthquake storage enclosure, a 68-square-foot sand storage, and a 54-square-foot hose drying tower. This new fire station would support the daily operation of the OFD in its existing Station 2 location to continue to serve the nearby neighborhoods, upgrading the facility to a larger, more modern space to better suit the OFD's needs. The fire station would include a single-story apparatus bay designed to accommodate two fire engines and one ladder truck. Adjacent to the large apparatus area are support spaces like turnouts where the firefighters would store firefighting equipment, a decontamination (decon) room where they would clean their gear and themselves, a shop space for equipment cleaning and repair of equipment and tools, an EMS storage room for required medical supplies, a restroom, and miscellaneous utility rooms that would support the fire station. The building would also provide living quarters to accommodate up to 10 fire personnel per shift, which would include separate bunk rooms, restrooms, a kitchen, laundry facilities, dining room, day room (living room), an outdoor staff patio, and a fitness room. In addition, an open office space would be included to provide workspaces for fire personnel. The majority of the remainder of the Project Site would be paved to provide parking and circulation, and would include a fueling station for the fire apparatus, earthquake storage building, hose drying tower, and emergency generator located north of the fire station building. A trash enclosure would be provided near the northeastern corner of the Project Site. Landscape would be provided around the perimeter of the site, adjacent to Cloyne Street and East Pleasant Valley Road. The fire station would have a maximum height of 29 feet and 8 inches; and would be designed to include a hose drying tower with a maximum height of 31 feet.

ceqa-14a13726a0e915583b.name: Emergency Ventura River Bank Repair and Protection for NYE Well #8
ceqa-14a13726a0e915583b.projectTitle: Emergency Ventura River Bank Repair and Protection for NYE Well #8
ceqa-14a13726a0e915583b.description: In late December 2025, a strong winter storm hit the Ventura area, with heavy rainfall totaling over 17 inches of rain in the upper Ventura River Watershed in a 4-day period. After the subsequent storm in early January, over 25 inches of rain had fallen in the upper watershed in a 2-week period. This deluge of precipitation caused high flows in the Ventura River that staff later discovered had eroded approximately 30 feet of bank adjacent to the City’s water production well, Nye Well #8. This erosion damaged existing rip rap protecting Nye Well #8, and the bank erosion is putting Nye Well #8 at risk of severe damage or total loss should another large storm event or high river flows occur, and emergency construction work is needed to repair the bank and protect the well. Construction will adjust the location of a secondary high-flow channel that has scoured the western bank, relocating the secondary channel further into the middle of the floodplain. Native riverbed material between the new channel location and the eroded bank will be used to rebuild the bank. Rip rap will be placed along the rebuilt bank to prevent erosion. Native riverbed material from within the relocated channel area will be used to cover the rip rap, and re-establish more gradual bank contours, restoring the bank condition. Re-vegetation is anticipated to include seeding with a native pallet, and erosion control measures will be placed along the bank.

ceqa-4e44d5f28600a374f0.description: The Department of Fish and Wildlife is issuing a permit to the MBC Aquatic Sciences pursuant to Fish and Game Code Section 2081(a) for scientific purposes. The Section 2081(a) permit authorizes the applicant to take steelhead trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) during the course of sampling, subject to terms and conditions set forth in the permit. The purpose of this sampling is for the Ventura Water Reclamation Facility’s monitoring surveys for their National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit No. CA0064726. The Section 2081(a) permit authorizes the applicant to potentially capture steelhead trout during surveys. The applicant will conduct year-round monitoring surveys for NPDES permit No. CA0064726 using bottom trawl, hook & line – baited dropper loop, hook & line – swimbait, and fish traps through December 31, 2029.

ceqa-27db52ec1307111034.name: Costco Parking Lot Addition
ceqa-27db52ec1307111034.description: The application proposes the addition of a new parking area to the Costco development. This parking area is currently a separate parcel on the corner of Paseo Mercado and Ventura Blvd, currently developed with a building that formerly was a Burger King. The building is proposed to be demolished. For the new parcel to maximize parking and better fit into the existing parking areas adjacent to the site, which share access, a majority of the existing parking spaces on site will be shifted to better align with adjacent parking and access ways. New parking spaces will also be developed on site. To align with the parking changes, the property lines will also shift, so that no parking spaces are left bisected by a property line. In addition to parking modifications, there is a significant amount of proposed landscaping. The property will remain subdivided from the primary development, however, the new Costco parking space total will rise to 828 spaces from 766.

ceqa-f0a3f9ec430e9d14c8.name: C3. Electric Reefer Plugs
ceqa-f0a3f9ec430e9d14c8.agency: Oxnard Harbor District – Port of Hueneme
ceqa-f0a3f9ec430e9d14c8.description: The proposed project consists of the installation of additional electric refrigerated container (reefer) plug infrastructure at the District's South Terminal, where refrigerated containerized cargo operations occur on a daily basis. Reefer plugs are specialized electrical connections that supply power to refrigerated 40-foot cargo containers. The purpose of the project is to expand the Port's capacity to support refrigerated cargo operations and maintain the cold chain for containerized fresh produce following offloading from ocean-going vessels. Increasing the number of available reefer plugs will enhance operational efficiency and flexibility at the terminal and allow the Port to better accommodate current and projected cargo volumes.

ceqa-7d8f94d74747cfec9e.name: VIG-based Residential Retrofits to Demonstrate Enhanced Efficiency and Comfort
ceqa-7d8f94d74747cfec9e.projectTitle: VIG-based Residential Retrofits to Demonstrate Enhanced Efficiency and Comfort
ceqa-7d8f94d74747cfec9e.description: This project will demonstrate the performance and benefits of vacuum insulated glass (VIG) windows via laboratory testing, thermal modeling and field demonstration. The project will also explore improvements in VIG value propositions, address cost and durability concerns, and develop a plan for broad market adoption. The project is partnering with major VIG and window manufacturers to develop and demonstrate high-performance VIG solutions in single-family and multi-family residential buildings. This demonstration will use 2 installation methods, a full replacement and a retrofit using the existing window frame.

ceqa-095470fe10d22682ae.name: Lower Olive Grove Restroom Repair Project
ceqa-095470fe10d22682ae.projectTitle: Lower Olive Grove Restroom Repair Project
ceqa-095470fe10d22682ae.description: The Lower Olive Grove Restroom at the Lake Piru Recreation Area, owned and operated by United Water Conservation District (District), needs repair to restore the original functionality of the facility. The drain system within the restroom regularly backs up and floods the restroom. The existing wall-mounted toilets are damaged at the connection to the wall. To address these deficiencies, a repair project has been proposed to repair the facility. Constructed in 1970, the restroom is situated within the Olive Grove campsite and is one of two restrooms and shower facilities serving the site. The work will consist of replacing all nine wall-mounted toilets and repairing the damaged wall connections. In addition, the original cast iron drainpipes within the floor slab will be excavated and replaced. Most of the drainpipe requiring replacement is located within the existing structure and approximately 25 feet of sewer pipe and 11 feet of sidewalk outside the facility also require replacement. The restroom repair will not increase the capacity of the existing facility. These repairs are restricted to restoring the original functionality of the restroom.

ceqa-fbd7d69cfe3dd9c9f7.name: Box Canyon Manhole and Road Improvement Project
ceqa-fbd7d69cfe3dd9c9f7.projectTitle: Box Canyon Manhole and Road Improvement Project
ceqa-fbd7d69cfe3dd9c9f7.description: The Project is located within the City of Thousand Oaks and lies primarily within the Arroyo Conejo Open Space area. The Project involves infrastructure upgrades and maintenance activities along the Box Canyon access road, which serves as a critical component of the City of Thousand Oaks (City) Public Works Department wastewater conveyance system. The purpose of the Project is to improve long-term access for maintenance vehicles, improve side canyon drainage transport across the access road, and ensure the continued reliability of the City's wastewater infrastructure. Proposed improvements include the installation of a new manhole and replacement of approximately ten feet of existing asbestos cement eight - inch diameter wastewater piping at the proposed manhole structure to facilitate maintenance and inspection of the wastewater system, and the concrete paving of approximately 260 linear feet of roadway segment of the existing, steep unpaved access road to provide stable, year-round access. To address stormwater management and erosion control, the Project also includes the installation of five new 18-inch storm drain pipelines across the unpaved access road, each with upstream and downstream headwalls, as well as the construction of three additional upstream headwalls for three existing storm drain culverts.
ceqa-fbd7d69cfe3dd9c9f7.crossStreets: Calle Las Trancas and Calle Pecos

ceqa-012611e0dd86d64091.description: The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), pursuant to authority granted under California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 22, Division 4.5, Chapter 20, Sec. 66270.61, has issued an Emergency Permit to the Teledyne Scientific Company, (EPA ID# CAD059221036) to treat hazardous wastes through a controlled reaction with chemical solutions. Specifically, one (1) 1-liter container of Diethyl Ether and one (1) 4-liter container of Tetrahydrofuran must be stabilized prior to transport to an authorized hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facility. These chemicals are currently being stored at Teledyne Scientific Company located at 1049 Camino Dos Rios, Thousand Oaks, California 91360. DTSC has determined as a safety precaution to prevent an accident or severe injury, an Emergency Permit should be issued to chemically stabilize the hazardous wastes prior to storage and eventual transportation off-site by Clean Harbors Environmental Services (Clean Harbors).

ceqa-c2b201936e8895280b.name: Downtown Thousand Oaks Project
ceqa-c2b201936e8895280b.description: The approximately 17.68-acre proposed project site is generally located at 2100 East Thousand Oaks Boulevard; refer to Exhibit 2, Site Vicinity. The project site is currently designated Institutional and Commercial Neighborhood, and zoned SP-11 and SP-20; refer to Exhibit 3, Existing Land Use Designations. The site is specifically bound by Thousand Oaks Boulevard and commercial uses (i.e., Saremi and Johnstone Dentistry) to the north, Conejo School Road and commercial uses (i.e., The Lakes shopping center) to the east, Highway 101 to the south, and Oakwood Drive, commercial uses (i.e., Enhanced Landscape, a private landscape company), and single-family residential uses to the west. The site is located within the Civic Arts Specific Plan (SP-11) and Thousand Oaks Boulevard Specific Plan (SP-20), and consists of three public right-of-way segments (i.e., Thousand Oaks Boulevard, Dallas Drive, and Oakwood Drive). The proposed project would use the parking facilities at 265 South Rancho Road and 110 South Conejo School Road for satellite parking during peak demand times. These locations would also be utilized for off-site construction laydown areas. The proposed project involves a General Plan Amendment to change the land use designation of a 5.33-acre portion of the project area to Mixed-Use and increase the height within that area, refer to Exhibit 4, Proposed Land Use Designations; amendment of the Civic Arts Plaza Specific Plan (SP No. 11) to facilitate development of a new pedestrian-oriented downtown, including mixed-use residential, a hotel, commercial, office, and entertainment uses; partial reconstruction of the existing City Hall; public amenities such as a park plaza and outdoor amphitheater; and supporting infrastructure, including new roadways, reconfigured utilities, and stormwater management improvements; a Tentative Tract Map consolidating 14 existing parcels into 9 new lots; a Development Permit for construction of four new buildings, including a seven-story, 142-key hotel; a seven-story, 161-unit mixed-use building (26 affordable units) with subterranean garage; a four-story, 79-unit mixed-use building (13 affordable units) with subterranean garage; a two-story restaurant building; and a public park with a children’s play structure, splash pad, interactive play equipment, informal stages and seating areas, and flexible open space; a Special Use Permit for the sale and consumption of alcohol; and a Protected Tree Permit for the removal and replacement of protected trees, as well as the encroachment into the protected zone of protected trees. The proposed project would be constructed in five phases, (refer to Exhibit 5, Phasing Plan) which are anticipated to commence in 2027 and be completed by 2032.

ceqa-b1611e48b353257fa6.description: The State Water Resources Control Board (State Water Board) is a Responsible Agency for the Project. The State Water Board is funding the Project referred to internally as Laguna Vista Elementary School Water Treatment Improvement Project. The proposed Project to be funded by the State Water Board includes modifying the Laguna Vista Elementary School Water System by installing an 8,000-gallon storage tank, associated piping, and a new chlorine injection and monitoring system; disconnecting two 14,000-gallon tanks from the service line to the School; installing two point-of-entry treatment systems to provide filtered water to the kitchen, nurse’s station, teacher’s lounge, and water fountains in common areas throughout the School; and installing approximately 900 to 2,000 feet of new one-inch pipe to convey treated water to the above-listed locations. ceqa-814bb920964f1e1e75.name: COSCA Invasive Plant Management Plan
ceqa-814bb920964f1e1e75.description: The COSCA Invasive Plant Management Plan (IPMP) has been prepared to guide and assist COSCA land managers in carrying out invasive plant management activities as part of fulfilling the agency’s commitment to protect and enhance natural resources. This IPMP will address the management of invasive plant species on 13,000 acres under COSCA ownership and management, and open space lands owned by the Conejo Recreation and Park District (CRPD) (Figure 1). Guidance presented in this IPMP will facilitate strategic control of invasive plants and ensure that available financial resources are utilized when and where they will yield optimal value for the recovery and enhancement of native plant communities and wildlife habitats. The IPMP describes existing conditions in the Plan area, identifies target invasive plant species to be controlled, and establishes treatment priorities. It also describes management goals and methods, infestation prevention and management strategies, monitoring and reporting protocols, adaptive management techniques, and best management practices to avoid environmental impacts.

ceqa-c4ad650f10c5b51e41.description: The project includes replacement of 125 existing polybutylene water services lines with copper tubing, installing 125 cathodic protection systems, removing and reinstalling 54 valves. The polubutylene service is prone to degradation from chlorine exposure, microfracturing, and sudden failures and replacing aging infrastructure with durable copper and corrosion protection, the work will significantly enhance water system reliability and service for residents.

ceqa-082a0b46db09ed904c.name: The Santa Susana Field Laboratory Site Remediation Program National Aeronautics and Space Administration Groundwater Phase 1 CMS and Statement of Basis
ceqa-082a0b46db09ed904c.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-082a0b46db09ed904c.description: The Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) has approved the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Final Phase 1 Groundwater Corrective Measures Study (Phase 1 GW CMS) dated January 4, 2024 and released the Final DTSC Statement of Basis (SB) dated January 2026 for the NASA Phase 1 GW CMS and selection of final remedies for the four Target Treatment Areas (TTAs) of groundwater and bedrock vapor contamination at the NASA administered federal property at the Santa Susana Field Laboratory (SSFL). The final remedy for the cleanup of contaminated groundwater and bedrock at the SSFL is being conducted under the 2007 Consent Order for Corrective Action between DTSC and the SSFL Responsible Parties (NASA, the U.S. Department of Energy, and The Boeing Company). The treatment technologies selected to address high concentrations of trichloroethene (TCE) and its breakdown products in groundwater and bedrock vapor in the TTAs include groundwater pump and treat, enhanced in-situ bioremediation, and bedrock vapor extraction.?DTSC will also oversee the implementation of monitored natural attenuation and a land use covenant to restrict land use. The NASA Phase 1 Groundwater cleanup is part of the overall program for soil and groundwater remediation activities and the removal of structures under DTSC oversight at the approximately 2,850-acre SSFL site, as described in the Final Program Environmental Impact Report certified on July 19, 2023. The overall program will be implemented through DTSC’s issuance of individual decision documents associated with remediation plans prepared by the Responsible Parties.

ceqa-33aec1c9ff8cf3b0d1.name: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, Oxnard College, Oxnard, California
ceqa-33aec1c9ff8cf3b0d1.projectTitle: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, Oxnard College, Oxnard, California
ceqa-33aec1c9ff8cf3b0d1.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-33aec1c9ff8cf3b0d1.description: The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), pursuant to authority granted under California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 22, Division 4.5, Chapter 20, Sec. 66270.61, has issued an Emergency Permit to Oxnard College, (EPA ID# CAD982034191) to treat hazardous waste through a controlled reaction with chemical solutions. Specifically, one (1) 3-ounce container of Picric Acid and one (1) 12-ounce container of Potassium must be stabilized prior to transport to an authorized hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facility. These chemicals are currently being stored at Oxnard College located at 4000 S. Rose Avenue, Oxnard, California 93033. DTSC has determined as a safety precaution to prevent an accident or severe injury, an Emergency Permit should be issued for Clean Harbors Environmental Services (Clean Harbors) to chemically stabilize the hazardous waste prior to storage and eventual transportation off-site.

ceqa-3c58aed2ca06bd8f1c.name: Supplemental Environmental Impact Report for Focused Update to the Piru Area Plan
ceqa-3c58aed2ca06bd8f1c.projectTitle: Supplemental Environmental Impact Report for Focused Update to the Piru Area Plan
ceqa-3c58aed2ca06bd8f1c.description: The Ventura County Public Works Agency received a request to evaluate the reduced parking on the west side of Main Street between Via Fustero and Sacramento Street, along with the need for a dedicated left turn pocket located on northbound Main Street for access to the Fillmore Piru Citrus Association packing plant. These improvements, along with the removal of the center concrete median at the southern leg of the intersection of Main Street and Via Fustero required by mitigation measure T-5 from the 2006 Focused Update to the Piru Area Plan EIR, were recently installed as part of the residential housing developments along Main Street. Between the concrete median and left turn pocket, a painted center median was installed, which serves as an area to permit northbound and southbound left turns without disrupting the flow of the respective through traffic. Pursuant to Section 15163(b) of the CEQA Guidelines, the Draft SEIR will contain only the information necessary to make the previous EIR adequate for the project as revised, which includes the elimination of the center concrete median at the southern leg of the intersection of Main Street and Via Fustero (EIR mitigation measure T-5). The elimination of the center concrete median will result in the following physical improvements that are provided for informational purposes only, and are not the subject of the Draft SEIR. • Removal of the painted two-way left turn pocket which was formed between the aforementioned concrete median and left turn lane • Restoration of the parallel parking along the western side of Main Street between Via Fustero and Sacramento Street; and • Elimination of the northbound left turn lane into the packing plant.
ceqa-3c58aed2ca06bd8f1c.crossStreets: Main St between Via Fustero and Sacramento St

ceqa-42f32e5f642248751c.name: OLD TELEGRAPH RD BRIDGE NO 485 EMERGENCY REPAIRS - PROJECT NO. P6X50688
ceqa-42f32e5f642248751c.projectTitle: OLD TELEGRAPH RD BRIDGE NO 485 EMERGENCY REPAIRS - PROJECT NO. P6X50688
ceqa-42f32e5f642248751c.description: The storm event that occurred in December 2025 caused extensive damage to the northwest abutment of the bridge. As a result of the high storm flows, erosion occurred at the abutment, exposing three steel beam piles and compromising the structural stability of the bridge. The purpose of this emergency project is to repair the damaged abutment, restore structural integrity, and reopen the bridge to the public as soon as practicable. The proposed work will consist of repairing the scoured abutment foundation through the installation of rock slope protection to stabilize the area, prevent further erosion, and protect the exposed piles from future storm events. These repairs are necessary to ensure the long-term safety and functionality of the bridge and to prevent additional damage during future storm events.

ceqa-e6df9e31db0a510c0e.projectTitle: REEVES ROAD EMERGENCY REPAIRS AT MP 0.25 - PROJECT NO. P6X50687
ceqa-e6df9e31db0a510c0e.description: As a result of the December 2025 storm flows, a portion of the south bank of Reeves Creek, along with the adjacent roadway, was washed out during the storm event. This damage has compromised the stability of the roadway and requires immediate emergency repairs. The proposed emergency work will include the placement of rock within and along the banks of Reeves Creek to stabilize the channel and prevent further erosion. In addition, the south bank will be reconstructed, and the affected portion of the roadway will be restored to reestablish safe and reliable access. These emergency measures are necessary to protect public safety and prevent additional damage during future storm events.

This Project will remove a fish passage barrier on Sisar creek and install an approximate 90-foot free span bridge to allow for volitional fish passage to upstream habitat for southern California steelhead (Oncorhynchus mykiss). CDFW has determined that the Project is a Qualifying Restoration Project pursuant to section 1671(d)(1) of the Fish and Game Code, and the Project is expected to result in a substantial, cumulative benefit to native fish and their habitat. This notice is to advise that CDFW issued the above-described RMP on the date signed below.

ceqa-03ece927bb15ee0256.name: 255-290 Maple Court Mixed-Use Project
ceqa-03ece927bb15ee0256.description: Project No. PROJ-25-0879 amends PROJ-22-0237 which was previously approved. The amended project would demolish 3 existing office buildings on-site to allow for the construction of 2 new mixed-use buildings with up to 224 multi-family residential unites and up to 2,020 square feet of ground-floor neighborhood-serving commercial uses on Lot 1 and construct a 59-unit for sale townhome development on Lot 2. Of the 238 residential units, 33 would be affordable units restricted to low-income households. The proposed residential units would comprise a mix of housing types, including market-rate and affordable apartments, or two-bedroom townhomes, ranging in size from 660 square feet to 1,700 square feet. Each of the buildings would include 3 levels of residentials units over 2 level of parking, lined with units and ground-floor commercial spaces. The project would also include private and common outdoor areas, up to 500 parking spaces, and landscaping and lighting improvements. Ground floor outdoor community paces would include a pedestrian paseo, gardens, seating areas, and a dog run. Given the project’s uses, density, and proximity to transit, it is considered a Transit Priority Project (TPP) per Senate Bill 373, and is eligible for streamlined CEQA analysis pursuant to Section 21155 of the Public Resources Code. The project requires the following discretionary actions from the City: (1) a Lot Line Adjustment pursuant to San Buenaventura Municipal Code (SBMC) Section 26.100.410, to adjust the property lines from the existing 3 legal parcels to 2 parcels, proposed as Lot 1 and Lot 2; (2) a Planned Development Permit (PD-08-25-0026),m pursuant to SBMC Section 24.234.050.3(a) and SBMC Chapter 24.525, to allow for the proposed multi-family residential buildings; (3) a Major Design Review (MDR-8-25-0063), pursuant to SBMC Section 24.545.030.1, for a proposed development of 5 or more residential units; and (4) Tentative Tract Map (TTM-08-25-0008) pursuant to SBMC Section 26.100. The original Project No. PROJ-22-0237 was analyzed under a Sustainable Communities Environmental Assessment (SCEA; State Clearinghouse No. 2024081121) (Attachment E, Exhibit 3 and PROJ-25-0879 Page 17 of 17), adopted by the City Council on April 8, 2025. In accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), an Addendum to the Adopted SCEA was prepared to analyze the proposed revisions to the Original Project and demonstrates that 1) these proposed revisions do not changed the Adopted SCEA’s conclusions regarding potential environmental effects and 2) no supplemental or subsequent environmental review is required for the Revised Project pursuant to the CEQA Guidelines Sections 151629.

ceqa-cf0d8c098e6e7db296.name: Ventura River Watershed Riparian Resilience Watershed Project (Project), California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) Restoration Management Permit Number
ceqa-cf0d8c098e6e7db296.projectTitle: Ventura River Watershed Riparian Resilience Program
ceqa-cf0d8c098e6e7db296.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, South Coast Region 5
ceqa-cf0d8c098e6e7db296.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 5 - South Coast, San Diego
ceqa-cf0d8c098e6e7db296.description: On January 13, 2026, CDFW issued the RMP pursuant to section 1670 et seq. of the Fish and Game Code to the Ventura County Resource Conservation District (District) for the Project. The Project includes management or propagation activities intended to benefit native fish, wildlife, plants, or their habitat, or a combination thereof. The Project includes the physical removal of invasive plant species and active revegetation with native riparian plant species throughout the Ventura River Watershed. The Project is expected to increase community resilience of native riparian habitat and benefit multiple native species that are listed under the federal Endangered Species Act or California Endangered Species Act, including southern California steelhead (Oncorhynchus mykiss), least Bell’s vireo (Vireo bellii pusillus), and Crotch’s bumble bee (Bombus crotchii).

ceqa-ceb4bf8f75cc3932bf.projectTitle: Medea Creek Maintenance Project #1 (Notification of Streambed Alteration, No. EPIMS-VEN-48802-R5)
ceqa-ceb4bf8f75cc3932bf.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, South Coast Region 5
ceqa-ceb4bf8f75cc3932bf.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 5 - South Coast, San Diego
ceqa-ceb4bf8f75cc3932bf.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has amended Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. EPIMS-VEN-48802-R5, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to Rancho Simi Recreation and Park District. The Project is limited to the removal of deadwood, debris, and invasive plant species from Medea Creek. Project activities will be conducted by crews operating on foot and using hand tools. Vegetation and debris will be removed by hand-pulling, cutting, and direct application of herbicide. Non-native trees will be cut into several sections and carefully lowered to the ground by crew members. The remaining stumps will be retained and herbicide will be applied directly to the cut stump. Invasive plants will be removed off-site and disposed of at a landfill. Debris and deadwood material will be mulched and evenly spread across the Project area outside of the stream banks.

ceqa-e4cc9c69ccb9ba07d4.description: The Subdivider requests that a TPM be granted and a PM be recorded to legalize the 14.35-acre parcel pursuant to CCC-8821 . The Subdivider is not proposing to reconfigure the lot lines or develop the site as a part of this TPM. Direct access to the site is provided by a 30-foot-wide private driveway to Burnham Road. Domestic water will be provided by the Ventura River Water District, pending approval from the Ventura Local Action Formation Commission (LAFCo) for annexation of the parcel into the District's service area1. The site has been used for animal husbandry for over 40 years and agriculture for the past 4 years, with developed areas on a riverine bluff above the Ventura River floodway consistently cleared of vegetation.

ceqa-2ac1288ab506142165.name: Food Share Ventura County
ceqa-2ac1288ab506142165.description: Food Share Ventura County is requesting to develop a new warehousing facility for food receiving, storage, and distribution. This development primarily consists of the construction of a new approximately 85,845 square feet of floor area), 49’9” high building. This would be accompanied by an enclosed shipping and receiving yard with loading docks, canopies, a trash enclosure, and a bin washing and storage area. The proposed development includes the following uses: administrative offices, conference/meeting areas, and a commercial kitchen to prepare meals for distribution. The property will have solar shade structures covering 84 of the 178 proposed parking stalls, as well as landscape and hardscape improvements, which include an employee outdoor amenity area and a fruit orchard. ceqa-a809b3b42ea0b1572d.name: New Installation and Upgrades of Streamgaging Systems Project (CalSIP)
ceqa-a809b3b42ea0b1572d.projectTitle: New Installation and Upgrades of Streamgaging Systems Project (CalSIP)
ceqa-a809b3b42ea0b1572d.description: The purpose of the project is to upgrade existing stream gaging infrastructure at three sites and install one new gaging station which will contribute to important flow data as a part of the California stream gage network. Watershed Protection District (WPD) has been awarded grant funding through the Stream Gage Improvement Program (CalSlP) to conduct the improvements. Work involves no new maintenance in the streams, less than 10 square feet of concrete footing and bollards installed in previously disturbed areas, little to no vegetation removal or trimming, and no damage to scenic resources. No substantive increase in maintenance or site visits would occur for the existing stations; monthly to quarterly gage visits for data collection and gage maintenance would occur for the new site at Santa Clara River. The work falls under Categorical Exemption Article 19, Section 15301, Class 1 and Section 15304, Class 4.

ceqa-fe1057b344224677b4.name: State Abandonment of Orphan Wells Project – Phase 2: Oxnard
ceqa-fe1057b344224677b4.projectTitle: State Abandonment of Orphan Wells Project – Phase 2: Oxnard
ceqa-fe1057b344224677b4.description: The proposed project consists of the plug and abandonment (P&A) of four existing orphan oil and gas wells in Ventura County as part of CalGEM’s State Abandonment Program. The proposed work involves well abandonment and decommissioning tanks and other production-related facilities attendant to the wells. For well abandonment, each well would be cleaned out and then plugged with cement and inert mud to surface. After abandonment, the well head would be removed, and any remaining well casings and surface conductors would be cut to just above the bay floor. Once the well bay is clean, it would have suitable fill placed and compacted. The well bay would be encapsulated with impermeable concrete to seal the bay area. These wells are generally situated within an established oil field in an industrial and agricultural setting. CalGEM has approved a task order for its contractor to perform the proposed work on the wells listed below. Notices of Intention will be issued to the contractor for administrative purposes only and do not constitute a discretionary approval. API # Well Name 0411121969 Lenox Ranch 101H 0411121971 Lenox Ranch 104H 0411121991 Lenox Ranch 107H 0411121984 Lenox Ranch 108H Exempt Status: As the Lead Agency, CalGEM has determined that the proposed project is exempt from full environmental review requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to the specified exemptions marked in the section below. CalGEM further finds that the proposed project would not result in a significant adverse impact to the environment, or that any of the exceptions to the application of the exemptions apply (14 CCR § 15300.2).

ceqa-833a9b1d02d44f2617.name: California Coastal Commission's Suggested Modifications to County-lnitiated Amendments to Articles 1, 2, 4, 5, and 11 of the Ventura County Coastal Zoning Ordin
ceqa-833a9b1d02d44f2617.projectTitle: California Coastal Commission's Suggested Modifications to County-lnitiated Amendments to Articles 1, 2, 4, 5, and 11 of the Ventura County Coastal Zoning Ordin
ceqa-833a9b1d02d44f2617.description: On October 8,2025, the California Coastal Commission conditionally approved Ordinance No. 4640, which consists of amendments to the Ventura County Coastal Zoning Ordinance (CZO) pertaining to transitional and supportive housing, residential care facilities, density bonus, and reasonable accommodations (collectively, the CZO Amendments), subject to the following suggested modifications: . Modification to CZO Section 8175-5.22.3.1 to change the required permit for supportive housing projects that qualify as a use by right from a Zoning Clearance to a ministerial Coastal Development Permit (CDP), approved by the Planning Director, without a public hearing; and to require consistency with the objective requirements of the Local Coastal Program. . Modification to CZO Section 8175-6.2 to remove a provision that would have prohibited the waiver, reduction or modification of specific coastal resource protection development regulations, unless othen ruise required by state law. . Modifications to Article 11 of CZO to revise Section 8181-9.5 to address appeals of supportive housing applications to the Coastal Commission, and to add a new Section 8181-1 5 to address procedures for ministerial CDPs for supportive housing. On December 16, 2025, the Board of Supervisors adopted a resolution acknowledging receipt of, accepting, and agreeing to the Coastal Commission's suggested modifications and adopted the CZO Amendments, as modified. The Board-adopted ordinance is available online on the County's website at: https://cobpublic.venturacountv.qov/documents/Ordinances/County%o20o9/o20Ventura/ 46,6.pdf The CZO Amendments, as modified, shall become effective and operative 30 days after adoption by the Board of Supervisors, or upon certification by the California Coastal Commission, whichever is later.

ceqa-a4f1352bfb063f3c1a.name: American Jewish University - Camp Alonim Project
ceqa-a4f1352bfb063f3c1a.projectTitle: American Jewish University - Camp Alonim Project
ceqa-a4f1352bfb063f3c1a.description: The Project Applicant requests a Major Modification to Conditional Use Permit No. 1776 and a Discretionary Tree Permit be granted to authorize development of additional facilities at Camp Alonim. Proposed facilities include the following: • Welcome Center: a 4,460 sq. ft. building consisting of a lobby, staff lounge, offices, and meeting rooms; • Camper Cabins: 13 camper cabins, each consisting of 1,930 sq. ft. with two bunkrooms and two bathrooms; • Head Counselor Cabins: three cabins of 441 sq. ft. each; • Arts Pavilion: a 2,307 sq. ft. open-air shade structure for arts and crafts activities; • Parking Lot: a new 58-space parking lot adjacent to the Welcome Center; and • Landscaping: landscaping improvements around the new structures. Three housing trailers, two cottages, and a garage would be demolished to accommodate the new development. The Project would also require the removal of 74 trees, 15 of which are protected. The protected trees to be removed include nine coast live oaks, one sycamore, and five large ornamental trees that are classified as heritage trees. The heritage trees include four pepper trees and one eucalyptus tree. The Project would also encroach upon the protected zones of 67 trees, 42 of which are protected trees. These include 20 oaks, 18 sycamores, and four heritage-sized pepper trees. The total allowed number of camp attendees would increase from 472 (400 for Camp Alonim, 72 for the Brandeis Collegiate Institute) to 572 (500 for Camp Alonim, 72 for the Brandeis Collegiate Institute). The allowable number of events, which are presently limited to 15 days per year on Saturdays and Sundays with up to 300 attendees, would increase to the following: • up to 150 annual event days with attendance of up to 300 people; • up to ten annual event days with attendance of up to 500 people; and • up to six annual event days with attendance of up to 1,000 people. There would be no change to the maximum number of camp staff, which would remain at 200. Peppertree Lane, a private road, provides access to the camp. Peppertree Lane is the southern continuation of Tapo Canyon Road, a major thoroughfare in Simi Valley. Access would remain unchanged with the development of the Project. Water services are provided by the Brandeis-Bardin Mutual Water Company, which receives imported water through the Calleguas Municipal Water District. Wastewater is handled by the City of Simi Valley. As part of the Major Modification, the Conditional Use Permit’s scope will also be expanded to include authorization of all existing and proposed Brandeis-Bardin Mutual Water Company facilities. The proposed project would also extend the life of the Conditional Use Permit for the camp and associated uses. Presently, the Conditional Use Permit is set to expire in 2042. As proposed, the permit would be extended indefinitely and would not have an expiration date.
ceqa-a4f1352bfb063f3c1a.developmentType: Recreational (Summer camp with ancillary assembly and event uses)

The subject property covers approximately 2,400 acres and the demolition work is located on APN 685-0-051-180, a 403.35-acre parcel for tax purposes only. The demolition work is confined to the area identified as Area IV within APN 685-0-051-180. The following structures are proposed to be demolished: Building Label Type: 44-100 abandoned industrial bldg. 8,200 sq. ft. 44-055 abandoned industrial bldg. 13,300 sq. ft. 44-155 abandoned breakroom bldg. 490 sq. ft. 44-009 abandoned industrial bldg. 14,000 sq. ft. 44-11 abandoned industrial bldg. 4,500 sq. ft. Total: 40,490 sq. ft. The demolition involves the removal of the above ground portions of the five Boeing-owned building structures. No foundations will be removed, and no subsurface work will be performed. This project is not part of the California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) remediation project at SSFL, and neither DTSC nor the California Department of Public Health have authority over the removal of the structures. In addition, the structures to be removed are not part of Department of Energy (DOE) building removal project. This is not a federal action of any sort. Boeing previously received zoning clearances for other Boeing-owned structures in this area of SSFL from the County. Stormwater protection measures are illustrated on the submitted plans that show the use of erosion control fiber roll in certain areas around the demolition work.

ceqa-46d719466e5b2981e7.name: Agromin Composting and Soil Amendment Facility Major Modification to CUP 5001-1
ceqa-46d719466e5b2981e7.projectTitle: Agromin Composting and Soil Amendment Facility Major Modification to Conditional Use Permit 5001-1
ceqa-46d719466e5b2981e7.description: A Conditional Use Permit to operate a large-scale commercial organics processing and soil amendment operations on 11.44 acres consisting of the processing of wood waste and green materials feedstock into compost for the property located at 6859 Arnold Road. Operational activities include composting, screening, chipping and grinding, and storage activities related to the production of compost, compost feedstocks, and chipped and ground materials. The project includes the use of an existing 9,275 square foot (sq. ft.) packing building, an existing scale and scale house, portable toilets, mobile grinder, mobile trommel screen and mobile trommel shaker screen, an 858 sq. ft. open bin, and a 283 sq. ft. storage trailer. The annual facility throughput is a maximum 93,000 tons per year, and maximum storage volume of feedstock and compost allowed on-site is 12,500 cubic yards. All trucks, deliveries and employee traffic shall use Hueneme Road to Arnold Road, and utilize the existing facility entrance at Arnold Road. The use of Olds Road is prohibited. Average heavy-duty truck trip estimates for throughput at the facility shall consist of 72 one-way trips/day for materials transportation and four one-way trips/day for vendor deliveries. Average employee trips are 29 trips per day (includes 9 full time and 4 seasonal employees). The operation of the commercial organics processing operation use shall be limited to Monday through Saturday from 6:00AM to 6:30PM. Soil amendment operations shall be limited to 7 AM to 4:30 PM, Monday through Friday and 7 AM to 3 PM on Saturday. The facility shall be closed on Sunday. All products (e.g., compost or mulch) must be sold, given away, or beneficially used within 24 months of the facility’s acceptance of the raw material. Feedstock materials shall not be accepted at any time when the storage capacity of the site would be exceeded by such delivery. Only separated organic (originally derived from living organisms) materials shall be accepted at organics processing operations. Asbestos-containing waste material, infections waste, or hazardous wastes shall not knowingly be accepted. All incoming materials shall be inspected for contaminants, such as plastic, and all contaminants shall be removed to the greatest extent feasible before processing.

ceqa-de9aaae50e9f034881.name: Approval of Local Energy Efficiency and Conservation Standards Application Findings Submitted by the City of Ojai for the 2022 Energy Code Cycle
ceqa-de9aaae50e9f034881.projectTitle: Approval of Local Energy Efficiency and Conservation Standards Application Findings Submitted by the City of Ojai for the 2022 Energy Code Cycle
ceqa-de9aaae50e9f034881.description: The California Energy Commission (CEC) adopts and regularly updates regulations that define a process for local governments to apply to the CEC to make certain findings regarding locally adopted energy conservation or energy insulation standards (CCR, Title 24, Part 1, section 10-106 and section 10-110; Public Resources Code section 25402.1(h)(2)). The local government’s proposed standards are often referred to as the Local Reach Codes and require local governments submit an application to the CEC consistent with the requirements listed in section 10-106(b). Before the local standards may be enforced, the CEC must make two non-discretionary findings pursuant to PRC section 25402.1(h)(2) and as listed in section 10-106(a): 1) The proposed local standards will require the diminution of energy consumption levels compared to the 2022 Energy Code, and 2) The local government has filed the basis of its cost-effectiveness determination with the CEC. On September 18, 2025, the City of Ojai (the City) submitted an application to the CEC that included: 1) the basis of its determination that the locally adopted energy efficiency standards contained in Ordinance No. 968 are cost-effective; and (2) documentation that the locally adopted energy efficiency standards contained in Ordinance No. 968 will require the diminution of energy consumption levels compared to the 2022 Building Energy Efficiency Standards (Energy Code), as required by PRC section 25402.1(h)(2) and by CCR, Title 24, Part 1, section 10-106 (section 10-106). Based on the information submitted, staff analysis, and the Executive Director's recommendation, the CEC approved findings of the City’s section 10-106 application at the CEC’s November 12, 2025, Business Meeting.

ceqa-08e03e3a3d56bc019b.description: The applicant requests a Planned Development Permit to authorize the construction of a 1,296 square foot wood-frame, agricultural barn with a pole barn foundation, without plumbing or electrical, and to permit an existing, unpermitted 304-square-foot shed. Access to the site would be provided via private driveway connecting to Santa Paula Ojai Road. The project would be served by an onsite septic system provided by the Ventura County Regional Sanitation District, and water would be supplied by an onsite well.

ceqa-91a5d879059b1397e5.projectTitle: Conejo Recreation & Park District Master Plan Update
ceqa-91a5d879059b1397e5.description: The CRPD proposes to update the 2011 Master Plan and prepared an ND Addendum. The purpose of this project is to improve vehicle and bicycle travel and safety, improve the freight movement corridor, increase connectivity for bicycle riders, and complete vehicle and bicycle improvements consistent with the County's General Plan.

ceqa-54e13e9763c8c5a480.name: The Unit W Wastewater Interceptor Condition Assessment Project (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-VEN-26963-R5)
ceqa-54e13e9763c8c5a480.projectTitle: Unit W Wastewater Interceptor Condition Assessment
ceqa-54e13e9763c8c5a480.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has amended Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-VEN-26963-R5, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to The City of Thousand Oaks (Permittee), as represented by Nader Heydari. The Project is limited to assessing the internal condition of the Unit W Interceptor and replacing broken isolation valves. The Project consists of nine components: creation of four temporary culvert creek crossings clearing of an area for staging and valve replacement for structure W-A, temporary excavation for installation of pipe access tees in two areas, shapell lateral valve replacement, and structure W-D and W-1 valve replacement. In 2025, a storm blew out materials related to the four crossings. The Agreement was amended to include differing materials and methodology for the temporary creek crossings. No new impacts will occur and the new crossing materials will fully span the creek, no materials will be placed in the channel.

ceqa-2f06c680545d57b345.description: The proposed Project would include removal of Rincon Island's remaining surface structures and remediation of the Island’s contaminated soil and interstitial water, improvements to the State Coastal Conservancy parcel adjacent to the Rincon Island causeway landing/abutment, decommissioning of onshore pipeline connections from the causeway abutment to the vault box, and remediation of the onshore facility. ceqa-c63e6241e8c6fb6afe.name: VCPBA Oak Woodland Conservation 2025--2029 Part II
ceqa-c63e6241e8c6fb6afe.description: The Ventura County Prescribed Burn Association (VCPBA) plans to conduct thinning, brushing, chipping, and prescribed burning (pile burning and broadcast burning) across numerous sites in Ventura County. The purpose of this project is to prevent tree mortality of mature oak trees by reducing dead woody fuels and certain vegetation growing under mature oak canopy that can cause cambium-kill and canopy fire if not prescribed burnt. This work will both reduce risk of catastrophic wildfire and fire-harden mature oak trees (primarily Quercus agrifolia, Q. lobata, and Q. john-tuckeri). VCPBA will also be surveying and managing golden spotted oak borer (GSOB). GSOB amplifier trees will be felled and chipped immediately to slow the spread of this non-native invasive beetle. Oak trees that that are minimally infested will be treated with insecticide and/or their bark will be burnt to reduce the spread and proliferation of these high risk beetles. At other project sites, dead vegetation and dead wood will be pile burned. Oak plantings may also occur on some project sites to encourage oak reforestation in non-native invasive plant habitats (particularly Centaurea solstitialis). Ventura County Fire Department (VCFD) will inspect burn units, prior to broadcast and pile burning. VCPBA will acquire burn permits from both VCFD and from Ventura Air Pollution Control District (VCAPCD), prior to any prescribed burns. Beneficiaries of this project include residents across Ventura County, particularly in certain areas of Lockwood Valley, Ojai, and Simi Valley.
