ceqa-35b18e746c13180031.name: Southern California Edison Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Installation
ceqa-35b18e746c13180031.projectTitle: Southern California Edison Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Installation
ceqa-35b18e746c13180031.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-35b18e746c13180031.description: Pursuant to California Public Utilities Commission Decision 19-11-017, as mandated by AB 1083 (Charge Ready Parks), and agreed upon by a master agreement between the California Department of Parks and Recreation and Southern California Edison (SCE), this project proposes site and electrical infrastructure improvements for the installation of electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) by SCE and/or its subcontractors in an existing day use parking lot (Lot A). The purpose of this project is to support the usage of electric vehicles by providing charging locations in State Parks and will contribute to the State’s goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Thirteen existing standard parking stalls will be replaced with eleven stalls equipped with eight Level 2 and three Direct Current Fast Charging (DCFC) charging ports, including one van ADA parking stall and one standard ADA parking stall, resulting in a net gain of two ADA stalls and a loss of four existing standard parking stalls that is not expected to impact visitor services. Construction activities include minor excavation, trenching, and backfilling to install new equipment. During construction, a traffic and pedestrian safety control plan will ensure there are no impacts to visitor services. A right of entry permit will be issued to SCE and/or its subcontractors to complete the work. All applicable regulatory permits are required prior to the start of construction, and all work shall adhere to Departmental policies and standard best management practices to minimize impacts to sensitive resources. Measures to be implemented to avoid and minimize impact may be obtained by submitting a request to the project contact listed below.
ceqa-35b18e746c13180031.crossStreets: E. Harbor Blvd. and San Pedro St.

ceqa-75ca55c6eca66c0948.name: Lake Piru Early Warning System Installation
ceqa-75ca55c6eca66c0948.projectTitle: Lake Piru Early Warning System Installation
ceqa-75ca55c6eca66c0948.description: United Water Conservation District (United) proposes to install a new siren to address a coverage gap in the existing emergency alarm systems at Lake Piru (Project). This new safety device will be located on the western shore of Lake Piru, near United’s existing Water Treatment Facility (34.473026, -118.757202), and will alert boaters on the lake and campers and visitors at the Lake Piru Recreation Area of an imminent emergency. The device will be equipped with a rotating speaker with four active speaker cells, capable of reproducing six standard warning tones and an audible range of 6,100 feet (1.2 miles) at 70 decibels (dB) and 12,200 feet (2.3 miles) at 60 dB. An excavator will be used to dig an 8-foot-deep hole to install a 60-foot pole. The hole will be backfilled with the native excavated soil and the Project will be completed in one day.

ceqa-aaaa84c4870072e3c3.name: Knolls Zone Water Facilities Project
ceqa-aaaa84c4870072e3c3.description: The project consists of construction and operation of a new aboveground water storage tank (the Crown Hill Tank) and associated piping and electrical infrastructure. The purpose of the project is to improve water storage capacity and to provide proper water pressure to some higher elevation lots on the Knolls Pressure Zone. The Crown Hill Tank would be a welded steel aboveground tank approximately 74 feet in diameter and 35 feet in height, with a storage capacity of one million gallons. In addition to the tank, the project would also include installation of a 10-inch pipeline and appurtenances to connect the Crown Hill Tank to the existing Alta Vista Tanks No. 1 and 2, construction of an access roadway and retaining walls, and landscaping in the areas surrounding the project components.
ceqa-aaaa84c4870072e3c3.crossStreets: Crown Hill Drive between Lyon Place and its southern terminus

ceqa-b8fa7d915f5a939348.name: Oxnard Fire Station No. 2 Project
ceqa-b8fa7d915f5a939348.description: The Project involves the demolition of the existing 4,145-square-foot fire station and adjoining community garden, and the construction of a 12,585-square-foot (gross) new fire station. The fire station would include a separate 312-square-foot trash enclosure, a 180 square-foot earthquake storage enclosure, a 68-square-foot sand storage, and a 54-square-foot hose drying tower. This new fire station would support the daily operation of the OFD in its existing Station 2 location to continue to serve the nearby neighborhoods, upgrading the facility to a larger, more modern space to better suit the OFD's needs. The fire station would include a single-story apparatus bay designed to accommodate two fire engines and one ladder truck. Adjacent to the large apparatus area are support spaces like turnouts where the firefighters would store firefighting equipment, a decontamination (decon) room where they would clean their gear and themselves, a shop space for equipment cleaning and repair of equipment and tools, an EMS storage room for required medical supplies, a restroom, and miscellaneous utility rooms that would support the fire station. The building would also provide living quarters to accommodate up to 10 fire personnel per shift, which would include separate bunk rooms, restrooms, a kitchen, laundry facilities, dining room, day room (living room), an outdoor staff patio, and a fitness room. In addition, an open office space would be included to provide workspaces for fire personnel. The majority of the remainder of the Project Site would be paved to provide parking and circulation, and would include a fueling station for the fire apparatus, earthquake storage building, hose drying tower, and emergency generator located north of the fire station building. A trash enclosure would be provided near the northeastern corner of the Project Site. Landscape would be provided around the perimeter of the site, adjacent to Cloyne Street and East Pleasant Valley Road. The fire station would have a maximum height of 29 feet and 8 inches; and would be designed to include a hose drying tower with a maximum height of 31 feet.
ceqa-b8fa7d915f5a939348.crossStreets: East Pleasant Valley Road and Cloyne Street/Cypress Road
